author: Brett Wilkins
title: Israel extends imprisonment of Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safiya for 6 more months
content:
Israeli authorities on November 18 extended the detention without charge of Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, the former director of northern Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, for another six months, prompting outrage from human rights defenders and renewed calls for the release of the pediatrician and scores of other imprisoned Palestinian medical professionals.

According to Abu Safiya’s lawyer, Nasser Odeh, an Israeli court in Beersheba extended the 53-year-old’s indefinite imprisonment through May 2027.

“Why must I spend another six months away from my family?” Dr Abu Safiya reportedly asked the court, claiming he is being punished for doing his job.

According to Al Jazeera, the court justified the continued detention by declaring that Abu Safiya “poses a threat to the state of Israel.”

Israel claims Abu Safiya is a colonel in Hamas’ Military Medical Services and has shown a photo of the doctor wearing a uniform that Al Jazeera said belongs to the Palestinian Directorate of General Military Medical Services, an organization providing healthcare to Gaza security personnel and civilians. The Qatar-based news network said that wearing the agency’s uniform does not establish Hamas membership.

There is also a dispute over the word “colonel”. Critics of Israel’s allegation say this is a professional or honorary designation within the medical services, not proof of a Hamas military command position, much like the United States surgeon-general is not an actual general.

The court’s decision came despite mounting international concern over Abu Safiya’s health and treatment in Israeli custody.

“The information that we are receiving about the health conditions of my father and how he’s being treated is very concerning,” Elias Abu Safiya, the imprisoned doctor’s son, told Al Jazeera on November 12. “My father weighs only 53 kilograms now, and he’s been suffering from very harsh conditions, three floors underground. He is in a solitary room, deprived of food, water, and medicine.”

Elias Abu Safiya continued: “We know he’s been subject to torture and bad treatment. My father still has some shrapnel stuck in his body, and he’s not seen a surgeon. This is inhumane, very harsh conditions that not even animals should be living in inside Israeli prisons. To add to this, he’s not been charged with anything. I don’t know why he’s being tortured this way. He’s a doctor, not a criminal or a murderer. He doesn’t deserve to be treated this way. The court denied the appeal to release him and 14 other doctors.”

Last week, Israel’s Supreme Court rejected a petition seeking the release of Abu Safiya and those 14 doctors, who are also imprisoned without charge or trial.

In July, the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights urged Israel to release the doctor immediately, or charge him and hold a fair trial. OHCHR said there were indications that Abu Safiya had been tortured and subjected to other abuse, including prolonged solitary confinement, repeated severe assaults resulting in serious injuries, and denial of medical care.

Abu Safiya’s 15-year-old son, Ibrahim Abu Safiya, was killed in an Israeli drone strike at the entrance to Kamal Adwan Hospital, where he was sheltering with his family, in October 2024. The following month, Abu Safiya suffered severe shrapnel wounds during yet another Israeli drone strike on the facility.

Israeli troops detained Abu Safiya on December 28, 2024 amid a prolonged siege and assault of the hospital after the director defied a forced displacement order and refused to evacuate the facility as long as patients were still being treated.

Former detainees released from Sde Teiman, the notorious torture prison in southern Israel, said they saw and met Abu Safiya there. According to testimonies collected by the Geneva-based Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor, Abu Safiya was tortured prior to his arrival at Sde Teiman, and also while imprisoned there.

A United Nations commission concluded in 2024 that “Israel has perpetrated a concerted policy to destroy Gaza’s healthcare system as part of a broader assault on Gaza” that has left more than 250,000 Palestinians dead, maimed, or missing. The commission — which separately found that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza — further accused Israeli forces of “committing war crimes and the crime against humanity of extermination with relentless and deliberate attacks on medical personnel and facilities.”

author: Sarah Garnham
title: One Nation is waging war on progress. Why won't progressives fight back?
content:
In 2018, One Nation struggled to get registered as a political party in Victoria, and progressives across the state took pride in it. Labor won the state election that year with a whopping 43 percent primary vote. Twenty years earlier, One Nation leader Pauline Hanson had been prevented from organising in Melbourne by protests, blockades and community events.

Today, the snarling menace and enemy of workers and the left that is One Nation is a major force in Victoria; it enjoys mass support, is vying for lower house seats, and setting the agenda in the state election campaign. The party and its policies have been legitimised by the capitalist press, the Liberal Party and, to a lesser extent, Labor. One Nation’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, has been invited to appear at the leaders’ debate.  

Progressive Victoria should be in uproar. This is the state of Trades Hall, Treaty and Pride. But aside from a few important exceptions—most notably high school students—the response to One Nation’s rise has been decidedly muted. Progressive NGOs and organisations have mostly stayed silent or offered tepid statements focusing on the fears of their constituents rather than forthright denunciation of One Nation and all it represents. The mood is closer to stunned awe than anger, almost as if the capacity to generate the ever-more-elusive commodity of popularity makes a party worthy of respect, however the popularity might be gained. 

Worse still, a layer of trade union organisers, Greens members and other progressives is arguing that the left must sympathise with the concerns of One Nation voters, or at least avoid antagonising them through political argument. In practice, this means sidestepping the signature issues that One Nation is pushing and building a base around. 

GetUp and Victorian Trades Hall Council (VTHC) are 

directing

 campaigners not to “play the racism card” or explicitly attack Pauline Hanson. After its costly and high-profile intervention in the Farrer by-election, GetUp concluded that criticising Hanson, her wealthy backer Gina Rinehart, celebrity defector Barnaby Joyce or the party’s links to Trump is not electorally expedient. Campaigners should instead seek to establish common ground with potential One Nation voters based on economic grievances. 

Senior VTHC researcher Oscar Kaspi-Crutchett 

argues

 to ignore the politics: “Don’t listen to the lyrics, listen to the beat of what they are saying”. The beat, he says, is dissatisfaction with the status quo, so supporters should be helped to “tease out” what that looks like and how it makes them feel. 

Federal Greens leader David Shoebridge 

says

 he has “understood the anger” driving One Nation support. Former Queensland Greens MP Max Chandler-Mathers 

goes further

, arguing that One Nation voters, especially the workers among them, are expressing legitimate protest against the system. He says they are driven by an “almost political nihilism”, and a desire to “blow it up” that makes them open to left-wing arguments and solutions. 

The same basic approach is being taken by more establishment political forces. Teal consultant Sue Barret gives the 

same advice

in four steps: validate the feeling, not the target; ask a genuine question and then be quiet; acknowledge the ground you share; offer a different path, not a different diagnosis.

Labor’s federal treasurer likewise 

warns

 progressives not to “scold” One Nation supporters, and to approach them “from a place of genuine respect and understanding”. The same advice is given by the media, from the establishment right through to liberal outlets. And all of this helps to reinforce One Nation’s 

spin

 about itself: that it is the party of “everyday Australians” who are “sick and tired of being ignored”. 

This appeasement goes further than merely tempering criticisms of One Nation for fear of alienating the party’s voters; it leads to actively opposing efforts to build resistance. 

The Labor-controlled National Union of Students, for example, pulled out of supporting the second student walkout against One Nation, and attacked office bearers for promoting it. Some Greens MPs have endorsed and spoken at the rallies, but others refused to speak on the grounds that it is not strategic and would alienate bigots. When a socialist promoted an anti-One Nation rally in a union activist online forum, the Victorian secretary of the CPSU and long-time leftist Jiselle Hanna replied that it is “more …

title: Medikal Hospital çalışanları: Hakkımız olanı istiyoruz
content:
Elâzığ- Elâzığ’da faaliyet gösteren Özel Medikal Hospital çalışanları, 9 Kasım’da Kod 17 (iş yerinin kapanması) gerekçesiyle işten çıkarılmış ve bu nedenle eylem başlatmıştı. Eylemlerinin 13. gününde Postane Meydanı’nda bir araya gelen işçiler, patronu bir kez daha uyardı.

Çalışanlar adına PTT Meydanı’nda açıklama yapan Tuba Yalçın, şu ifadeleri kullandı: “Bugün burada, yıllarca alın teri dökerek çalıştığımız; Medical Park’tan devrolan Sonomed ve Medikal Hospital olarak bildiğiniz hastaneden çıkarılışımızın 13. gününde sesimizi duyurmak için toplandık. Hastanemizin kapanmasına sebep olan şirket sahipleri, geceleri rahat mısınız? 401 emekçinin ve onların omuzlarında yükselen yüzlerce ailenin ekmeğiyle oynamak bu kadar kolay mı? Unutmayın; bu insanların alın teri, gözyaşı ve kul hakkı her iki dünyada da boynunuzda olacaktır. Devam etmekte olan iş yerlerinizden, bizim gibi emekçilerin sırtından servetinize servet katarken bizler burada, her türlü şarta rağmen yılların emeği olan tazminat haklarımız için direniyoruz. Haklı mücadelemizin maddi tarafı için ‘Mahkemeye gidin’ diyen şirket sahipleri, bu sözleriyle korkmadan adalete meydan okumuştur.”

Yalçın, daha önce verilen sözlere ve ödenmeyen maaş ile özlük haklarına değinerek sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: “Şimdiye kadar söyledikleriniz, samimi olmayan vaatlerinizin bir parçası mıydı yoksa günü kurtaran birer balon muydu? Taleplerimiz nettir: İşten çıkaran şirketin, çalışanların alamadığı tüm özlük haklarını hiçbir kesinti yapmadan ödemesi ve yeni açılacak hastanenin bir an önce faaliyete geçerek işsiz kalan tüm emekçilerin yeniden işe alınmasıdır. 13. gün bitti, 14. gün de gelir ama biz hakkımızı alana kadar susmayacağız, geri adım atmayacağız.”

Elâzığ halkından, kurum ve kuruluşlardan destek talep eden işçiler, hastane sahibinin Medikal patronunun kentte ikinci bir hastanesi ve eczanesi bulunduğunu hatırlatarak boykot çağrısında bulundu.

Eylem sırasında patronun sözlerini balona benzeten çalışanlar, şişirdikleri balonları patlattı. Halaylar çekip sloganlar atan işçiler, oturma eylemi de yaparak meydanda iki saati aşkın süre kaldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Evren: Poor children pushed out of education into cheap labour
content:
The Ministry of National Education's (MEB) proposed 2027 budget, approved by the Turkish Parliament's Planning and Budget Committee on 12 November, continues to spark debate ahead of a vote in the General Assembly in December.


The ministry's initial budget for 2026 was set at 1 trillion 943 billion 965 million Turkish lira. The proposed budget for 2027 has been increased by 26.5 percent in nominal terms to 2 trillion 458 billion 762 million lira. Despite this increase, however, the ministry's share of the central government budget and national income continues to decline. Its share of the central government budget fell from 13.38 percent in 2016 to 10.24 percent in 2026 and 9.02 percent in the 2027 proposal. Its share of gross domestic product (GDP) also declined from 2.91 percent to 2.21 percent over the same period.


Of the proposed 2027 budget, 82.1 percent has been allocated to personnel expenses and payments to the Social Security Institution (SGK). Teachers' salaries remaining below the poverty threshold, alongside attempts to address shortages of permanent cleaning and security staff in schools through temporary employment programmes, have once again brought problems in public education to the forefront.


Problems in meeting basic needs at state schools persist, while private schools now account for 20.1 percent of all schools. This means that one in every five schools in the country is privately run. Meanwhile, the proposed budget of 229 billion 64 million lira for the Presidency of Religious Affairs has increased in real terms and exceeds the individual budgets of the ministries of Interior, Foreign Affairs, Trade, Culture and Tourism, and Energy and Natural Resources.


Including the budgets of the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), the Measuring, Selection and Placement Centre (ÖSYM), and universities, the total proposed education budget for 2027 stands at 3 trillion 755 billion 688 million lira.


'The budget cannot be assessed through economic figures alone'


Sami Evren, co-spokesperson of the Education Policies Commission of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF about the budget proposal approved by the committee. Evren said that assessing the budget solely through economic figures would be insufficient. Evren said that problems concerning education, healthcare and justice in the country were directly linked to the question of democracy, adding that the government had closed its budget proposals to criticism from the opposition. Evren also said that the budget deficit of approximately 3.9 trillion lira, within an overall budget exceeding 27 trillion lira, would once again be covered by the public.


Evren said that the approximately 13 percent allocated to the Ministry of National Education was focused on mandatory personnel expenses rather than investment. Evren argued that the government's calculations, based on its own announced inflation figures, reflected a preference for capital interests rather than the public.


Evren said, "This actually means that, in real terms, the political government has prepared the budget according to the priorities of its own financial circles rather than in favour of public education and the people."


'T

he public character of education has been undermined'


Evren said that the future of approximately 17 million students, representing a quarter of Turkey's population, and 75,000 schools would be shaped by this budget. Evren argued that the existence of approximately 15,000 private schools had undermined the public character of education.


Evren said that state schools were increasingly becoming institutions attended primarily by children from poor families, creating a new class hierarchy in education. Evren also stressed that teachers working in private schools were being exploited as cheap labour. Evren argued that expanding private education meant pushing the public sector out of education. He said, "When public education is marginalised, you cannot see students with disabilities or students from poor families. You cannot address the debates about the content of education."


'Peace is impossible without education in the mother tongue'

author: Marx-lover
title: Review of "Design of a Worker Cooperatives Society," by Geert Reuten
content:
This is a review of a book published in 2023.

Ancien régimes are always tenacious, but it is clear that society in its present form cannot last. Capitalism itself, as Marx predicted, is evidently unsustainable. The question is, what will come after it? Social thinkers have pondered this question for almost two centuries, and we seem to be no closer to an answer now than in the 1840s. It remains just as difficult now as then to imagine a radically different society than our own oligarchically structured one. Notoriously, it is easier to imagine social chaos or human extinction than an organized post-capitalist world.

Nevertheless, in the (overlapping) anarchist, socialist, and communist traditions, there has been no shortage of visions and sketches of a new society. In some cases, a continued role for government is envisioned; in others, society is to consist of a federation of communes and voluntary associations. Typically, the sketch of the future is not at all detailed, both because it is impossible to predict social evolution and because it is up to people themselves to forge new institutions in their struggles against oppression. Marx famously disdained to write “recipes for the cookshops of the future,” and most socialists and anarchists have been similarly reticent.

Not all have, however. Among the small minority of thinkers who have been bold enough to plan the new world in minute detail, Geert Reuten is probably the boldest. His new book Design of a Worker Cooperatives Society: An Alternative Beyond Capitalism and Socialism, and the Transition Towards It consists of an incredible profusion of detail—420 pages of it—about all the major institutions of a possible new society and what the transition process might look like. Whatever flaws the book has, it is an astonishing imaginative feat, a tour de force of imaginary social reconstruction. A former professor of economics who has previously written from a Marxist viewpoint, Reuten seems to have thought of everything, down to the organization of hospitals, pharmacies, museums, and concert halls. The book is hardly pleasure-reading, but it is so dense with ideas that anyone seriously interested in building a non-capitalist society might want to use it as a kind of reference book.

Before proceeding to the impossible task of summarizing the book, however, it may be worthwhile to express some reservations about Reuten’s project. Specifically, one can’t help sharing Marx’s intuition that writing such an astoundingly detailed recipe for the kitchens of the future is profoundly misguided. The book has plenty of intriguing ideas, but there is approximately zero chance that its grand Design (as Reuten calls it) will ever be enacted. This just isn’t how history works, from the ideal to the material. Rather, new institutions emerge laboriously out of popular economic and political struggles, as new challenges arise and people come up with new ways to meet them. Reuten justifies his book in the following terms (p. 3):

"General accounts or main lines of the organisation of a future society are in my view insufficiently convincing for most people to really see it as an alternative to capitalism... Hence, for the judgement on the possible functioning of a “worker cooperatives society” and the adequacy thereof, one needs a design of its full economic and state organisation that is blueprint-like in its detail. Detailed such that the feasibility and consistency of the design can be fully scrutinised."

But even if the Design is consistent and highly detailed, people can still object that it’s completely unfeasible because of the realities of social conflict and the messiness of society. The latter isn’t pliable enough to be molded into fitting an ideal blueprint. This was one problem with, say, Charles Fourier’s utopianism, and it’s a problem with all utopian blueprints. They’re all more-or-less unfeasible, precisely because they’re blueprints (and thus idealistic, conceived out of thin air far in advance of the era when supposedly they might be realized).

One might object, moreover, that in an age of ecological collapse, it is an oversight for a book outlining a future society not to acknowledge humanity’s grim prospects. Escalating global warming and the ongoing destruction of ecosystems might seem to vitiate any attempt to establish a socialist utopia. (And yes, despite the book’s subtitle, the society Reuten envisions is a type of socialism, in which workers …

author: Bianca Blell
title: Trump Administration Proposes Cuts to Pregnancy-Related Work Protections
content:
The Trump administration is preparing to narrow federal workplace protections for pregnant workers, potentially limiting access to accommodations for a range of reproductive health conditions.

On November 2nd , the New York Times reported that the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) is considering revisions to regulations implementing the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA), spearheaded by President Donald Trump. The PWFA was passed by Congress in 2022, initially implemented during the Biden administration.

The original law was meant to fill a gap in disability and discrimination protections that employees are guaranteed in the workplace. Under current regulations, employees are generally required to make reasonable adjustments for qualified employees experiencing pregnancy-related limitations. Examples of such accommodations include additional bathroom breaks, schedule changes, lighter duties, temporary reassignment, and time off for prenatal appointments, including more.

The proposed revisions aim to narrow workplace protections under the PWFA, potentially shrinking the types of accommodations employers are required to provide. One of the changes being considered is a modification to how the EEOC interprets the phrase “pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.” This agency, under the President’s advisory, could present reversals that affect accommodations related to abortion and fertility treatments.

The potential rollback extends beyond abortion access. Under the current regulations, employers may be required to provide accommodations for employees seeking abortion, including time off for the procedure and related travel. While voluntary abortions have already been removed from this scope by a 2025 federal court ruling, medically necessary procedures currently remain covered.

The potential rollback extends beyond abortion access. Employees undergoing fertility treatments may need time off for medical appointments, medication schedules, or procedures. Workers experiencing miscarriages or postpartum depression may also require temporary adjustments to their schedules or responsibilities. Without clear federal protections, employees could face greater difficulty securing accommodations for these conditions, particularly in workplaces where employers are unwilling to provide flexibility.

Research also demonstrates the importance of workplace accommodations for maternal health. A 2025 study found that the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act was associated with a 3.2% increase in births in states newly covered by the law. The original 2022 law has contributed to a nearly 10% decrease in miscarriages.

The current administration strives for a pro-natalist agenda, encouraging American women to marry and increase births per family. In May 2026, the White House announced new initiatives aimed at expanding fertility benefits and supporting mothers. Yet the administration’s consideration of narrower workplace protections could make it more difficult for workers to access the reproductive health care and employment accommodations that help them build and support families.

The Pregnant Workers Fairness Act was an important bipartisan achievement that recognized workers should not have to choose between maintaining their employment and protecting their health. Although the law itself remains in effect, weakening its implementing regulations could leave workers with fewer protections during some of the most vulnerable periods of their lives. The federal government should strengthen protections, not undermine the progress that workers and advocates fought to achieve.

author: Z Waite
title: AI Is Monitoring and Scoring Fast-Food Workers’ Every Move
content:
One app measures how quickly workers walk to and from their cars. Another judges how warmly workers greet customers.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Corrin Kearney had been delivering pizzas for a Domino’s in North Texas for a few months when their store asked them to install a new app on their phone and keep it open during their shift. Soon, Kearney learned the app was tracking and scoring every delivery route they drove, with the results displayed on a leaderboard back at the store for the whole crew to see.

The app uses technology from Drivosity, a company that sells what it calls “cutting edge GPS and AI” driver-monitoring to fast-food chains, including Domino’s and Papa John’s. Each trip is scored from 0 to 100 based on factors including acceleration, braking, cornering and speed. According to Kearney, drivers at their store are expected to keep their scores above 85. Anyone below that score is written up by managers and eventually locked out of the Domino’s system. “Drivosity can effectively fire people,” Kearney said. As a driver captain, Kearney has to write up other drivers, even though they have found the app doesn’t recognize the nuance of many real-world situations. Drivers can be penalized for sudden braking to avoid a collision or rapid acceleration to merge on a highway, forcing them to choose between risking an accident or getting points docked, according to Kearney. “It’s infuriating,” Kearney said. “The AI can tell you you haven’t driven well enough and you get fired.”

Drivosity also sells coaching and analytics features, including HustleTime®, which measures how fast employees walk from the store to their car, how long they take handing the pizza to a customer and how long they take walking back. In Drivosity’s promotional videos, franchise owners and managers at Domino’s and Papa John’s praise HustleTime®’s ability to track workers in real time down to the second. Stores can “gamify” this, according to the company website, by having workers compete for better scores.

Domino’s and Drivosity did not respond to requests for comment.

Fast-food companies are increasingly using AI-powered technology to turn worker behavior — how fast you drive, how warmly you greet a customer, how long you spend in the bathroom — into data that can score, rank, discipline and manage employees. To understand how these AI-driven tools are impacting fast-food workers, Capital & Main interviewed over a dozen workers, researchers and labor advocates, who described error-prone technologies being deployed at a rapid pace, without the consent or awareness of staff, even as their pay and promotions are increasingly shaped by AI-enabled monitoring.

“They basically use their population of workers as guinea pigs,” Alexandra Mateescu, a researcher at the nonprofit Data & Society, said of the way that fast-food companies are deploying these new tools.

In February, Burger King announced that an OpenAI-powered assistant named Patty was being rolled out at about 500 U.S. restaurants, with plans to reach all U.S. stores by the end of 2026. A few weeks later, the tool arrived at the Burger King in Niagara Falls, New York, where Dante Vasquez took drive-thru orders.

“It started with a little AI voice in our headset,” said Vasquez.

Then the monitoring features started. Each drive-thru conversation was scored on friendliness and upselling, with the numbers displayed on a screen in front of Vasquez as he worked. Anyone could click on a transaction to hear a recording and review the AI-generated transcripts. Green boxes marked what he’d done well — a “Good morning!” or “You rule!” Red boxes marked what Patty counted against him: points off for saying “please hold,” or “um,” or not speaking clearly.

Managers watched the scores closely, constantly reminding the crew to stay above the 70% friendliness target, Vasquez said. Workers who scored low were cut from the schedule, he added.

Vasquez learned to speak the way that Patty wanted. He got so good at it, that customers started asking if he was a bot. His co-workers nicknamed him “Gemini.” “The system wants me to talk like a robot, so I’m talking like a robot,” Vasquez said. “It just gets so mentally degrading.”

Burger King has said publicly that the system was not designed to evaluate individual employees. But Capital & Main reviewed screenshots from a Burger King training module, and images of the …

title: ¡A la Huelga!: A Full Report on Spain’s General Strike from Vallekas, Madrid, and Barcelona
content:
In response to the violent eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, a disabled 87-year-old woman, people around Spain poured into the streets and set up

encampments

 in the plazas in a movement against evictions and gentrification. On November 11, a general strike took place throughout the country—the first in

fourteen years

. Here, we present accounts of the events from the vantage points of

Madrid

 and

Barcelona

.


This is a valuable document for all who seek to build the power to defend our communities.


The View from Madrid


We sit in a loosely arranged circle in a local social center run by a trade union. It’s just past midnight. When the clock strikes 12, marking the beginning of Wednesday, November 11, we erupt into cheers. Spain’s first general strike in 14 years is underway.


4.5 million people mobilized


1340 committees across the Spanish state


108 cities mobilized


4 million+ leaflets distributed


600,000+ posters put up


“General Strike for Housing” website


The building opened at 8 pm on Tuesday; it will stay open until 8 pm on Wednesday, with a room designated for strikers to take naps. People mill about, preparing food for our late dinner, drying wet clothing with a hairdryer that someone thought to bring from home. Some catch up with old friends, as the social center has become a gathering place for all in the area who need it. Others sign up to take shifts making coffee, preparing food, and protecting the space over the hours ahead.


We are

Vallekanos

, some by birth, others more recent transplants. Vallecas, known as Vallekas to many, is an urban area of Madrid so large that it was divided into two districts (Puente de Vallecas and Villa de Vallecas). The area is an epicenter of anti-fascist working-class resistance in Spain’s capital. After

Maricarmen was evicted

 in September and the general strike was announced in October, local organizations and social movements in the districts came together to help organize for the strike. Similar convergences have taken place in thousands of localities around Spain.


“It’s syndicalist terrorism.”


—Isabel Díaz Ayuso, right-wing President of the “Madrid Community”


The enthusiasm that fills this social center on the eve of the general strike flows from the same energy that erupted in millions of Spaniards on the day that Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman, was evicted from her home of 70 years in Madrid. Something clicked in the collective consciousness of the country at that moment. The percentage of Spain’s population that lives as tenants has risen steadily over the last few decades, reaching 25%, and recently, rents have skyrocketed.


All of us have heard the horror stories. A coworker who lives in a village a hundred kilometers away because they couldn’t afford housing near the office. Families with children who are forced to live in a single sub-letted room. Residents of protected housing who were evicted after their homes were sold to ruthless investment funds.


A memorial to Maricarmen a few steps away from her home.


Thanks to years of hard work by grassroots housing movements across the country, a voice has emerged to connect these struggles. The

Sindicato de Inquilinas

 (“Tenant’s Union”) has become a household name, appearing day after day in the news and on social media. The Union has shown the country that it is neither normal nor right that decent, stable housing has become increasingly impossible to find in this country, and the opportunity to become a homeowner even more so. The Union has exposed these struggles as the product of a deliberate political and financial strategy perpetrated by the wealthy. The Union has developed a powerful architecture of local assemblies, which made it possible to channel this collective outrage into a call for a general strike.


What follows is a local report and analysis from the districts of Vallekas and the city of Madrid as a whole, tracing the efforts leading up to the strike and the events of the day itself.


It Was About Time for a Strike!


As

we reported last month

, the current housing crisis in Spain had been approaching a breaking point in the months leading up to Maricarmen’s eviction. In Madrid, rental prices have risen 50% over the past five years, and many in the city find themselves forced to spend upwards of 70% of their monthly salaries on rent. In 2025, there were nearly 25,000 evictions nationwide, 74.6% of which were due to non-payment of rent …

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Labour’s Plan to Get Young People Working Is Mostly a Plan to Get Big Business Paid
content:
As they say: fish gonna swim, birds gonna fly, and a Labour government gonna try to implement some kind of workfare scheme which benefits corporations. This week’s headlines were dominated by Alan Milburn, one of Tony Blair’s ministerial stalwarts, and his report into the state of Britain’s NEETs (those not in employment, education, or training).

Milburn recommended

 that the government abolish the health component of universal credit for under-25s, and replace PIP payments for under-25s with a new “additional cost allowance”. Cynics amongst you may quibble with the idea that it’s the benefits system stopping young people from entering work, as opposed to, say,

 the recent bonfire of entry-level jobs

.


In any case, Milburn has been rewarded for his contributions with an appointment to

chair of the new Youth Opportunities Unit

, reporting directly to the prime minister. Well, it’s nice to know that somebody’s out there finding work. 


The Cortado


          Get your shot of political analysis from

Ash Sarkar

 and

Steven Methven

, every Monday and Friday morning.


First name:


Email:


I agree to the

Privacy Policy


      Sign up error:

. Try again later.


      Thanks for signing up.


It’s undeniable that young people are getting screwed over. The youth share of the labour market has gone down, even as employment overall has gone up. While the headline percentage of NEETs hasn’t changed drastically in the last 20 years, the composition of NEETs has. In 2005,

four in ten

 young NEETs had never had a job. Now, it’s six in ten. A young person first claiming health and disability benefits in 2019 is a third more likely, in five years time, to still be out of employment, education or training, than those who first claimed in 2010. NEETdom is stickier than it used to be, as is joblessness as a result of ill health.


To be fair to Milburn, he isn’t saying it’s all young people’s fault. His

interim report

, released earlier this year, acknowledged that recruitment has become “more remote, more automated and less human”. Print this out, and show it to your Dad who says you just need to get out there and hand out CVs: “The young person who once might have walked into a shop, spoken to a manager and been given a chance in the past is now screened by a portal, a test, a recorded interview or an algorithm before anyone has looked them in the eye.” 


And yet, taking the government’s sunny line on the advantages of AI, Milburn’s report insists that it’s “wrong to blame AI for the recent rise in youth detachment”. Cool, fine, let’s just ignore what

research

 and

business leaders

 have to say about the specific role of AI in cutting entry level jobs. But in case you were worried that Milburn wasn’t taking the threat of AI to young people’s jobs seriously enough, he does propose setting up “a small AI Youth Observatory” whose remit is tracking “changes in youth recruitment, entry-level tasks and occupations by sector and place”. That sounds nice and urgent.


Beyond cutting benefits and establishing yet another quango, Milburn’s work has prompted the government to set up

a youth job creation scheme

. It promises guaranteed jobs for young people on universal credit, and vows to support over 90,000 young people furthest from work into a role. The state will fully fund up to 25 hours of paid work a week for six months, at the relevant minimum wage, and 400 employers, including Lidl, Leonardo Hotels and Boots have already signed on.


So, instead of using government money to fund socially useful jobs – insulating homes or planting trees, for instance – taxpayers are paying Boots to help young NEETs flog tingle-sensation lube. 


Milburn’s report urges the government to go further, recommending that employer national insurance contributions for workers aged 21 to 24 (starting in the retail and hospitality sectors) are lowered over five years. As

Private Eye has pointed out

, the majority-owner of the Burger King UK ‘master franchise’ is an investment management firm that Milburn just happens to advise and be a shareholder in.


Funny how the biggest beneficiaries of government spending turn out to be corporations.

title: God and Groypers: The Christo-Fascist Conference in Texas
content:
Irving, TX – White supremacist Nicholas J. Fuentes walked on stage of the Irving Convention Center just outside of Dallas to roaring applause and chants. One young attendee shot up from his seat and exuberantly began clapping his hands above his head.


Behind Fuentes was a WWE-like promo video where the streamer shouts that he will “die for America” while a cross flashes in the center of the screen and a battleship fires munitions at an unknown target.


At the podium, a smirk crept across his face as the audience broke out into “USA” chants.


“Yes,” he said, nodding his head and basking in the zealotry before him.


Nick Fuentes on stage at the Christ is King conference. Source: NXR Live stream.


This was the third and final day of the “Christ is King: America after Trump” conference in Irving, a diverse suburb of Dallas, Texas. Until moments before he was welcomed on the stage, Fuentes was an unannounced mystery speaker intended to cap off the Christo-fascist jubilee.


Roughly 1,000 people showed up from around the country to attend the convention, put on by Pastor Joel Webbon’s New Christian Right, or NXR, an explicitly Christian nationalist organization that aligns more with Fuentes’ groypers than the MAGA coalition that holds power in the Republican Party. For Fuentes and Webbon, the resounding defeat of Republicans in the midterm election presents an opportunity to begin a takeover of the Grand Old Party.


The forward-looking political event, headlined by 12 far-right personalities, would ultimately circle around the personalities of Webbon and Fuentes as they discussed Hitler and the next two years while papering over theological differences.


In the main auditorium, attendance for speaking events was at its highest on the final day in anticipation of the mystery speaker.


The strategy laid out by Fuentes at the lectern is to assume that they will have 100,000 politically activated groypers by the time of the 2028 Iowa Caucus to influence who is chosen as the presidential candidate in the Republican primary process.


The plan also assumes that 100,000 groypers, not known for their social affability, will be able to persuade the average Republican primary voter to support whatever extremist candidate they inevitably land on as their standard bearer.


“One-hundred thousand groypers won’t flip the country, but they can make 100 million phone calls, knock on 100 million doors,” Fuentes said. “We can get out there in the Iowa caucus.”


Speakers at the event, apart from Webbon and Fuentes, included far-right conspiracy theorist Alex Jones – who was billed as the events major keynote speaker and opened the profanity-free event with a profanity-peppered speech – Tucker Carlson’s brother Buckley Carlson, and former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback.


Fishback, who has long aligned himself with Fuentes and groypers, used the opportunity to announce his candidacy for the 2028 presidential election to major fanfare, despite the fact he would not meet the constitutional age requirements for the position by the time of his theoretical inauguration.


Another notable speaker was far-right British Friar Calvin Robinson, a mixed-race cleric who earlier this year

threw out a Roman salute following his remarks at a pro-Life event

, an act that would result in the Anglican church stripping him of his right to serve as a priest in the church. Only days after the conference, Robinson

would call for the expulsion of Jewish people from America

.


Calvin Robinson speaking at the Christ is King conference. Source: NXR Live stream

.


NXR is a new project for Webbon, taking over the 12-year-old Right Response Ministries YouTube channel in December 2025. The first video launched under the brand was the first episode in a ten-part series, a conversation between Fuentes and Webbon, in which the two discuss their vision for a Christian government.


As the two are inclined to do, the conversation naturally veered toward Adolf Hitler

in a clip from the first episode

.


“Why can’t we have nice things? Because Hitler,” Webbon said, implying that our society is failing because of its aversion to Hitler and fascism.


In another clip

, Webbons said its fair to say that “all Black people” are impulsive and lazy, and that “all Jews” are subversive, allowing for “some exceptions.”

title: Veranstaltungsreihe Gegen Krieg
content:
Überall heisst es Aufrüstung sei alternativlos!


Wir, die arbeiten müssen, um zu überleben sollen alle den Gürtel enger schnallen, während die Tech- und Rüstungsindustrie Rekordgewinne feiert. Fürs Militär werden Milliarden locker gemacht, finanziert durch sozialen Kahlschlag und höhere Steuern auf unseren täglichen Einkauf.


Die Überwachung nimmt zu, patriarchale Verhältnisse verhärten sich und die bürgerliche Politik und Medien reden pausenlos von «Sicherheit» und der Bedrohung von Aussen.


In dieser Veranstaltungsreihe betrachten wir gemeinsam verschiedene Brennpunkte und Perspektiven der aktuellen Kriegstendenzen. Wir schauen uns an, wieso die Zeichen aktuell auf Krieg stehen und woher die Bedrohung tatsächlich kommt. So wollen wir Erkenntnisse sammeln, um uns gegen die Kriegstreiberei und die weltweite Aufrüstung zu organisieren und Widerstand zu leisten. Schliesslich wollen wir auch gemeinsam diskutieren, was nötig ist für echten, dauerhaften Frieden und für eine Welt ohne Kriege.

author: Antifa Marburg
title: Marburg bleibt rot! Kampagne zur 500 Jahr-Feier der Philipps-Universität
content:
Ein Ausschnitt aus 500 Jahren Widersprüchen


Nach der militärischen Niederlage der Nazis am 8. Mai 1945 tummelten sich auch in Marburg weiterhin SympathisantInnen und AnhängerInnen des nationalsozialistischen Regimes. Ihre Strukturen funktionierten weiterhin, so konnte sich beispielsweise im Jahr 1946 Klaus Barbie, ehemaliger Gestapo-Chef von Lyon, in Marburg verstecken. Er wurde wegen mehrerer Kriegsverbrechen gesucht und konnte sich hier dem Zugriff der Alliierten entziehen. Gleichzeitig wurde der bekennende Marxist und Widerstandskämpfer Wolfgang Abendroth Anfang der 1950er Jahre Professor für Politikwissenschaften an der Philipps-Universität. Er setzte sich für die Demokratisierung der Hochschule ein und stellte sich klar gegen die an der Universität noch agierenden Nazi-TäterInnen, die auf ihren Posten verblieben waren.


Spätestens seit der Studierendenbewegung 1968 jedoch wurden Nazis der Erlebnis-Generation sowie in den folgenden Jahrzehnten auch ihren ideologischen Nachkömmlingen, in Marburg vermehrt gesellschaftlicher Raum genommen – der Ruf des „Roten Marburg“ etablierte sich.


Rotes Marburg?


Marburgs linke Hegemonie ist Ergebnis von sozialen und politischen Kämpfen, wurde in den letzten Jahrzehnten aber regelmäßig angegriffen. Schon 1968 verfassten 35 Professoren ein »Marburger Manifest« gegen die »Demokratisierung der Universität«, dieser schlossen sich 1500 konservative Hochschullehrer aus der ganzen BRD an. Reaktionäre und FaschistInnen waren in Marburg schon immer verankert, auch das Aussterben der Nazis hat daran nichts geändert. Während sie in der Universität an Raum verloren hatten, tragen Marburgs militaristische Vergangenheit und die bis heute etablierte, aber diverse, Studentenverbindungsszene zentrale ideologische Bestandteile über die Zeit weiter.


Exportschlager Faschismus


Bis heute sind an der Marburger Universität ausgebildete FaschistInnen ein Exportschlager. Gerne zieht es diese auch gen Osten. Von den Morden von Mechterstädt (1920), wo Marburger Studenten, die sich noch kurz zuvor am extrem-rechten Kapp-Putsch beteiligten, und dort 15 Arbeiter erschossen, bis zu Marburger Naziburschen im AfD-Kader Thüringens (https://www.lebensbund.org/torben-braga-mdl-thueringen-fuer-die-afd-27-08-1991-beitritt-2013/).


Aber auch an der Philipps-Universität werden Dozierende von FaschistInnen mit dem Tode bedroht (https://autonome-antifa.org/breve9892).


Am Fachbereich Geschichte und Kulturwissenschaften werden Naziburschen in den Studienausschuss gewählt und repräsentieren die Marburger Archäologie nach außen (https://stadtlandvolk.net/?p=1151).


Bildung als Ware


Das Ziel demokratischer und kritischer Bildung richtet sich darauf, dass Faschismus in Deutschland nie wieder geschehen solle. Mit dem neoliberalen Umbau der Universität (z. B. Einführung des Bachelor/Master-Systems) ist dieses Ziel allerdings in den Hintergrund gerückt – Bildung ist vermehrt zur Ware geworden. Wie in allen Bereichen fördern Privatisierung und Sparmaßnahmen auch an der Universität Umstände, die eher Individualismus, Leistungsgesellschaft und das Treten nach unten begünstigen als gemeinsam solidarische Antworten auf soziale Krisen zu finden. Diese Umstände bedingen, dass rechte Akteure es leichter haben, ihre Politik umzusetzen.


Wegfall unserer Räume


Nachdem bereits in den 2000er Jahren das zweite, neben dem Bettenhaus, selbstverwaltete Studierendenwohnheim, Collegium Gentium, privatisiert wurde (https://jungle.world/artikel/2005/07/we-dont-need-no-reeducation), soll die PhilFak, Symbol für antifaschistische Bildung, platt gemacht werden. Die zeitweise Abwahl des Antifareferats im Asta 2025 durch Konservative und Liberale, zeigte, dass auch unter Studierenden kritische Bildung nicht mehr den Stellenwert hat, den sie einmal hatte. Aber auch außeruniversitäre Orte wie das HavannaAcht oder das Ohm, welche Treffpunkte der linken und alternativen Studierenden waren, sind über die Jahre weggefallen.


Wir feiern keine 500 Jahre mit euch – what we need is Antifa!


Wir feiern diese Verbindung von langjährigen etablierten rechten Strukturen und der Neoliberalisierung der Universität nicht mit euch. Deswegen rufen wir über den Zeitraum des gesamten Jubiläums dazu auf, euch an unserer Kampagne zu beteiligen.


Im Kampf dagegen können wir uns nur auf uns selbst verlassen. Informiert euch, wer und was hier gefeiert werden soll! Zeigt Solidarität mit den noch vorhandenen antifaschistischen Strukturen und Personen! Lasst uns …

author: CNT Valladolid
title: Vivienda y antifascismo en tiempos de Desokupa
content:
El miércoles 21 de octubre, como parte de las jornadas de inauguración del nuestro nuevo local en Valladolid, se celebró un debate sobre el tema de la vivienda desde tres perspectivas complementarias: la del

Sindicato de Vivienda de Valladolid

, la del Sindicato de Inquilinas (por parte de

Javier Gil

, autor del libro

Generación Inquilina

, que se vendió durante el acto) y la de

Sistema 161

, grupo de investigación de entramados reaccionarios.


Gracias a los ponentes se perfiló una detallada imagen del problema de la vivienda mostrando que éste es consustancial a un capitalismo que año tras año ha ido deviniendo en un capitalismo rentista en lugar de productivo, especialmente en el Estado español. Lo que la clase trabajadora arañamos a los empresaurios como sueldo, se lo devolvemos teniendo que pagar precios de vivienda inflados por la especulación.


La inversión en vivienda está siendo la tabla de salvación de un capitalismo en crisis, sin tener en cuenta costes humanos de los aumentos de rentabilidad, y eso ha convertido a la vivienda en una palanca estratégica para el cambio social.


Apoyando y sosteniendo este sistema encontramos desde empresas de desokupación encargadas de llevar a cabo brutalmente los desalojos de la nueva clase rentista, hasta todos los gobiernos del Estado españoi, que no han contribuido a dar salida a esta situación e incluso la han empeorado con medidas legislativas que favorecen los desahucios.


La impunidad de las empresas de Desokupa -cuyo sórdido árbol genealógico pudo consultarse en una exposición simultánea a la mesa redonda- es un nuevo ejemplo de que “los ricos siempre han llevado mal que los pobres tengan derechos”; estas empresas son un nuevo nicho de negocio que facilita a la clase rentista saltarse la ley, y que opera gracias a la tolerancia policial y a las campañas favorecedoras de determinados medios.


Quedó claro que el silenciamiento no sólo del historial delictivo de los componentes de estas empresas, sino de sus vínculos tangibles con el negocio inmobiliario -adquiriendo los pisos que desahucian- es algo que los medios de comunicación masiva ocultan por, en el mejor de los casos, negligencia.


Pero el rechazo generalizado a los desahucios que se va extendiendo en la población está restando espacio a esta propaganda, y convocatorias como la de huelga general por la vivienda están desmantelando un espacio público en el que los debates fomentados por la ultraderecha ocupaban el lugar de la discusión de problemas reales.


Es significativo que una semana de acampadas por la vivienda hayan provocado un adelanto de elecciones que no han producido dos años de manifestaciones ultras frente a las sedes del PSOE pidiendo lo mismo, pero también está claro que hay que ir más allá de las elecciones.


Dada la ausencia de una representatividad de la clase obrera en los sistemas parlamentarios habituales en la que ésta vea sus intereses de clase expresados y llevados a cabo, se impone la necesidad de reconstruir una acción política al margen de estos cauces habituales.


Necesidad que se percibe también en todas las movilizaciones por la vivienda, que han abandonado la posición anti-organización que tuvo peso en algunas acampadas del 15M. Las acampadas y movilizaciones por la vivienda no están siendo una repetición del 15M, sino un paso hacia una articulación de una nueva forma de política desde la base.


Una nueva forma de acción política que pasa por hacer nuevas formas de sindicalismo – más combativo y autogestionado- y por fortalecer un nuevo sentido común compartido, y que sean un dique contra las soluciones autoritarias a la pérdida de rentabilidad de los negocios capitalistas.


La entrada

Vivienda y antifascismo en tiempos de Desokupa

 apareció primero en

CNT Valladolid

.


La entrada

Vivienda y antifascismo en tiempos de Desokupa

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Unknown
title: I nipotini del fascismo usano l’antisemitismo per mettere il bavaglio sulla Palestina
content:
Gli eredi politici di chi promulgò le leggi razziali del 1938 approvano una legge che confonde antisemitismo e critica a Israele. Un’operazione di potere che protegge il governo responsabile del genocidio a Gaza e punta a reprimere la solidarietà con il popolo palestinese.


da

OsservatorioRepressione


C’è qualcosa di politicamente osceno nel vedere gli eredi del fascismo italiano ergersi a difensori della lotta contro l’antisemitismo. Sono gli eredi di una tradizione politica che nel 1938 trasformò il razzismo antiebraico in legge dello Stato, espulse gli ebrei dalle scuole, dalle università, dagli impieghi pubblici e contribuì, con la Repubblica sociale italiana, alla loro persecuzione e deportazione nei campi di sterminio. Oggi quella stessa tradizione politica, attraverso i suoi discendenti, pretende di stabilire quali critiche allo Stato di Israele siano ammissibili e quali debbano essere considerate manifestazioni di antisemitismo. Non è una contraddizione accidentale. È un’operazione politica che utilizza la memoria della persecuzione antiebraica per legittimare nuove forme di repressione del dissenso.


Con 147 voti favorevoli, 93 contrari e 5 astenuti,

 la Camera ha approvato definitivamente il disegno di legge sull’antisemitismo, già passato al Senato. Il provvedimento recepisce la controversa definizione 

dell’International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)

, che attraverso i suoi esempi applicativi rischia di 

sovrapporre l’odio antiebraico alla critica politica dello Stato di Israele e del sionismo. 

Non introduce un divieto penale generale di criticare Israele, ma costruisce un dispositivo istituzionale che può essere utilizzato per colpire la libertà di espressione, la ricerca universitaria e le mobilitazioni politiche. Il problema non è dunque soltanto ciò che la legge vieta espressamente, ma ciò che rende possibile attraverso interpretazioni estensive, provvedimenti disciplinari, pressioni amministrative e forme di censura preventiva.


La maggioranza ha respinto tutti gli emendamenti delle opposizioni, compreso quello che chiedeva di impedire l’intitolazione di strade, monumenti ed edifici pubblici a persone che avessero sostenuto o propagandato l’antisemitismo e l’odio razziale. Un passaggio che rivela molto della natura politica dell’operazione. Chi pretende di combattere l’antisemitismo attraverso una legge che rischia di criminalizzare l’antisionismo non ha voluto accogliere neppure una disposizione diretta a contrastare la celebrazione pubblica dei propagandisti dell’odio razziale. E mentre si votava una legge presentata come necessaria per difendere la memoria della persecuzione antiebraica, nell’aula di Montecitorio alcuni deputati della destra riabilitavano Giovanni Gentile e insultavano i partigiani comunisti che lo uccisero. Rossano Sasso li ha definiti «vigliacchi», mentre Alessandro Amorese di Fratelli d’Italia ha parlato di un «commando di assassini». La risposta di Gianni Cuperlo, «State zitti, fascisti!», ha restituito almeno per un momento il significato storico di quella discussione.


Ma sarebbe un errore fermarsi all’ipocrisia dei postfascisti. Il rapporto tra le destre europee e il governo israeliano ha assunto negli ultimi anni una precisa funzione politica. L’adesione alla definizione IHRA permette a formazioni provenienti da tradizioni nazionaliste, razziste e antisemite di presentarsi come difensori delle comunità ebraiche, senza mettere realmente in discussione la propria concezione etnica della nazione. In cambio, il governo Netanyahu trova alleati disponibili a sostenere le sue politiche e a delegittimare chi denuncia l’occupazione, l’apartheid e il genocidio in Palestina. La conferenza internazionale sull’antisemitismo promossa nel 2025 dal ministro israeliano Amichai Chikli, con la partecipazione di esponenti dell’estrema destra, ha reso evidente questa convergenza. Il punto di incontro non è l’universalismo dei diritti, ma un nazionalismo fondato sull’esclusione, sull’individuazione di nemici interni e sulla criminalizzazione di chi contesta il potere.


La nuova legge italiana si inserisce perfettamente in questo disegno. Dopo due anni di mobilitazioni contro il genocidio a Gaza, il governo Meloni ha dovuto fare i conti con manifestazioni di massa, occupazioni universitarie, scioperi, campagne di boicottaggio e iniziative di solidarietà che hanno denunciato anche le responsabilità politiche e materiali dell’Italia nel sostegno a Israele. La risposta non è …

author: Bulatlat Staff
title: ‘No red carpet’ for Trump’s arrival in the Philippines
content:
Kampuhan Kontra Pax Silica, a UP Diliman-based formation, together with progressive groups, students, faculty members, and rights advocates hold an indignation protest along Katipunan Avenue in Quezon City on November 15, 2026. Photo by Carlo Manalansan/Bulatlat

By Aaron Ernest Cruz and Anne Marxze Umil

“The Filipino people will never welcome a warmonger, racist, fascist, misogynist, sexual offender, and corrupt leader like Trump.”

Despite attempts to derail their protest, progressive groups continued with their action as US President Donald Trump arrived in the country on November 17.

“The Filipino people will never welcome a warmonger, racist, fascist, misogynist, sexual offender, and corrupt leader like Trump,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) said in a statement.

“His war on Iran, support for Israel’s genocide in Gaza, military interventions in Venezuela, Cuba, and the Carribean, tariff wars and brutal trade sanctions, and racist immigration policies have hurt people all over the world, destroyed the global economy, and undermined world peace,” Bayan added.

An estimated 6,000 individuals trooped at Liwasang Bonifacio to express their condemnation of the government’s red carpet welcome for Trump and the Pax Silica deal.

According to Bayan, the police blocked the truck to be used in their program and attempted to get their sound system. But the group managed to bring the sound system to Liwasang Bonifacio. During the early morning, the group reported that there were many police deployed in the area.

“Manila is just like a garrison as police were scattered around the city’s entry point,” Bayan Secretary-General Mong Palatino said in an interview.

Bayan President Renato Reyes Jr. also condemned the police for attempting to tow their vehicle, stressing that police violated the Batas Pambansa Blg. 880 which protects the right to hold protests in designated freedom parks without permits. “We don’t need your [police] here and we won’t allow you to tow our vehicle just like what happened last Sunday [November 15].”

Funa-ay Claver, secretary-general of Indigenous group Katribu described the Marcos Jr. administration as a lapdog of the US government, giving up the country’s land for Pax Silica.

“They say it is for development, but we should always ask: Who will benefit from it? It is clear that Pax Silica serves foreign interests rather than the interests of its own people,” Claver said.

Karapatan said that it is not surprising that Marcos Jr. had an extravagant welcome for Trump. “Trump is a fascist, a warmonger and enabler of brutal, genocidal regimes, making the extravagant welcome prepared for him by his fellow fascist and tyrant Ferdinand Marcos Jr. come as no surprise,” the group said in a statement.

Karapata said that it was under Trump that the Marcos Jr. regime began to transform the Philippines into a manufacturing hub for US armaments.

They said that the country became a cog in the US global supply chain, making parts for weapons now being used in US wars of aggression against countries that have stood up against US hegemony. “Only a fellow fascist and tyrant like Ferdinand Marcos Jr. could be motivated to welcome the likes of Donald Trump to our shores.”

The groups tried to march to the ASEAN Summit venue but were blocked by the police. There are also Special Weapon and Tactics (SWAT) personnel holding rifles at the flyover. Under Batas Pambasa Bldg. 880, law enforcers are prohibited to bring guns in a peaceful protest.

“These guards of Trump are arrogant because they have shields and weapons. But the weapons of the Filipino people are truth, democracy, and militant struggle,” Bayan Chairperson Teddy Casiño said in front of the police. He added that even though they were not able to march through PICC where Trump is, he said, their protest is resonating around the world. (DAA)

author: Stelinsky
title: Ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους του αγώνα
content:
«Ο φασισμός δεν έρχεται από το μέλλον, καινούργιο τάχα κάτι να μας φέρει». Δεν εμφανίζεται σαν κεραυνός εν αιθρία και η επανάνοδός του δεν αποτελεί έκπληξη. Αποτελεί βασική δικλείδα ασφαλείας για το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο: Είναι το πιο σκληρό τους πολιτικό εργαλείο, το οποίο αντλείται από την ίδια εργαλειοθήκη που περιέχει και τη δημοκρατία. «Αναβιώνει», πάντα, όταν η τελευταία παρουσιάζεται αδύναμη να διαχειριστεί τον κοινωνικό και ταξικό ανταγωνισμό, για να τις παράσχει εξωθεσμικές λύσεις.

Σε μια συγκυρία γενικευμένης πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, η εθνικιστική ιδεολογία εξυπηρετεί τη στροφή του πολιτικού σκηνικού σε ζητήματα «εθνικής κυριαρχίας» και αυστηρότερες συνοριακές πολιτικές. Ταυτόχρονα, η διάχυση του ρατσιστικού μίσους στην κοινωνία έρχεται να πλαισιώσει τις κρατικές αφηγήσεις περί εσωτερικού εχθρού – διεργασία που κυρίως γίνεται μέσα από τη στοχοποίηση των μεταναστ(ρι)ών, και τις επαναλαμβανόμενες αναφορές περί «συνεχούς επίθεσης και εισβολής», με σκοπό τον αποπροσανατολισμό της κοινωνικής βάσης από τα βασικά αίτια εξαθλίωσης της ζωής της, και τη συσπείρωσή της γύρω από την εθνική ιδεολογία.

Παράλληλα, οι φασίστες αποτελούν τον απαραίτητο παρακρατικό μηχανισμό που θα αναμετρηθεί με το ανταγωνιστικό κίνημα απέναντι στις επερχόμενες κοινωνικές διεκδικήσεις και αντιστάσεις: Μηχανισμός που δεν υπόκειται στους περιορισμούς της νομιμότητας, και με όρους δρόμου, δρα συμπληρωματικά στο μονοπώλιο της νόμιμης βίας του κράτους. Είναι ακόμα νωπές οι μνήμες από τη δράση των φασιστών κατά τα ταραχώδη χρόνια που ακολούθησαν την εξέγερση του 2008. Τότε, αφενός η προβολή της Χρυσής Αυγής από τα καθεστωτικά media, και αφετέρου η στήριξή της και η συνεργασία με κυβερνητικά στελέχη (κυρίως της Δεξιάς) συνέδραμαν προς αυτήν ακριβώς την κατεύθυνση. Ταυτόχρονα, η δραστηριότητά της αξιοποιήθηκε ως «αντιπολιτευτική» πίεση εκ δεξιών, ώστε το κράτος να ενσωματώσει υπό τον δημοκρατικό μανδύα τα προτάγματά της (χαρακτηριστικά παραδείγματα οι κρατικές επιχειρήσεις-σκούπα «Ξένιος Δίας» στο κέντρο της Αθήνας, όπως και οι επιθέσεις μπάτσων από κοινού με ναζί απέναντι σε αγωνιστές). Κατά τραγική ειρωνεία, η κυβέρνηση Σαμαρά, βασικός υποστηρικτής της Χ.Α., καρπώθηκε και την αντιφασιστική «αναγνώριση» ως αυτή που έβαλε τους φασίστες στη φυλακή. Εκείνα τα χρόνια, βέβαια, το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα έδωσε μεγάλες μάχες στους δρόμους, αναχαιτίζοντας επιτυχώς το φασιστικό φαινόμενο, διατηρώντας διαρκώς οξυμένα τα αντιφασιστικά κοινωνικά αντανακλαστικά.

Το τελευταίο διάστημα, η ακροδεξιά ρητορική και ο φασιστικός οχετός αναβιώνουν σε επίπεδο κεντρικής πολιτικής σκηνής, σε παγκόσμιο κλίμακα. Από τις ΗΠΑ και τη ρατσιστική αντιμεταναστευτική πολιτική του Τραμπ (ICE, τοίχος στα σύνορα με το Μεξικό, απελάσεις μεταναστ-ρι-ών), την επάνοδο ακροδεξιών φιλοαμερικανικών κυβερνήσεων σε χώρες της Νότιας Αμερικής (Χιλή, Βολιβία, Βενεζουέλα, Αργεντινή), μέχρι την εφαρμογή αντιμεταναστευτικών πολιτικών από χώρες της Ευρώπης (κλειστά σύνορα, pushbacks, κατάργηση ασύλου) και την άνοδο ακροδεξιών κομμάτων σε πολλές από αυτές (Ουγγαρία, Αυστρία, Γερμανία, Ιταλία, Γαλλία, Ουκρανία). Και φυσικά τη συνεχιζόμενη εξολόθρευση του παλαιστινιακού λαού από το γενοκτονικό κράτος του Ισραήλ, με τη στήριξη και συμμετοχή των ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ-ΕΕ.

Όλη αυτή η διεργασία διεξάγεται με τηναδιαμφισβήτητη στήριξη εκπροσώπων του κεφαλαίου: Ένας από τους πλουσιότερους ανθρώπους του πλανήτη, ο Ίλον Μάσκ, επιλέγει να στηρίζει οικονομικά την άνοδο φασιστικών/ακροδεξιών κομμάτων και οργανώσεων σε ολόκληρο τον κόσμο (Ρεπουμπλικάνοι-Τραμπ στις ΗΠΑ, Εθνικό Μέτωπο-Λεπεν στη Γαλλία, Λίγκα του Βορρά-Μελόνι στην Ιταλία, AfD-Βάιντελ στη Γερμανία, Κασιδιάρης στην Ελλάδα). Παράλληλα, η στήριξη κολοσσών της ενέργειας, μεγάλων βιομηχανιών και εταιρειών προς το κράτος του Ισραήλ, ώστε να συνεχίζει, χωρίς οικονομικό κόστος, το αιματοκύλισμα των Παλαιστινίων, αποτελεί την ιστορική συνέχεια της σύνδεσης βιομηχάνων-ναζί από τον Β’ Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο.

Στον μικρόκοσμο της ελλαδικής επικράτειας, οι πολιτικές που εφαρμόζονται ενάντια στις/στους μετανάστ(ρι)ες (επανεξέταση ασύλων και αναστολή υποβολής νέων αιτήσεων, μαζικές δολοφονίες στην Πύλο και στην Χίο, pushbacks, τείχος στον Έβρο, στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης-κράτησης), όσο και η εθνικιστική ρητορική περί «εθνικών απειλών» και διαφύλαξης της «εδαφικής ακεραιότητας»συνθέτουν ένα ολοκληρωτικό τοπίο. author: Michael_1973
title: Socialism or Barbarism? - S'bu Zikode
content:
Keynote address by S'bu Zikode, from Abahlali baseMjondolo, at the Third National Conference of the Aotearoa New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies held in Ōtepoti Dunedin, on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

Comrade Programme director, thank you for welcoming me to Aotearoa once again. May I express my sincere gratitude to the New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies and Palestine Solidarity Network Aotearoa for inviting me to speak here today, and across the country. I bring greetings from Abahlali baseMjondolo, our movement in South Africa which now has more than 200,000 members.

I want to begin with the words of a song, a song about socialism, that is often sung in the struggles of the left in South Africa.

Yini iSocialism? Umhlaba wonke ezandleni zabantu Akunamuntu, akunamuntu ongaphatha umhlaba ngayedwa Ayayesaba bo, ayesaba amabhujwa, nongxiwa Ngoba bona, ngobabona befuna ukusetshenzelwa ngabantu

The song asks, ‘What is socialism?’ It answers that socialism is the whole world in the hands of the people. It goes on to say that no one person can own the world on their own. It concludes that the bourgeoisie are afraid of socialism, because they want the people to work for them.

Comrades, as you will all know, in 1915, during the mass slaughter of the First World War, Rosa Luxemburg wrote from a prison cell in Germany that humanity stood at a crossroads. Either it would move towards socialism, towards global justice and peace, or it would collapse into further barbarism. She was writing as millions of workers were being sent to kill each other in the trenches for the profits of their rulers. Four years later she was murdered.

In our movement we have our own version of this choice. Lindokuhle Mnguni, the gifted young chairperson of one of our branches, the eKhenana Commune in Durban, introduced the slogan ‘Socialism or Death’ into our movement. For Lindokuhle, socialism was not something that would come one day in the future, after a revolution, or after an election. Socialism had to be lived now, in the way we occupy land, ensure that it is not bought and sold, manage it democratically, grow food together, ensure that nobody goes hungry, care for each other, build and manage social infrastructure like halls, creches and kitchens, and make decisions together.

For us, like urban and rural movements elsewhere in the world, building socialism from below means building communes, connecting them and building wider forms of democratic popular power from these communes. In the same way that the liberated zones were the bases for anti-colonial movements in countries like Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau, communes – from South Africa to Brazil, Venezuela and elsewhere – are the strongest bases for our movements to build socialism. As Ruthie Wilson Gilmore says, ‘Freedom is a place’.

The price for challenging oppression can be very high. Many comrades around the world have given their lives. On 20 August 2022, Lindokuhle was shot dead in his home. He was the third leader of the eKhenana Commune to be assassinated in less than six months.

Frantz Fanon taught that ‘Each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfill it, or betray it.’ Comrades like Rosa Luxemburg and Lindokuhle Mnguni understood the mission of their generation, and gave their lives to it. Our generation also has a mission. We are living in a time of genocide, of wealth beyond imagination for a few and hunger for millions, of the far right and fascist forces rising and of the poor being turned against each other. We have to decide whether we will fulfil our mission or betray it. In our movement we have often used Fanon’s words. When people find themselves pushed to the margins of the city and of life, they have the opportunity to discover their mission and to decide whether they want to fulfil it or betray it.

I want to speak today about the barbarism that we see around us, in South Africa and around the world, and about the work of building socialism from below, as we have tried to do it in our movement.

When Luxemburg wrote about barbarism she was thinking of the slaughter of the First World War. Today we are witnessing another mass slaughter of human beings. We have all watched the genocide in Gaza. We have watched children being starved, hospitals and schools being bombed, and whole families being buried under the rubble of their homes. We have watched the most powerful governments in the world supply the weapons …

title: AfD-Meldeportale gegen Lehrerinnen und Lehrer: Teil einer weltweiten Kampagne der Rechten gegen emanzipativen Unterricht
content:
Dossier


Der

faschistische brasilianische Präsidentschaftskandidat

 hat es im Programm: Schule ohne Parteien (was bedeutet, schön, wie früher, kolonialistisch lehren, das Land sei am 22. April 1500 von den Portugiesen „entdeckt“ worden); die Teesäufer des Herrn Trump haben es als Ziel: Ideologiefreie Schulen (sprich wir haben den „Wilden Westen“ zivilisiert und die paar toten Indianer haben es eh verdient) und noch mehrere andere. Indische Safran-Faschisten wollen den muslimischen Teil der eigenen Geschichte nicht gerne hören, bei Orban sollen die Kinder auf Panzern rumklettern statt Sozialkunde  und so weiter – da konnte ein rechtsradikaler Ideologen-Verein wie die AFD nicht fehlen: Neutrale Schule nennen sie ihr Denunziations-Programm, erfindungsreich waren sie halt noch nie.

Die Neutralität

 soll dann vermutlich anfangen bei historischen völkischen Idiotien wie etwa der Frankenkönig (und Sachsenschlächter) sei der erste „deutsche“ Kaiser gewesen und enden mit dem Ende des Lehrplanes in bezug auf Nazi-Diktatur und (natürlich, schon aus Eigeninteresse) Kritik an Rassismus aller Art. Erfindungsreicher allemal als AFD-Hetze ist etwa der Protestmodus der fzs gegen diesen Vorstoß. Siehe dazu das allgemeine Echo auf die AFD-Denunziantenkampagne, gewerkschaftliche Stellungnahme und weitere Informationen:


AfD setzt Lehrkräfte unter Druck – Forscher fordert: „Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung“


„Sozialwissenschaftler Tim Engartner erklärt, warum politische Neutralität im Unterricht weder möglich noch gewünscht ist. Er fordert mehr Courage – auch angesichts der AfD-Meldeportale.


Erstarkende Kräfte von Rechts, namentlich die AfD, fordern Lehrkräfte zunehmend dazu auf, sich politisch neutral zu verhalten und berufen sich dabei unter anderem auf den Beutelsbacher Konsens. Der ist seit 50 Jahren die Grundlage politischer Bildung. Im Interview erklärt der Sozialwissenschaftler der Universität zu Köln, Tim Engartner, warum Lehrkräfte nicht nur Haltung zeigen dürfen, sondern sogar müssen, wo Grenzen von Meinungsfreiheit und politischer Einflussnahme liegen und weshalb der Beutelsbacher Konsens angesichts sozialer Medien und gesellschaftlicher Polarisierung weiterentwickelt werden sollte. (…)


Der Beutelsbacher Konsens kennt kein Neutralitätsgebot. Es geht darum, politische Mündigkeit und Urteilsfähigkeit zu fördern – und gerade nicht darum, politische Positionen aus dem Unterricht herauszuhalten.


[Was soll eine Lehrkraft tun, wenn sie von Schülerinnen und Schülern nach ihrer politischen Einstellung gefragt wird?]


Deutlich machen, dass es sich um eine persönliche Überzeugung handelt. Und die Lehrkraft darf den Schülerinnen und Schüler nicht die eigene Meinung aufdrängen.


[Dürfte eine Lehrkraft also sagen: „Ich wähle auf jeden Fall eine demokratische Partei“?]


Ja, das ist eindeutig erlaubt. Sie dürfte auch sagen, dass sie persönlich die AfD für eine Partei hält, die menschenfeindliche Positionen vertritt. Man darf nicht nur deutlich machen, dass bestimmte Werte und Positionen, die von Parteien vertreten werden, nicht mit dem Grundgesetz oder den Menschenrechten vereinbar sind. Man muss es sogar. (…)


Wo genau die Grenze zwischen zulässiger Kritik und unzulässiger Abwertung liegt, ist umstritten – und muss im Einzelfall entschieden werden. Was aber klar ist: Schulen und Lehrkräfte müssen zwar parteipolitisch neutral sein, nicht aber wertneutral. Das ist zentral. (…)


[Kann man denn politisch neutral unterrichten?]


Ich halte das für geradezu unmöglich – und es ist auch nicht das Ziel. Im Gegenteil: Die Lehrkraft soll ihre politische Position durchaus deutlich machen, um Diskussionen anzuregen. (…)


Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung, denn wer schweigt, stimmt zu. Allerdings hat auch die Schulleitung eine wichtige Aufgabe: Sie muss die Lehrkräfte schützen, ihnen den Rücken stärken und darf nicht zulassen, dass Eltern oder auch Parteien einzelne Lehrkräfte persönlich anzugreifen, obwohl diese unsere demokratischen Werte verteidigen

…“
