author: anred
title: Embarcación: cuando la destrucción del monte prepara el terreno para la catástrofe
content:
El violento temporal que azotó a Embarcación, en la provincia de Salta, el jueves 12 de noviembre dejó alrededor de 150 personas que necesitaron atención médica, viviendas dañadas, escuelas afectadas y árboles, postes y tendidos eléctricos derribados. Pero detrás de la devastación provocada por las lluvias y los fuertes vientos hay una historia que no comenzó con la tormenta: décadas de desmontes, avance de la frontera agropecuaria y explotación de los bienes comunes que transformaron profundamente el territorio.

Por Adrián Flores, para Red Eco Alternativo.


Salta – La localidad de Embarcación, en el departamento General José de San Martín, fue el epicentro de un fenómeno meteorológico de enorme intensidad. Las precipitaciones, las ráfagas de viento y la actividad eléctrica provocaron voladuras de techos, caída de árboles y postes de media tensión, cortes de electricidad y daños en establecimientos educativos. La magnitud del temporal obligó a desplegar operativos de emergencia y suspender las clases en las escuelas afectadas.


La violencia de esta tormenta también debe leerse en el contexto de los fenómenos climáticos extremos asociados a El Niño, cuya intensidad puede incrementar las precipitaciones y elevar el riesgo de inundaciones en distintas regiones. El escenario del Súper Niño vuelve todavía más preocupante esta situación. Pero estos fenómenos no actúan sobre territorios intactos: encuentran ecosistemas profundamente degradados por décadas de explotación.


Aquí se cruzan dos dimensiones de una misma crisis. Por un lado, un modelo de producción y consumo capitalista basado en la explotación intensiva de la naturaleza, que contribuye al calentamiento global. Por otro, la expansión de la frontera agropecuaria, los desmontes y la destrucción de los bosques nativos, que reducen la capacidad de los territorios para absorber y regular las lluvias.


En Embarcación, ambas dimensiones convergen dramáticamente. La misma matriz extractivista que impulsa la destrucción del monte profundiza las condiciones para que los fenómenos meteorológicos extremos se conviertan en catástrofes sociales. Las tormentas tienen causas meteorológicas, pero sus consecuencias están profundamente condicionadas por las decisiones económicas y políticas que transforman los territorios en mercancías.


Topadoras sobre territorios ancestralesMientras Embarcación enfrenta las consecuencias del temporal, las comunidades originarias del departamento San Martín continúan resistiendo el avance de los desmontes y el despojo territorial.


A principios de enero de 2026, en Misión Chaqueña, una comunidad wichí de más de 2.000 habitantes ubicada a 48 kilómetros de Embarcación, sus integrantes detectaron nuevamente a personas que derribaban árboles y quemaban sectores del bosque nativo. La respuesta fue inmediata: decenas de mujeres se organizaron y cortaron el camino para impedir el avance sobre su territorio ancestral.


El conflicto involucra al empresario agrícola salteño Claudio Ferrari, quien desde 2023 pretende apropiarse de una franja de monte que rodea a la comunidad. Aquel año, trabajadores vinculados al empresario comenzaron a abrir picadas, talar árboles y colocar postes para alambrar la zona. Ferrari sostuvo que había comprado esas tierras, aunque, según el abogado que acompaña a la comunidad, no presentó documentación que respalde sus pretensiones.


La defensa del territorio también tuvo consecuencias represivas. El miércoles 7 de enero de 2026 fueron detenidos Leonardo Pantoja y Marta Herrera cuando se presentaron en un destacamento policial para denunciar la tala del monte y las amenazas atribuidas al empresario. Marta fue liberada, mientras Greenpeace reclamó la inmediata libertad de Pantoja.


La comunidad cuenta con carpeta técnica, relevamiento georreferenciado y registro de Asuntos Indígenas. Sin embargo, sus integrantes denuncian obstáculos para acceder a la Justicia y señalan que el empresario pretende avanzar sobre tierras ocupadas ancestralmente por el pueblo wichí.


No se trata solamente de una disputa por la propiedad de la tierra. Es la defensa de un territorio que sostiene la identidad, la cultura y las condiciones materiales de vida de generaciones.


3.300 hectáreas arrasadas en territorio wichíLa dimensión de la destrucción quedó nuevamente expuesta en octubre de 2026, cuando Greenpeace difundió una denuncia realizada junto con comunidades wichí por el desmonte de más de 3.300 hectáreas de bosques nativos en el área …

author: Steven Methven
title: Cuts to Benefits Are Not the ‘End to Neoliberalism’ We Were Promised
content:
Tomorrow, the government will publish the Milburn report. That’s a long-awaited review into Britain’s one million young people not in employment, education or training – the so-called NEETs. Its contents, though, won’t come as a huge surprise, with its author, Tony Blair-era health secretary Alan Milburn, taking to the Sunday morning news rounds to pitch his plans while others briefed its contents to the press.


They’re trying to get ahead of what could be

a significant rebellion

 amongst backbench Labour MPs. And who can blame the rebels? After all, with swingeing cuts incoming, they’re the ones who’ll have to explain to young voters with disabilities and other health issues – as well as angry parents – why their lives are apparently worth less than those just a few years older than them.


In politics, life comes at you fast. But not so fast that we can’t remember what prime minister Andy Burnham pledged just four months ago – an

end to neoliberalism in this country

. That’s a tricky term to define, and while Burnham mentioned deregulation, privatisation and the fantasy of trickle-down economics as its major symptoms, there’s a simpler understanding near at hand. Neoliberalism is when a state decides that corporations, rather than citizens, are its clients.


Far from killing neoliberalism off, there’s more than an element of it in Milburn’s NEET plans. 


The shape of his proposals are familiar, the usual carrot-and-stick approach to welfare aimed at the bottom line, rather than the underlying conditions that put people in need of it. First, the cuts. Milburn will recommend that under-25s will

no longer be able to claim sickness and disability benefits

. Instead, there’ll be a one-stop “youth allowance”, capped at the standard rate of universal credit. So that will be a sharp cut to those who might expect to receive the additional universal credit health element. 


Personal independence payments will also be restricted: under 25s will no longer be able to access PIP. Instead, they’ll be able to

apply to “local funds” for help

 with specific “short-term expenses,” though those with the most severe needs will have their existing entitlements protected. 


Who knew that disability or debilitating illness take on a special reality when a person turns 25? Obviously, they don’t. But that ever-present national thought is at the heart of these proposed cuts: the problems – even the health problems – of the young are always a little bit unserious. They won’t be helped by empathy or care, that thought goes on, but only discipline and downplaying.


In his

government report released last month

, professor Peter Fonagy lists in detail the material conditions driving the mental health crisis in the country’s youth. Increased poverty, insecurity and crippling housing costs. Atomisation, loneliness and lack of opportunity. Growing existential dread around the climate, technology and the political future. An education system impoverished by alienation, comparison and intense scrutiny. 


Burnham has called the number of young people on existing benefits

“a moral failure”

. And it’s a profound one for sure. But it’s not their moral failure. It’s ours.


So will our collective failure be addressed in this review?


Unlikely. Instead, what’s been briefed is that the new, pared-back youth allowance will likely be contingent on recipients engaging with programmes aimed at getting them back into work. And while the scope of the cuts are crystal clear, that positive package remains vague. The papers have been told there’ll be investment for employment advisers, mental health support and internships, backed up by – potentially –

a new legal duty on the government

 to furnish every young person with a route into work. 


Great – but maybe let’s get that in place before the cuts? 


No, no. Young people must always get the stick first. And business? It’s the carrot for them.


“I think we should subsidise wages,”

Milburn told Laura Kuenssberg

 on Sunday, “Because young people today are walking into the workplace often with a mental health problem, ADHD or anxiety, and if you’re a small business, that’s a cost that you’ve got to absorb. The state has a responsibility to help them with that.”


The state has a responsibility to help

businesses

 to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on businesses to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on…


Stop the merry-go-round, it’s making us sick.

author: Unknown
title: Russell Means - Revolution and American Indians: “Marxism is as Alien to My Culture as Capitalism”
content:
Author

: Russell Means

Title

: Revolution and American Indians: “Marxism is as Alien to My Culture as Capitalism”

Date

: July, 1980

Source

: https://www.filmsforaction.org/news/revolution-and-american-indians-marxism-is-as-alien-to-my-culture-as-capitalism/


The following speech was given by Russell Means in July 1980

, before several thousand people who had assembled from all over the world for the Black Hills International Survival Gathering, in the Black Hills of South Dakota. It is Russell Means's most famous speech.*


A member of the Oglala Lakota tribe, he was perhaps the most outsized personality in the American Indian Movement, beginning with the 1973 occupation of Wounded Knee. He also had an acting career beginning with his role as Chingachgook in Last of the Mohicans. He passed away Oct 22nd, 2012 at the age 72.


 The only possible opening for a statement of this kind is that I detest writing. The process itself epitomizes the European concept of "legitimate" thinking; what is written has an importance that is denied the spoken. My culture, the Lakota culture, has an oral tradition, so I ordinarily reject writing. It is one of the white world's ways of destroying the cultures of non-European peoples, the imposing of an abstraction over the spoken relationship of a people.


 So what you read here is not what I've written. It's what I've said and someone else has written down. I will allow this because it seems that the only way to communicate with the white world is through the dead, dry leaves of a book. I don't really care whether my words reach whites or not. They have already demonstrated through their history that they cannot hear, cannot see; they can only read (of course, there are exceptions, but the exceptions only prove the rule). I'm more concerned with American Indian people, students and others, who have begun to be absorbed into the white world through universities and other institutions. But even then it's a marginal sort of concern. It's very possible to grow into a red face with a white mind; and if that's a person's individual choice, so be it, but I have no use for them. This is part of the process of cultural genocide being waged by Europeans against American Indian peoples' today. My concern is with those American Indians who choose to resist this genocide, but who may be confused as to how to proceed.


 (You notice I use the term American Indian rather than Native American or Native indigenous people or Amerindian when referring to my people. There has been some controversy about such terms, and frankly, at this point, I find it absurd. Primarily it seems that American Indian is being rejected as European in origin--which is true. But all the above terms are European in origin; the only non-European way is to speak of Lakota--or, more precisely, of Oglala, Brule, etc.--and of the Dineh, the Miccousukee, and all the rest of the several hundred correct tribal names.


 (There is also some confusion about the word Indian, a mistaken belief that it refers somehow to the country, India. When Columbus washed up on the beach in the Caribbean, he was not looking for a country called India. Europeans were calling that country Hindustan in 1492. Look it up on the old maps. Columbus called the tribal people he met "Indio," from the Italian in dio, meaning "in God.")


 It takes a strong effort on the part of each American Indian not to become Europeanized. The strength for this effort can only come from the traditional ways, the traditional values that our elders retain. It must come from the hoop, the four directions, the relations: it cannot come from the pages of a book or a thousand books. No European can ever teach a Lakota to be Lakota, a Hopi to be Hopi. A master's degree in "Indian Studies" or in "education" or in anything else cannot make a person into a human being or provide knowledge into traditional ways. It can only make you into a mental European, an outsider.


 I should be clear about something here, because there seems to be some confusion about it. When I speak of Europeans or mental Europeans, I'm not allowing for false distinctions. I'm not saying that on the one hand there are the by-products of a few thousand years of genocidal, reactionary, European intellectual development which is bad; and on the other hand there is some new revolutionary intellectual development which is good. I'm referring here to the so-called theories of Marxism and anarchism and …

author: Unknown
title: Socialist Strategy within the Architecture of Power
content:
The artwork in this dossier, produced by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, depicts three forms of power: social power in magenta, governmental power in yellow, and systemic power in cyan. Where these forms overlap, new colours emerge, representing their different configurations and interconnections within a broader architecture of power. This composition invites us to consider how power is organised, contested, and transformed through processes of emancipation.


When a radical government takes office with a mandate for transformation, the next morning it will have to confront banks that remain in private hands, mines under corporate control, private mainstream media, and public administration governed by inherited procedures. Capital can postpone investment, transfer money abroad, close factories, hoard essential goods, dismiss workers, and speculate against the currency. The havoc wrought on the economy and population can then be presented as proof that transformation is impossible, all while the government is held responsible for a crisis produced or intensified by forces beyond its control.


This reality reveals a central problem for socialist strategy. Taking governmental office can be an important step toward systemic transformation, but misunderstanding these two forms of power as one and the same can have dangerous consequences. A clear analysis of where power resides and how its different forms interact is necessary to avoid patterns that have plagued revolutionary processes across the world.


An electoral victory may be mistaken for a revolutionary event when a left-wing party has taken office even though the wider state apparatus, the economy, and the institutions that shape common sense remain largely beyond its control. Conversely, a socialist movement may possess considerable social strength without being able to translate that strength into governmental authority or changes to the structures of the state and economy.  The ruling class exercises power through its control over production and the structures that reinforce it, while the working class exercises collective power through strikes, demonstrations, and the organisations it builds through struggle. To use a single word – power – for all these different capacities can confuse political strategy. In this dossier, we therefore distinguish three related forms of power as an analytical framework for debate and discussion:


Social power

 is the organised capacity of a class or political bloc to act collectively, reproduce material life, and contest the ruling class’s command over society. It is built through institutions of struggle and cooperation such as trade unions, peasant and women’s organisations, cooperatives, community structures, cultural and media projects, political education, and political parties. Through these institutions, a class or political bloc can struggle to reshape common sense and establish moral and intellectual leadership.


Governmental power

 is the capacity to assume governmental authority, whether through elections, insurrection, or another political rupture, and to use executive, legislative, and administrative institutions to pursue a programme. It provides access to important instruments of administration and policy but does not, by itself, amount to control of the state or the wider system.


Systemic power

 is the capacity to transform the class character and institutional form of the state, bring the major means of production and the social surplus under democratic authority, and reorganise the relations through which society reproduces itself. It includes state power but cannot be reduced to it because capitalist social relations are reproduced beyond the formal institutions of the state – through property, finance, the world market, colonial relations, culture, and social reproduction – and many of these relations exceed the reach of any single government or national state.


These forms are analytical distinctions, not sealed compartments, and do not constitute a fixed sequence. They overlap, develop unevenly, and can pull in opposite directions. Governmental power may become a bridge between organised social power and systemic transformation. It may also weaken popular organisation and reconcile it to the existing system. The central strategic question is therefore not which form of power matters but how the three can be connected in a process of emancipation.


Social Power


Society is not …

author: Freedom Editor
title: To remember Durruti: “Solidarity is the best incentive”
content:
Ninety years since the death of Buenaventura Durruti, the greatest military leader of the Spanish Revolution

Born into the working class on 14 July 1896 in Leon, Buenaventura Durruti became a mechanic by trade and a prominent local union organiser of the socialist Unión General de Trabajadores (UGT, General Union of Workers). Expelled from UGT after the August 1917 general strike for his militancy, he left Leon and joined the mass anarcho-syndicalist union, the Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT, National Confederation of Labour), and became an anarchist. He soon became a leading activist within the movement, playing a key role in the resistance to Franco’s coup of July 1936 and the subsequent social revolution.

The Trotskyist Felix Morrow proclaimed in his Revolution and Counter-Revolution in Spain that Durruti was “the greatest military figure produced by the war” while, of course, dismissing anarchism by suggesting he was “no theoretician, but an activist leader of masses… his words express the revolutionary outlook of the class-conscious workers”. This ignores that Durruti’s words, activity, and outlook did not spring out of thin air but rather were informed by and reflected his anarchist politics, history, activity, and vision—which in turn reflected his experiences and needs as a member of the CNT and the working class.

While undoubtedly remembered as a man of action, indeed his exploits across Spain, Europe and South America are legendary, Durruti read anarchist literature and press, took part in the debates within the Spanish anarchist movement, and was a noted public speaker. However, it is for his role in the Spanish Revolution and Civil War that he is best remembered.

When the military did revolt on 17 July 1936, Durruti took a leading part in organising the resistance in Barcelona amongst the various CNT unions and defence committees. A general strike was called, weapons seized, and 19 July saw the army defeated by the people armed.

The long desired social revolution swept the city and other parts of free Spain – as anarchists had long argued, workers seized the workplaces, peasants the land, popular assemblies and revolutionary committees were formed. The collectivised economy benefited all rather than the owning class, while also providing weaponry to the militias (with workplaces refashioned to do so). Non-economic social relationships likewise began to transform, and anarchist women organised the Mujeres Libres to empower women and fight the sexism that permeated Spanish society and, sadly, the anarchist movement.

Anarchist theory, which had always argued that a social revolution could only be defended by the people armed, was also applied when the CNT organised militias to liberate those areas of Spain under military control. Other unions and parties did likewise, although unlike those the CNT militias were run by their members with elected officers and committees, all sharing the same living conditions. As Durruti argued:

“I don’t believe – and everything happening around us confirms this – that you can run a workers’ militia according to classic military rules. I believe that discipline, co-ordination, and planning are indispensable, but we shouldn’t define them in terms taken from the world that we’re destroying. We have to build on new foundations. My comrades and I are convinced that solidarity is the best incentive for arousing an individual’s sense of responsibility and a willingness to accept discipline as an act of self-discipline.”

As the Durruti column marched towards Zaragoza, liberated villages and towns started the process of transforming society and the economy by forming collectives. These voluntary groups turned the land, machinery and other resources into common property, to be managed, worked, and benefited from by all rather than a few landlords or capitalists. For Durruti, the war and the revolution were inseparable:

“Our comrades on the front know for whom and for what they fight. They feel themselves revolutionaries and they fight, not in defence of more or less promised new laws, but for the conquest of the world, of the factories, the workshops, the means of transportation, their bread and the new culture.”

With the Republican government preferring to arm the rearguard (against the revolution) over the CNT militias, the Aragon Front stagnated. Yet the CNT militias were recognised as being the best fighters, as shown by part of the Durruti being sent to Madrid …

author: Unknown
title: “Gen Z Regulates” : A New Wave of Unrest in Germany?
content:
For months, unrest has been spreading across Europe. In

Spain

, a movement against evictions and gentrification culminated on November 11 in a countrywide general strike. In

France

, student revolt set off the most intense street confrontations since the

Yellow Vest movement

. Albania has seen wave upon wave of clashes since last February. On Halloween, the European youth protests finally reached Germany.


Under the motto

“Gen Z regelt”

 (“Gen Z regulates”), tens of thousands took to the streets of nearly 40 German cities on October 31. While a large-scale uprising like the

one

 in France remains unlikely, the first cracks in the pacification of society are starting to show. In this report, two anarchists describe their experiences in two different demonstrations and discuss the potential of the events.


More demonstrations on the same theme are scheduled for

November 20

.


A stylish banner in front of the “Gen Z Regelt” protest in Göttingen. What would Goethe have said?


Germany in Crisis


The demonstration on October 31 took place in a general context of crisis. In Germany, as elsewhere around the globe, inflation has run rampant over the last six years, driven by the pandemic, Putin’s invasion of Ukraine and the consequent loss of cheap natural gas from Russia, and, most recently, the US-Iran war.


Another growing influence on the economy is the climate catastrophe. It is

estimated

 that Germany will lose around 30 billion euros a year as a consequence of its impact. In one week, a heatwave at the end of June

killed

 close to 10,000 people. Unlike countries that have long-term experience with temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius, only 10% of homes in Germany have air conditioning; with the exception of intensive care units and operating rooms, most hospitals and nursing homes don’t have it, so people who experienced heat stroke were treated in overheated rooms. Senior citizens and those with preexisting health problems were especially hard hit: in at least one nursing home, temperatures

reached

 up to 50 degrees Celsius.


A protester in the German city of Essen asks to stop some of the impacts of climate change.


Who dies as a consequence of climate change is determined mostly by class. Germany also faces a housing crisis—

something like 53% of people live in rented homes

—and the cheapest flats are generally located right beneath the roofs of buildings several stories high. These buildings were built to keep heat in, so during heat waves, temperatures in the flats at night often stayed above the outside temperatures at same time.


On top of this, the government comprised of the neoliberal left (SPD) and Christian conservative (CDU/CSU) parties has introduced an unpopular austerity program in order to push through a massive increase in military spending, which started after the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It would take another article to list all the financial cuts involved. Workers and middle-class people will have many billions less in “social benefits”—in other words, they get less back from the work and resources that the state and capitalists take from them.


Some 12% of all jobs in Germany are

directly in state institutions

, in addition to fully state-owned companies and other organizations connected to the state, like the public health insurance agencies and public media companies. Many of these have stop hiring because of the financial situation. At the same time, German economic growth is stagnating. Consequently, “Gen Z” career entrants confront a context in which companies are trying to figure out how to use artificial intelligence to replace them amid an employment market that is already much worse than previous generations faced. This is undermining the last vestiges of a social contract between companies and the state on one side and segments of the youth on the other.


Study, get degree, and you can have a middle-class life? Not anymore.


Finally, some international fashions trends like ski glasses are reaching German youth.


Unemployment is rising among university and college graduates. The social situation isn’t as catastrophic as it has become in other countries, but by contrast with many other countries, people in Germany do not have much experience helping each other directly. German society has focused on the state as the only thinkable source of support when people lose their jobs or experience other setbacks.


As a result, anger has spread …

author: Unknown
title: Kalkan: The women's freedom movement provides leadership to the entire struggle
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave a lengthy interview to Medya Haber TV.


In the third and last part of this lengthy interview, he spoke about the importance of the women's movement, the PKK and the international situation.


Part one of the interview can be read

here

, and the second

here

.


I

t seems that there are people around the world raising their voices against this situation. Developments are taking place in this direction. The left has returned to power in Brazil. In Serbia, the side supported by the student movement came to power. Trump also lost. There are protests on the streets of Europe every day. How should we interpret these developments in the context of your latest assessment?


Recently, I have been thinking about certain things. Why have they destroyed Iran and Ukraine to such an extent? They also destroyed Syria. I remember the period when efforts were being made to develop Syria. A great deal of capital had been invested, and construction was taking place. This is the nature of the system. It destroys everything and then creates new business opportunities for itself through reconstruction. Naturally, while reconstruction takes place, the owners of capital add billions to their existing billions. They exploit people to such an extent and make enormous profits. Soon, for example, the reconstruction of Iran and Ukraine will begin. The monopolies will profit. They will make unprecedented profits from rebuilding Ukraine. New weapons will also be manufactured to replace those used in its destruction, and the monopolies of the arms industry will profit as well. This situation demonstrates more clearly than anything else the nature of the existing system, the system of power and the state, and the point it has reached under capitalist modernity. It is a system capable of launching even more severe attacks. Its internal contradictions and conflicts have become so deep.


Their greed for profit is so powerful that they are prepared to carry out every kind of attack to make more money and seize what others possess. Do you know what frightens them? Two things. The first is the fear of the revolutionary struggle of the peoples. They fear that if they fight among themselves, society might take advantage of the situation, develop consciousness, organise itself and enter into a revolutionary democratic struggle. They fear that an alternative capable of overthrowing them might emerge. That is their first fear. The October Revolution of 1917 instilled this fear in them. Earlier revolutionary attempts also did so. Many revolutionary developments throughout the twentieth century reinforced it. Today, they calculate this possibility every day. They live in fear. The second thing they fear is the weapons they have created. For example, we have been saying that the Third World War has been continuing for 30 or 35 years. It is not as intense or decisive in military terms as the First World War. Nor is it like the Second World War. Why? Because it cannot be. They cannot conduct the Third World War in that way. If they did, those launching the attacks would not only destroy their opponents but also destroy themselves.


The weapons they would use have reached a level where they threaten to destroy nature, the Earth, humanity, all living beings and the planet itself. That is the point we have reached. It is this fear that prevents them from escalating the war further. Some people say, "The military dimension is weak. These are preparations for the Third World War. The Third World War will come." The Third World War is already taking place. As we say in Kurdish to such people, "Rojbaş", meaning "Good morning!" It has been going on for 30 or 35 years. There will not be a war like the First or Second World War. That will not happen. Anyone who attempts such a thing would have to be considered completely insane. It would lead humanity towards extinction. Recently, people who do not seem entirely rational have risen towards positions of power. Naturally, humanity has experienced great fear in many areas. That is what was actually described as the rise of the right. There is no such thing as simply the rise of the right. What is rising is this danger. The system of capitalist modernity has reached that point. For the time being, they are still exercising some restraint. We should recognise that. But nobody really knows how long this can continue.


'We must resist this …

author: Antisystemic
title: Αναζητώντας τον Χαμένο Πολιτικό Χρόνο:  Για τους φίλους και τους εχθρούς του πολυεθνικού προλεταριάτου  στον ελλαδικό χώρο
content:
Αναζητώντας τον Χαμένο Πολιτικό Χρόνο


Αναδημοσιεύω εδώ το κείμενο πολιτικής ανάλυσης που έλαβα από σύντροφο και συνέταξε η Ομάδα Πολιτικής Αυτομόρφωσης, μέσα από τη συλλογική της εργασία. Το κείμενο ανοίγει την κουβέντα γύρω απ’ το φλέγον θέμα ενός διεθνισμού στην πράξη, στραμμένου όχι μόνο προς τα έξω, αλλά και προς τα μέσα. Μιλάει για μια διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη που έχει σαν αποδέκτη το πολυεθνικό προλεταριάτο που ζει στη χώρα μας, η οποία θα σφυρηλατηθεί οργανικά μέσα από κοινούς αγώνες και την αμοιβαία σύμπραξη σε εγχειρήματα ταξικής χειραφέτησης. Με άλλα λόγια, το ζήτημα που θέτει δεν είναι άλλο από την ενότητα του συνόλου της εργατικής τάξης από-τα-κάτω και ως τέτοιο θεωρώ πως αξίζει να διαβαστεί.


Για έναν συμπεριληπτικό και πρακτικό διεθνισμό


ενάντια στην κυρίαρχη τάξη πραγμάτων


Κρίση, Πόλεμος, Φασισμός, Γενοκτονία. Αυτές είναι οι κυρίαρχες συντεταγμένες της εποχής μας, μετά την παγκόσμια δομική καπιταλιστική κρίση που ξέσπασε από το 2008. Τα αφεντικά ακολούθησαν ξανά την ίδια συνταγή που έμαθαν από τις κρίσεις του 1870-1880, του 1929-1945, του 1970-1980 κ.ο.κ: πόλεμος και υπερεκμετάλλευση της εργασίας, εξόντωση των πλεοναζόντων πληθυσμών, τακτική χρήση του φασισμού απέναντι στους καταπιεσμένους, στρατιωτικοποίηση της κοινωνικής ζωής και του κρατικού μηχανισμού, εξωτερίκευση σε έναν παγκόσμιο αποικιακό πόλεμο. Και όμως, ξανά και ξανά, οι/τα καταπιεσμένοι/ες/α δεν έπαψαν να απαντούν στην πολεμική αναδιάρθρωση των αφεντικών. Την καπιταλιστική κρίση ακολούθησαν κύματα παγκόσμιων κινητοποιήσεων και εξεγέρσεων όπως το 2009-2012, το 2018-20201, την περίοδο του lockdown, και μέχρι σήμερα, με ατμομηχανή της ιστορίας τα κινήματα στον Παγκόσμιο Νότο, στη Δυτική Ασία, την Αφρική και τη Λατινική Αμερική, και την άνοδο του κοινωνικού ανταγωνισμού και εντός του Παγκόσμιου Βορρά, στην καρδιά των μητροπολίτικων κέντρων.


Και κάθε παγκόσμιος εξεγερτικός κύκλος απαντήθηκε μέχρι σήμερα από μια καπιταλιστική αντιεξέγερση: περισσότερη αστυνομία, στρατιωτικά πραξικοπήματα, «αριστερές κυβερνήσεις», καταστολή, ενσωμάτωση, έλεγχος. Όμως μετά το 2020, έχουμε περάσει σε μια νέα φάση της καπιταλιστικής αναδιάρθρωσης. Φαίνεται πως πια η καπιταλιστική καταστολή, ενσωμάτωση, έλεγχος, δεν αρκούν.


Ο καπιταλισμός βρίσκεται σε παρακμή, που καθώς βουλιάζει στη δίνη των ιστορικών του αντιφάσεων, λυσσάει και αντεπιτίθεται. Ο δυτικός, αμερικανοσιωνιστικός άξονας αντιδρά στην άνοδο των νέων κοινωνικών, επιθυμητικών και παραγωγικών δυνάμεων, με φορείς τις νέες γενιές καταπίεσης, εκμετάλλευσης και αντίστασης εκτός του δυτικού κέντρου και στις εσωτερικές περιφέρειες των καπιταλιστικών μητροπόλεων. Οι πολεμικές εκστρατείες του αμερικανοσιωνισμού, στις οποίες πρωτοστατεί η Ελλάδα, δεν στρέφονται απλώς κατά ένοπλων οργανώσεων ή κρατών στο Ιράκ, στο Αφγανιστάν, στη Συρία, στην Παλαιστίνη, στο Ιράν, στο Λίβανο, στην Υεμένη και αλλού, αλλά, πρώτα και κύρια, στρέφονται κατά ολόκληρων λαών, επιδιώκοντας την κατάκτηση της γης και των πόρων της, και καταστρέφοντας κρίσιμες υλικές υποδομές κοινωνικής αναπαραγωγής της ζωής, όπως ενεργειακά, διατροφικά και υγειονομικά συστήματα. Θέτοντας το δίλημμα φασιστική γενοκτονία ή υποταγή στον κατακτητή, ο αμερικανοσιωνιστικός καπιταλισμός επιδιώκει να επιβάλλει στους λαούς της Παλαιστίνης, των αραβικών χωρών, του Κουρδιστάν, της Αφρικής και της Λατινικής Αμερικής, μια ψεύτικη συναίνεση στην υποταγή και την εκμετάλλευση, στους κόμβους κρίσιμων εμπορικών και ενεργειακών ροών στην Ασία, τη Μεσόγειο, την Αφρική.


Απέναντι στην παρακμιακή, αυτοκρατορική λύσσα και επιθετικότητα του αμερικανοσιωνιστικού άξονα, με τη βαθιά εμπλοκή της Ελλάδας, εμφανίζονται η Ρωσία, η Κίνα και άλλες δυνάμεις, υποσχόμενες ένα εναλλακτικό μέλλον για τις εργατικές τάξεις και τους λαούς του κόσμου, αναπαράγοντας όμως καταπιεστικές και εκμεταλλευτικές δομές στο εσωτερικό τους.


Από την επαναστατική πλημμύρα Αλ-Άκσα της 7ης Οκτώβρης του 20232, η Σιωνιστική Αποικία εμφανίστηκε ως αυτό που πραγματικά είναι: ένα γενοκτονικό οικοδόμημα πάνω σε σαθρά εποικιστικά κοινωνικά θεμέλια, και ένας αδύναμος κρίκος του παγκόσμιου δυτικοκεντρικού και αυτοκρατορικού καπιταλισμού, με τη Γάζα να συμπυκνώνει εκρηκτικά τις αντιφάσεις του. Ο κοινωνικός πόλεμος στην ιστορική Παλαιστίνη, ανάμεσα στο εποικιστικό στρατιωτικοποιημένο κεφάλαιο και τον παλαιστινιακό προλεταριοποιημένο πληθυσμό, αποτέλεσμα ιστορικών διαδικασιών εκτοπισμού του αντιστεκόμενου παλαιστινιακού λαού από τις διαδικασίες αναπαραγωγής του όλο και πιο τριτογενοποιημένου και αυτοματοποιημένου …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: In Amsterdam on MONDAY? Join Chris dePloeg, Jason Hickel and more, LIVE, for “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
Pakuis de Zwijger

, Monday, November 23rd: :ive with Jason Hickel,

Ghassan Abu-Sittah

,

Harriët Bergman

,

Chihiro Geuzebroek

,

Max de Ploeg

 and the author!


In collaboration with In collaboration with Pijke ter Laak, join

Pakuis de Zwijger

 for a conversation with author Chris de Ploeg about his new book, a radical and urgent indictment of the global capitalist system and the imperial violence it unleashes upon people and planet alike. At its core, the book argues that genocide and ecocide are not tragic byproducts of capitalism – they are its fundamental features.


Together with renowned climate author Jason Hickel (in person), frontline Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah (joining online) and our moderator, climate justice activist and researcher Harriët Bergman, we will dive deeper into the interconnections of the great challenges of our time–and more importantly, how to fight back. There will also be cultural performances from Chihiro Geuzebroek and brothers Chris and Max de Ploeg, tying their ancestral struggles in Bolivia and Armenia to the global struggle for liberation.

REGISTER HERE!


REVIEWS:


Morning Star

:

 “How did such a horror come to pass?” by Alex Hall


“

The Exterminating Empire

 began life as a Master’s thesis, nurtured into book form by Jason Hickel — the degrowth economist and author of The Divide, who contributes the foreword. The mentorship was well placed and De Ploeg has produced an impressively searing panorama of our global predicament…”


Counterpunch

, “

Resisting Annihilation: Reviewing “The Exterminating Empire”

, by Seth Sandronsky


“…de Ploeg, who does far more than compile lists of atrocities, draws parallels between the American holocaust of the native inhabitants’ relations with buffaloes and Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and their farming of olive trees. Land theft and separating those living on the land from it are nothing new. The author has skin in the game, given his family survived the Armenian genocide and Nazi holocaust…”


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition …

author: Stelinsky
title: Ο ήλιος που χάνεται στον ορίζοντα του πολέμου
content:
Στοχεύοντας πληθυσμούς μέσα από τον εσωτερικό εχθρό

Το κεφαλαιοκρατικό οικονομικό σύστημα βρίσκεται, αδιαμφισβήτητα, σε κρίση. Αλήθεια, ποιος πείθεται από τις «αναπτυξιακές» αφηγήσεις που αντικατέστησαν μια μακρινή κρίση που παρήλθε; Η κρίση στον καπιταλισμό αποτελεί δομικό στοιχείο. Δεν είναι σύμπτωμα κακοδιαχείρισης, ούτε προϊόν τεχνικών σφαλμάτων. Δεν είναι δείκτης αρρώστιας, αλλά το αντίθετο – δείκτης υγείας. Ο ήλιος που χάνεται στον ορίζοντα, για να ξαναβγεί την επομένη, δεν σημαίνει πως ο κόσμος έχει πρόβλημα.

Το φυσικό σκοτάδι, βέβαια, κρύβει μια γοητεία. Αντιθέτως, η σκοτεινιά των καιρών μας, μας προδιαθέτει μονάχα για φρικαλεότητες – ιδρώτας, αίμα, πόνος, και στο βάθος θάνατος.

Η μετά-covid εποχή είναι η εποχή της πολεμικής διαχείρισης αυτής της κρίσης. Η ηγεμονία του δυτικού μπλοκ συμφερόντων τίθεται υπό αμφισβήτηση. Δεν είναι μόνο η «εξάντληση» των πετρελαϊκών αποθεμάτων και των φυσικών ορυκτών πόρων σε μια εποχή αυξημένης «ζήτησής» τους. Οι νέες τεχνολογικές δυνατότητες ανοίγουν νέα πεδία εκμετάλλευσης και κερδοφορίας όσον αφορά την ταχύτητα μετάδοσης και επεξεργασίας πληροφοριών, τις παραγωγικές δυνατότητες, και φυσικά τον έλεγχο των πληθυσμών. Η στροφή όλο και περισσότερων εθνικών οικονομιών προς την πολεμική βιομηχανία αποδεικνύει με τον πιο εμφατικό τρόπο πως ο κόσμος, όπως τον ξέρουμε, γυρίζει σελίδα, ακριβώς επειδή το γεωπολιτικό σκηνικό ρευστοποιείται σε μια φάση που ο καπιταλισμός χρειάζεται το σκοτάδι για να ξεφορτωθεί το περισσευούμενο κεφάλαιο (ανθρώπινο και υλικό). Στην παρούσα συγκυρία, τα δύο κεντρικά ανταγωνιστικά κρατικοκαπιταλιστικά μονοπώλια (των ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ και της Κίνας-Ρωσίας), βρίσκονται σε μια τροχιά ανταγωνισμού και αποκεντρωμένης σύγκρουσης, προσπαθώντας να ξαναμοιράσουν τη γη και τους πόλους επιρροής τους, και να εξασφαλίσουν νέες κερδοφόρες ενεργειακές και εμπορικές οδούς. Ο ρωσο-ουκρανικός πόλεμος, η εισβολή στην Βενεζουέλα και αποκλεισμός της Κούβας από τις ΗΠΑ, η σύγκρουση ΗΠΑ-Ισραήλ με το Ιράν και ο αποκλεισμός των στενών του Ορμούζ, η αλλαγή καθεστώτος στην Συρία, υπό τον έλεγχο της Τουρκίας-ΝΑΤΟ, αλλά και η συνεχιζόμενη γενοκτονία του Παλαιστινιακού Λαού, από το Ισραήλ, με την στήριξη και συνενοχή ολόκληρης της Δυτικής ιμπεριαλιστικής μηχανής, είναι μερικά από τα βασικά στιγμιότυπα που συνθέτουν ένα γενικευμένο πολεμικό σκηνικό σε χρόνο ενεστώτα. Αντάρτες αγωνιστές/ριες απ’ το Κουρδιστάν και το Μεξικό, περιγράφουν αυτή τη συνθήκη ως το αποκορύφωμα του Γ’ Παγκοσμίου Πολέμου που διαρκεί ήδη από τα τέλη της προηγούμενης χιλιετίας.

Η καπιταλιστική κρίση μεταφράζεται σε στεγαστική, επισιτιστική κρίση, στην ακρίβεια του πληθωρισμού, σε πιο εντατικές εργασιακές συνθήκες με φθηνότερη εργατική δύναμη, σε υποτίμηση των δημοσίων προνοιακών παροχών (υγεία, παιδεία, μετακίνηση) και των βασικών κοινωνικών αγαθών (ρεύμα, νερό, στέγη).

Η διαχείριση της κρίσης αυτής, φυσικά απαιτεί από κάθε κράτος μια πολιτική προληπτικής αντιμετώπισης του πληθυσμού. Η ανασφάλεια και ο φόβος είναι πάντοτε για την κυριαρχία αχαρτογράφητα νερά, ικανά να εκβάλλουν σε συλλογικές αντιστάσεις και κοινωνικούς αγώνες, που θα προτείνουν εναλλακτικές στην ανέχεια του καπιταλισμού (όπως συνέβη με τον μεγαλειώδη αγώνα για την υπεράσπιση των Προσφυγικών). Ο φόβος και η ανασφάλεια είναι εκρηκτικές ύλες που με τον κατάλληλο πυροκροτητή μπορούν να οδηγήσουν σε κοινωνικές εξεγέρσεις (όπως στη Γαλλία και την Ισπανία), βάζοντας στιβαρά αναχώματα στην πολιτική εξαθλίωσης των από τα κάτω, επισημαίνοντας πως η έφοδος προς έναν άλλο κόσμο είναι εφικτή.

Ένα κλασικό εργαλείο διαχείρισης πληθυσμού, λοιπόν, είναι αυτό του «εσωτερικού εχθρού», κατά το οποίο ποινικοποιούνται κοινωνικές ομάδες, συμπεριφορές, στάσεις κ.λπ., η αντιμετώπιση των οποίων προβάλλεται μεθοδικά ώστε να αποτελέσει παράδειγμα για όλη την κοινωνία. Ο κόσμος του αγώνα και το ευρύτερο ανταγωνιστικό κίνημα βρίσκονταν ανέκαθεν στο στόχαστρο, ενώ ανά περιόδους στοχοποιούνται και άλλες κοινωνικές ομάδες όπως οι οπαδοί, η παραβατική νεολαία, οι μετανάστες κ.ο.κ. – στοχοποίηση που πάντα συνοδεύεται από επικοινωνιακές καμπάνιες διάχυσης ηθικού πανικού στην κοινωνία.

Αν σε περιόδους «ειρήνης», η πολιτική σταθερότητα αποτελεί κρίσιμο παράγοντα για την οικονομική ανάπτυξη, τότε η διασφάλισή της σε μια περίοδο γενικευμένης πολεμικής προετοιμασίας κρίνεται επιτακτική. Σε μια τέτοια περίοδο, όπως αυτή που διανύουμε, η έννοια του εσωτερικού εχθρού διαστέλλεται, ενόσω τα κράτη οχυρώνονται νομικά-ποινικά, και επικοινωνιακά-πολιτικά απέναντί του. title: Groupe de parole & d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste
content:
Groupe de parole & d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste


On vous invite chaleureusement à notre prochain groupe de parole et d'organisation anarchiste contre l'inceste, qui se tiendra le vendredi 27 novembre à partir de 18h30 au

CICP

, 21 rue Voltaire, 75011, Paris (salle verte, 1

er

 étage).


Puisque l'inceste nous concerne tous.tes, mais aussi parce que s'y reconnaître n'est pas toujours chose facile, l'espace est ouvert à tous.tes. On pourra se scinder en deux si besoin : un groupe de parole + un groupe d'organisation.


L'idée du groupe de parole


Elle part de nos besoins : celui de casser les silences qui nous détruisent, en parlant collectivement d'inceste. Mais aussi celui de se reconnaître pour s'entraider face à la famille, au trauma, aux institutions, face aussi à la vie qui ne nous épargne pas, voire face à nous-même et à la reproduction des violences que nous avons subies.


L'idée du groupe d'organisation


Elle part de notre envie de diffuser une culture de lutte contre l'inceste, d'organiser des événements publics, de faire de l'agitation autour du sujet, des tags, d'écrire ou de dessiner ensemble pour faire des tracts, des revues, des livres ou des podcasts, ou toute autre chose qui nous paraîtra nécessaire et nous fera envie

 

!


Pourquoi un groupe anarchiste contre l'inceste

 

?


Il existe de nombreux groupes de parole et d'organisation contre l'inceste qui basculent souvent dans le développement personnel ou dans l'organisation autour de leaders ou de figures individuelles (pour ne citer que ces deux exemples). On a envie de pouvoir attaquer la famille, l'État, la police et la justice et on a envie de faire les choses par nous-mêmes. Politiser l'inceste nous paraît être une donnée essentielle de notre démarche puisque le système-inceste se fonde sur l'autorité familiale, la domination adulte et/ou patriarcale. On avait envie de pouvoir tisser des discussions qui nous ressemblent et de développer ensemble une analyse politique à la fois pragmatique et radicale contre l'inceste.


Amène de la nourriture à partager si tu peux

 

!


Hâte de vous y voir

 

!


Des incesté.es révolté.es

Note for readers: This is a transcript of Zimbabwean-American Zoé Samudzi’s panel titled “On A Black Feminist Anarchism” given at the Orange County Anarchist Bookfair on March 25th, 2017, in Anaheim, California. Despite the rougher audio quality from the video recording of the original panel, the folks associated in the production of “A Black Autonomy Reader” (Seditionist Distribution, 2024), a compilation of Black autonomist and anarchist texts throughout history, were able to transcribe a large amount of Zoé’s panel. While there was a Q&A section where Samudzi answered roughly 3-4 questions from the audience, much of the audience’s questions are garbled compared to Zoé’s clear answers picked up by their microphone. As such, this transcription is solely of what they said as part of her panel, not the answers they gave.

This updated transcription, done by myself, corrects nearly all omissions from the original, restores words that were left out, corrects misspelled names, and includes revisions to grammar and citations. Samudzi’s multiple “and’s” were omitted for readability. Public figures, book titles, and specific events mentioned have been footnoted, recognizing that readers may be unfamiliar with the histories and cultural contexts of what is being discussed. - AnarchoGuac

Hi everyone. I’m really excited to be here. I don’t like — I much prefer to have generative dialogue spaces than to talk at you. So I’m gonna try to keep it on the shorter side, and then we can have some more conversation on what I am trying to talk about.

In her 1983 literary work In Search Of Our Mothers’ Gardens, Alice Walker described a womanist as “a woman who loves another woman, sexually and/or non-sexually. She appreciates and prefers women’s culture, women’s emotional flexibility. She’s committed to the survival and the wholeness of an entire people. She’s not a separatist, except periodically for health. She loves the spirit, she loves struggle, she loves herself, regardless.”[1]

So I have a really complicated relationship with political theory, particularly as someone that studied political science as an undergraduate. My relationship to political theory, especially to the kind of horribly white supremacist enlightenment values of “rationality” and “objectivity” is generally, like, a knee-jerk reaction to the whiteness and the eurocentricity of it and of the canon. With regards to anarchism specifically, I often feel alienated from the theory because of the non-white and non-western globality of the politics of the ideology that have, all of a sudden, been turned into this white politic. Anarchistic values of horizontalism, of mutual aid, of voluntary participation, of non-extra or markably anti-state organization existed prior to Pierre-Joseph Proudhon’s self description of “anarchist” in the mid-1800s, or William Godwin’s framework laying work in the 1790s. title: Когда срок не заканчивается — воркшоп «Огней свободы» на Анархистской книжной ярмарке в Амстердаме
content:
Проект «Огни свободы» сообщает, что в это воскресенье в 11:30 в Амстердаме группа проведёт воркшоп о положении заключённых анархисто:к в России и возможных путях их освобождения:

В России сроки заключения для анархисто:к и других политических заключенных становятся не только очень длительными, но и потенциально бессрочными. В последние годы силовики все чаще возбуждают новые уголовные дела против людей, уже находящихся в заключении, — на основании разговоров с сокамерниками или провокаций. Первоначальный конец срок уже не обязательно означает освобождение.

Используя преследование анархиста-математика Азата Мифтахова в качестве отправной точки, мы поговорим о нескольких взаимосвязанных формах тюремного подавления: неоднократные преследования, неформальная тюремная кастовая система и способы ее использования властями, пытки и изоляция, а также о том, как заключенные продолжают сопротивляться, мыслить, творить и поддерживать других.

Далее мы хотим выйти за рамки вопроса о том, как поддержать заключенных, и задать более сложный вопрос: что может сделать международная солидарность, когда помощи человеку в течение срока заключения уже недостаточно? Какие стратегии могут реально способствовать освобождению?

Встреча будет сочетать презентацию с открытой дискуссией. Между этими двумя частями мы сделаем небольшой перерыв чифиром и коряком — тюремный торт. Кастовые правила в российских местах заключения определяют, кому разрешено находиться в круге в такие моменты. Мы хотим символически отвергнуть эту иерархию, употребляя чифир и коряк, не воспроизводя это разделение.

Мы надеемся, что эта встреча станет не только дискуссией о репрессиях в России, но и обменом мнениями о том, как международная анархистская солидарность может перейти от поддержки заключенных товарищей к борьбе за их свободу.

Где: Амстердам IIRE Lombokstraat 40

title: Intensify, Disrupt, Sabotage, De-bank, Abolish & Liberate* – Solidarität mit Daniel V. [de+eng]
content:
* “Disrupt, Identify, Defund, Debank, Arrest & Prosecute”: Trump-Regierung droht linken Gruppen in einem Interview des US-Außenministeriums.


Disclaimer: Leider können viele Informationen über Daniel V. und die von ihm übernommenen Verantwortungen nicht bestätigt werde, da die meisten der „zugänglichen“ Quellen in den Händen der deutschen Medien liegen. Da sein Brief nie vollständig veröffentlicht wurde, können wir keine akkuraten Informationen wiedergeben und wir haben entschieden, nicht für ihn zu sprechen. Obwohl wir versucht haben, so viele Informationen aus online Quellen wie möglich zusammen zu sammeln, können wir deren Richtigkeit nicht garantieren und bitten die Lesenden nichts als definitiv hinzunehmen.


In verschiedenen Kämpfen intensiviert sich die Repression gegen jene, die Widerstand leisten. Von der Solidarität mit Palästina und Widerstand gegen die Militarisierung, zu militantem Antifaschismus und direkter Aktion – der Staat breitet seine Werzeuge aus, um diejenigen zu verfolgen, einzuschüchtern und zu isolieren, welche seine Autorität in Frage stellen. Unter dem öffentlich ausgerufenen Krieg gegen „Linksextremismus“ [1] wird Widerstand zunehmend als so schnell wie möglich zu eliminierende Bedrohung behandelt. Diese Entwicklung ist Teil einer breiteren autoritären und faschistischen Verschiebung, in welcher die Sprache und die Praxis der extremen Rechten die politische Agenda über verschiedene Grenzen hinweg prägt. Repression richtet sich gegen Demonstrationen, Selbstorganisation, Solidarität, Sabotage und jeden Versuch, die Legitimität der Machttragenden zu hinterfragen. Die reformistischen Grenzen dessen, was als „akzeptable Opposition“ erachtet wird werden ständig neu gezogen und die Widerständigen werden fortgehend als Kriminelle, Extremisten, Terroristen oder Mitglieder sogenannter krimineller Organisationen bezeichnet. Dies passiert oft bereits schon bevor die Öffentlichkeit erfährt was passiert ist, indem die politischen Motivationen, die hinter deren Aktionen stecken zensiert und unsichtbar gemacht werden.


Am 8. September 2026 wurde Daniel V. aufgrund mehrerer Sabotageakte in der Nähe eines Kohlekraftwerks bei Aachen verhaftet. Kurze Zeit nachdem seine Mutter in ihrem Zuhause von Journalisten interviewt wurde, wurde das Haus in dem sie mit Daniel lebt durchsucht. Außerdem gab es eine Razzia im Hambacher Forst und die dort lebenden Besetzer*innen wurden von der Bullenpräsenz und ihren Drohnen belästigt. Ein paar Tage zuvor hatte Daniel V. einen Brief an eine Zeitung gesendet, in welchem er die Verantwortung für mehrere Aktionen in unterschiedlichen Bundesländern übernommen hat, darunter Nordrhein-Westfalen und Brandenburg. Die Aktionen zu denen sich Daniel bekannte sorgten für Kurzschlüsse und vorübergehende Stromausfälle. Dafür feuerte er selbsterfundene und -gebaute Raketen in Hochspannungsleitungen. In diesem Text streben wir nicht an, die von Daniel verwendeten Taktiken zu analysieren, sondern stattdessen den Fokus auf die Art der darauf folgenden Repressionen zu legen und sie in den breiteren Kontext des Terrors zu stellen, der vom rechten Regime ausgeht.


Kurz nach dem 1. September wurde eine großangelegte Fahndung losgetreten – wieder einmal begleitet von den Taktiken des sozialen Kannibalismus, welcher die Menschen dazu anregen soll sich gegenseitig ans Messer zu liefern, um eine Belohnung zu erhalten, während die Medien mit ihrer Performance weiter machten. Daniel hat sich dazu entschlossen, sein Statement (hier die erste Seite seines Briefs: https://kontrapolis.info/18718/) an die Zeitung TAZ [2] zu senden. Anstatt Daniels eigene Worte zu veröffentlichen, entschied sich die TAZ einen eigenen Artikel über ihn zu schreiben und somit zu dem breiteren journalistischen Narrativ beizutragen, welches ihn als Psycho oder Terroristen porträtiert. Eine Zeitung, die Stolz darauf war den Tisch [3] der Kommune 1 [4] im Hinterhof zu haben und zu behaupten Teil einer linken Bewegung zu sein.


Dieses Narrativ ist Teil einer generelleren Tendenz der Medien, Menschen als psychologisch instabil, irrational oder gefährlich darzustellen, anstatt die wahren Gesichter des Widerstands und die Niederlagen des Staates und die Unfähigkeit sich selbst zu verteidigen anzuerkennen. Durch den Entschluss der Nicht-Veröffentlichung von Daniels Statement, hat die TAZ mal wieder gezeigt, dass die etablierten und kommerziellen Medien nicht als Teil irgendeiner Bewegung von unten angesehen werden können und dies …

author: winter oak
title: Feted or forgotten? A tale of two very different anarchists
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


An important split took place in the French anarchist movement at the very end of the nineteenth century.


This revolved around the question of whether the conviction of Jewish army captain Alfred Dreyfus for treason represented an important question of injustice and institutional anti-semitism or whether,

au contraire

, the case was irrelevant to the anarchist struggle.


François Jarrige writes in the

latest issue

 of

Brasero: revue de contre-histoire

: “The Dreyfus affair, which tore France apart from 1897-1898 onwards, also divided the anarchist milieu”. [1]


In what he terms “an extreme polarisation”, anarchists, “traditionally distrustful of the army and the state, split into convinced

dreyfusards

 and supporters of a strict indifference to what they considered an internal conflict within bourgeois institutions.


“Sébastien Faure, a major figure in the anarchist movement and co-founder of

Le Libertaire

, nevertheless managed to drag a number of activists into the active defence of Dreyfus”. [2]


We’ll come back to Faure later, but first I want to relate what Jarrige has to say about one of the anarchists who refused to climb on board the

dreyfusard

 bandwagon –

Emile Gravelle (1855-1920)

.


He was the founder of a current in the French anarchist movement called

naturien

 – there is no real English equivalent but the meaning is nature-loving or nature-based.


This, Jarrige explains, emerged in the Parisian

quartier

 of Montmartre and was a current that was “critical of industrial society and its goods, idealising prehistorical and primitive living and calling for a return to nature”. [3]


Gravelle, an anarchist painter, illustrator, pamphleteer and activist, was one of the first to formulate such a critique of “progress” and “civilisation”, prefiguring the green anarchism that emerged towards the end of the twentieth century. [4]


An important influence on Gravelle’s understanding of the world was his five-year stay in Buenos Aires, after leaving his home town of Douai in northern France at the age of 30.


Jarrige writes: “At the time Argentina was going through a phase of expansion: political stabilisation after civil wars, the conquest of indigenous lands, the expansion of cattle-rearing on the great plains of the

pampa

 and a massive influx of European immigrants. This context of brutal modernisation, mixing prosperity and social violence, had a deep impact on Gravelle…


“When he returned to France in 1890 he brought out a pamphlet in which he related his unpleasant experience. In this virulent text,

La République argentine dénoncée

 (‘The Argentine Republic denounced’), he describes how he had been taken in by the embroidered tales of a ‘shipping agent in the

rue de Dunkerque

‘, only to discover a reality of misery, exploitation and disillusionment.


“He writes about the diseases, the violence of the

gauchos

, the insalubrity of the towns and the suffering of immigrants pushed into suicide or madness. This pamphlet, laced with bitterness, also bears witness to a political realization: Gravelle denounces the illusions of progress and the mechanisms of capitalist exploitation”. [5]


Gravelle’s years in South America shaped his understanding of modernity in another way. Through his encounters with indigenous Guarani people he discovered “man, in the midst of nature, happy as a god in the triumphant splendour of its strength and beauty”. [6]


Jarrige says this provided him with “an alternative model to the European ways of living shaped by industry, the growing consumerism and imperialism”. [7]


It fed his rejection of modern urbanisation and his aspiration to a way of life founded on simplicity, autonomy and closeness to nature – “when Gravelle returned to Paris, he was thus no longer simply an illustrator looking for work: he was the bearer of a vision of the world opposed to that of the European civilisation of his age”. [8]


In the early 1890s Gravelle set up home in Montmartre, a bohemian, artistic and anarchic enclave on a hill in Paris. At the time, it was still semi-rural and was imbibed with the spirit of resistance to the new urban order, inherited from the Paris Commune of 1871.


Says Jarrige: “This landscape in transition, where the industrial smoke of the capital mixed with the last remains of rurality, deeply nourished Gravelle’s anarchist imagination”. [9]

title: Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου 2026 – Τελική ανακοίνωση: «Για να ζήσουμε όλ@ και κανείς να μην κυβερνά»
content:
Τελική ανακοίνωση


του Βαλκανικού Αναρχικού Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου 2026


Πηγή

: https://bab2026.espivblogs.net/2026/11/17/final-statement-of-the-balkan-anarchist-bookfair-2026/


Mετάφραση

: clandestina


Δεκαπέντε χρόνια μετά την πρώτη του επίσκεψη στα Σκόπια, το Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου επέστρεψε στην πόλη για τη 18η διοργάνωσή του. Από τις 24 ως τις 27 Σεπτέμβρη 2026, εκατοντάδες σύντροφισσες-οι, συλλογικότητες, εκδότ(ρι)ες και πρωτοβουλίες τόσο από την περιοχή των Βαλκανίων όσο και από ευρύτερες γεωγραφίες συγκεντρωθήκαμε για να μοιραστούμε και να διαδώσουμε πολιτικές προσεγγίσεις και γνώση μεταξύ των κινημάτων, για να (ξανά)ονειρευτούμε το μέλλον.


Μιλώντας με αριθμούς, στο BAB 2026 (που φιλοξενήθηκε στη Σχολή Καλών Τεχνών)  συμμετείχαν πάνω από 80 εκδοτικά εγχειρήματα, συλλογικότητες, πρωτοβουλίες και καλλιτεχνικά σχήματα· πραγματοποιήθηκαν περίπου 40 συζητήσεις, παρουσιάσεις, εργαστήρια και προβολές και τρεις βραδιές συναυλιών σε αυτοδιαχειριζόμενους και ανεξάρτητους χώρους σε ολόκληρη την πόλη (Κοινωνικό Κέντρο Dunja, La Kaña, Dze).


Η Αναρχική Συλλογικότητα Smokva ανέλαβε να διοργανώσει το φετινό BAB. Ωστόσο, αυτό δεν θα ήταν δυνατό χωρίς τη συμβολή των πολλών συμμετεχόντων/ουσών που ανέλαβαν την ευθύνη να φροντίσουν ώστε ο χώρος να λειτουργήσει με τρόπο που ξεπέρασε τις προσδοκίες μας.


Η εμπειρία της διοργάνωσης του φετινού BAB στα Σκόπια ήταν καθοριστική για τη συλλογικότητά μας, καθώς μας έδωσε τη δυνατότητα να διαδώσουμε σε τοπικό επίπεδο τις αναρχικές ιδέες της επαναστατικής πολιτικής, καθώς και τις αρχές της αλληλεγγύης, της αλληλοβοήθειας και της αντιεξουσίας. Ήδη βλέπουμε ανθρώπους γύρω μας, ιδίως νέους, να θέτουν ερωτήματα για την κοινωνία μας και τους καταπιεστικούς και κατασταλτικούς μηχανισμούς της, μέσα από μια πιο αναρχική οπτική. Με τη βοήθεια του BAB και της απίστευτης συγκέντρωσης διεθνιστικών αναρχικών προοπτικών που το συνοδεύουν, ιδέες που παρέμεναν στο περιθώριο αυτής της πόλης είχαν την ευκαιρία να έρθουν στο προσκήνιο. Τις εβδομάδες που ακολούθησαν το φέστιβάλ βιβλίου, ζήσαμε ήδη την ανάπτυξη ενός πνεύματος αυτοοργάνωσης· νέες ιδέες για πρωτοβουλίες και καμπάνιες σχετικές με ζητήματα που αφορούν τους κατοίκους των Σκοπίων εμφανίζονται διαρκώς. Για εμάς, στα Σκόπια, αυτή είναι μία από τις σημαντικότερες παρακαταθήκες αυτής της συνάντησης. Η ανασυγκρότησή μας μετά το φεστιβάλ βιβλίου ήταν μια δύσκολη προσπάθεια, αλλά το καλύτερο αποτέλεσμα του φεστιβάλ, το οποίο εξακολουθεί να συγκεντρώνει τις προσπάθειές μας, είναι οι συνθήκες που δημιουργήθηκαν ως αποτέλεσμα αυτής της συνάντησης, συνθήκες από τις οποίες μπορούν να αναδυθούν νέες μορφές οργάνωσης και αγώνα.


Όσον αφορά το πρόγραμμα, στο φετινό BAB η οργανωτική συνέλευση ανέλαβε την πρόκληση να πειραματιστεί με τη δομή του. Αντί να δομήσουμε το πρόγραμμα ως μια συλλογή προτάσεων για ξεχωριστές παρουσιάσεις από διαφορετικές πρωτοβουλίες, δουλέψαμε πάνω σε ένα σύνολο κοινών πολιτικών θεματικών που ανακοινώθηκαν και στα οποία οι συμμετέχοντες/ουσες κλήθηκαν να φέρουν τις εμπειρίες, τις ιδέες και τις αναλύσεις τους. Σκοπός μας ήταν να δημιουργήσουμε περισσότερο χώρο για συζήτηση μεταξύ των συμμετεχόντων-ουσών, ώστε να συνδεθούν εμπειρίες που συχνά παραμένουν απομονωμένες λόγω γεωγραφικών αποστάσεων και διαφορετικών γλωσσών. Η ίδια η μορφή στόχευε να διερευνήσει μια πιο συλλογική και διαλογική προσέγγιση. Μια προσέγγιση που επικεντρώνεται λιγότερο στην παρουσίαση συγκεκριμένων απόψεων ατόμων και συλλογικοτήτων και περισσότερο στη σύνθεση της κοινής μας, αν και σε σημεία διαφοροποιούμενης, οπτικής. Με άλλα λόγια, η ελπίδα μας ήταν να εργαστούμε προς συλλογικές βαλκανικές αναρχικές πολιτικές αναλύσεις και οράματα.


Πιστεύουμε ότι τα οφέλη μιας τέτοιας προσέγγισης αποδείχθηκαν αποτελεσματικά στην πράξη. Σε πολλές συναντήσεις, καταφέραμε να ξεπεράσουμε την απλή επανάληψη μεταξύ μας αυτών που ήδη γνωρίζουμε: ότι το κράτος, ο καπιταλισμός, ο μιλιταρισμός και η πατριαρχία παράγουν κυριαρχία, εκμετάλλευση και βία. Καταφέραμε να θέσουμε πιο δύσκολες ερωτήσεις. Πώς μεταφράζεται ο αγώνας ενάντια σε αυτές τις συνθήκες σε πράξεις; Πού οι μορφές οργάνωσής μας πετυχαίνουν και πού αποτυγχάνουν; Πώς οικοδομούμε αλληλεγγύη που είναι ουσιαστική και όχι δηλωτική προθέσεων; Πώς διατηρούμε αυτόνομους χώρους, δομές αμοιβαίας φροντίδας και αντίστασης; Πώς μπορούμε να χτίσουμε κοινή στρατηγική;


Aυτές είναι οι ερωτήσεις που συνέδεσαν ένα ευρύ φάσμα εκδηλώσεων, που αφορούσαν τον εξορυκτισμό και την οικολογική καταστροφή, την επιτήρηση και την …

author: anarchozoe
title: How Marxism Influenced Anarchism - Zoe Baker
content:
Essay detailing how Marxist social theory influenced the anarchist movement.

During the latter half of the 19th century anarchism and Marxism emerged as social movements in parallel and opposition to one another. Marxists and anarchists (anarchist communists and anarchist collectivists) agreed on the broad end goal of a stateless, classless, moneyless society, in which the means of production and land were owned in common and production and distribution were organised, co-ordinated, and planned through the free and equal association of the producers (Baker 2023, 79-93; Baker 2025). The principal disagreement between anarchism and Marxism was about how to achieve this broad end goal. Marxists generally believed that the working class must conquer state power, establish a workers’ state, and use it to overthrow the capitalist class. Once the revolution had been successful and a classless society achieved, the state would wither away (MECW 24, 320-21; MECW 26, 272; Lenin 1968, 265-335). Anarchists, in contrast, generally thought that workers should simultaneously abolish capitalism and the state and establish their own independent organs of self-management – workplace and community associations – and armed self-defence – workers’ militias. After the revolution, workers would lay down their arms and transition to living under full communism or collectivism (Baker 2023, 99-107, 154-61). This interpretation of the core dividing line between Marxism and anarchism was acknowledged by authors at the time, such as the anarchists Michael Bakunin (Bakunin 1990, 179), Peter Kropotkin (Kropotkin 2018, 211), Errico Malatesta (Malatesta 2015, 137-38), and Luigi Fabbri (Fabbri 2017, 19-20).

Anarchism and Marxism of course agreed and disagreed on other points beyond this. A few brief examples are as follows. Both Bakunin and Marx: embraced materialism and conceptualised reality in terms of processes and relations between parts that make up an interconnected whole (Marx 1990, 93, 102-3; Marx 1993, 99-100; Bakunin 1964, 53–68); broke the broad sweep of human history down into a series of economic periods characterised by specific kinds of technology, ways of organising production, and class divisions (Marx and Engels 1996, 1-9; Marx 1996, 159-60; Bakunin 1985, 174, 188-91); and argued that humans are social animals who can only be free in and through social relations (MECW 5, 78; Bakunin 1985, 46-8). Even on the contentious topic of strategy, they both endorsed the achievement of universal human emancipation through the self-emancipation of the working classes and viewed class struggle by workers as the driving force of revolutionary social change under capitalism (Marx 1990, 449, 929-30; Marx 1992, 256-7; MECW 20, 14, 148-49; MECW 24, 340; Bakunin 1985, 97-110).1

The points of disagreement between anarchism and Marxism were similarly diverse. Marxists generally advocated the formation of political parties that engaged in electoral politics, while anarchists rejected this and only endorsed direct action outside of and against the state (Baker 2023, 130-35, 143-53; MECW 24, 340; Taber 2021, 39-40, 51-2). Marxists, in turn, critiqued those anarchists who believed that assassinations and bombings were an effective means to spread anarchist ideas and build towards or trigger a mass working class uprising (MECW 50, 254-55, 272, 287; Plekhanov 1912, 135-42). Yet several debates between anarchism and Marxism also occurred within these social movements themselves such that these differences do not map onto a simple anarchism versus Marxism dichotomy. This can be seen in the two examples I just gave. Firstly, in the 1920s Marxists who were council communists rejected electoral politics and participation in bourgeois parliaments because it was inappropriate to the era of proletarian revolution. They were then critiqued by other Marxists like Lenin for adopting this position (KAPD 1920; Lenin 1968, 539-47). Secondly, Malatesta and Kropotkin critiqued other anarchists who advocated the strategy of assassinations and bombings on the grounds that it would not lead to fundamental social change and was actively harmful when it killed or wounded innocent civilians (Malatesta 2014, 187–91; Malatesta 2015 53-8; Malatesta 2016, 58, 125-27, 263-65; Miller 1976, 206-7).

It is furthermore the case that individuals in both camps misrepresented each other’s ideas and made ridiculous accusations that have no basis in reality.2 For example, in 1914 the …
