title: Reuben Rose-Redwood, Wil Sahar Patrick - Why activists are vandalizing statues to colonialism
content:
Author

: Reuben Rose-Redwood, Wil Sahar Patrick

Title

: Why activists are vandalizing statues to colonialism

Date

: March 17 2020

Source

: Retrieved on November 14 2026 from https://theconversation.com/why-activists-are-vandalizing-statues-to-colonialism-129750


 In 2018, statues of

Edward Cornwallis

 and

John A. Macdonald

 were removed from their respective pedestals in Halifax and Victoria. Across Canada, colonial statues

have also been vandalized

 as an act of protest.


 Statues and monuments have become major

flashpoints

 of political conflict over the past decade.


 After the 2015

Charleston Massacre

, in which a neo-Confederate white supremacist murdered nine African Americans at the Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church in Charleston, South Carolina, a movement to remove

Confederate monuments and place names

 swept across the United States.


 Another wave of Confederate statue removals and place renamings occurred in the

aftermath

 of the Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville, Virginia in 2017.


 In South Africa, the

#RhodesMustFall movement

 led to the removal of a statue honoring the British imperialist Cecil Rhodes at the University of Cape Town in 2015. This inspired efforts to challenge Rhodes’s legacy

elsewhere

 as well.


A crowd looks on as the statue of imperialist Cecil Rhodes is removed from its perch at the University of Cape Town in 2015. Schalk van Zuydam


 Monument controversies are not unique to the 21st century.

Commemorative landscapes

 have been radically transformed during political regime changes throughout history. Following the Second World War, monuments to the Nazi regime

were toppled

. Similarly, the

fall of the Soviet Union

 and the

end of apartheid in South Africa

 led to significant changes to the memorial landscape.


The Legacies of Settler Colonialism


Settler colonialism

 is a process of colonization based upon the replacement of Indigenous or colonized peoples with a settler society. This involves both the disposession of Indigenous land and the erasure, either through assimilation or elimination, of Indigenous peoples.


 Colonial statues and place names are part of the political infrastructure of settler place-making in Canada. As a result, they have become focal points for challenging settler-colonial power and testing the limits of reconciliation.


 On Jan. 31, 2018, the Cornwallis statue was taken down from its pedestal in Halifax. As an honorific commemoration for the “founder” of Halifax, Mi'kmaw elders

have long viewed

 the statue as a sign of the ongoing dispossession of Indigenous peoples and called for its removal.


 As if answering the East Coast, the John A. Macdonald statue was removed from the entrance to City Hall in Victoria on Aug. 11, 2018. The decision to remove the Macdonald statue was made as part of the city’s

formal reconciliation process

 with the Songhees and Esquimalt First Nations.


 As Canada’s first prime minister, Macdonald was chief architect of its residential school system and promoted genocidal policies against Indigenous peoples. His monumental presence at the entrance to City Hall was a major barrier to reconciliation efforts.


 In August 2018, a second plaque was installed to replace a bronze statue of Canada’s first Prime Minister John A. Macdonald after the first was vandalized shortly after the removal of the statue from the front of City Hall in Victoria, BC. Chad Hipolito/THE CANADIAN PRESS


 A year later, the city of New Westminster followed suit, removing a statue of the

“Hanging Judge” Matthew Begbie

 from the grounds of the provincial courthouse.


 Those opposed to the removal of statues often propose adding historic plaques as a way to recontextualize statues while leaving them in public spaces. Some activists, however, have chosen a different option: vandalism.


Vandalizing Colonial Statues and Monuments


 Across Canada, contentious statues and monuments linked to settler colonialism have been targeted with vandalism. In Montréal, the

John A. Macdonald and Queen Victoria monuments

 have been regularly spray-painted. Macdonald statues have been vandalized in

Kingston

 and

Regina

 as far back

as 2012

.


 Accompanying the campaign to remove the Cornwallis statue in Halifax were several

incidents

 of

vandalism

 as well.


 These are not random acts of hooliganism. The vandalism of colonial statues is an expression of political protest against the …

author: The Elephant
title: Alternative Leadership As A Decolonial Paradigm
content:
Sarova Stanley, Nairobi | 11 November 2026


Theme: Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency


Dr. Kawive Wambua;


The leadership and team of Inuka Kenya Ni Sisi!;

Representatives of civil society;

Distinguished guests;

Fellow Kenyans:


Good morning.


Thank you for inviting me to join you at the launch of the Inuka! Angaza Kura Campaign.


Your theme, “Reimagining Leadership, Reclaiming Citizen Agency,” brings us to the central question of our democracy: The Constitution proclaims Sovereignty of the people, but who truly exercises power in Kenya?


Is it the citizen whose taxes sustain the state, whose labour builds the economy, and whose vote confers authority? Or is it the officeholder who, once elected, hijacks power and behaves like the master, relegating citizens to subjects?


What must the citizens do to reclaim their agency, their power? 


You have asked me to reflect on “Alternative Leadership as a Decolonial Paradigm.”


The language may sound academic, but the issue is profoundly practical.


It concerns the relationship between a Kenyan citizen and the person entrusted to serve them. It concerns whether a police officer offers protection or inspires fear; whether a public office provides a service or demands a favour; whether public money builds opportunity or finances private privilege.


Above all, it concerns whether independence has become an everyday experience of dignity and quality services for us. 


From subjects to citizens


The colonial state was organised to control people and extract resources. Its authority flowed downwards. The population was expected to comply, while those who governed were insulated from meaningful accountability to the governed.


Independence was supposed to transform that relationship.


Yet changing the nationality of those occupying public office could not, by itself, dismantle the habits, incentives and institutions of domination, without changing the mindset of the office holders. Understanding leadership to be service and sacrifice, rather than entitlement and a life of privilege at the expense of basic needs for the people. Imagining leadership as an opportunity to ensure protection of the rights of the people and to uphold and affirm the dignity of the people you serve. Ensuring that, as a leader, you remain loyal to the purpose- service with openness and accountability. These are the minimum standards demanded by the constitution we gifted ourselves. 


Whenever leadership demands obedience without accountability, the colonial model or inheritance survives. Whenever citizens must seek political patronage to obtain public services, it survives. Whenever criticism is treated as disloyalty, it survives.


Decolonising leadership therefore requires us to confront the exercise of power in our own time.


We must ask whether the state serves citizens as people with rights, or manages them as subjects who should remain grateful for favours.


A hospital is a public responsibility. A road is a public investment. Education is an investment in the nation’s future. Every service by leaders is part of their duty to us, funded by our taxes, not a favour. 


None of these should become a personal gift for which citizens owe a politician their silence. Service should not be in exchange for citizens losing their freedom to exercise their right to demand accountability. Service must never be at the cost of citizens losing their agency, their power to oversee leaders, the government. 


An alternative must be radically different in word and deed. 


Comrades,


The word “alternative” carries an obligation.


Those of us who seek to offer alternative leadership must demonstrate how we would govern differently. We must affirm our allegiance to the Constitution, whose main objective is to restrain, or in other words, limit the exercise of power.  Alternative leadership must affirm citizens’ right to seek accountability and readiness to vacate office should citizens unequivocally so demand. The Alternative leadership must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and the people of Kenya, and affirm the sovereignty of the people. Demonstrate an understanding that leadership is a privilege to serve, not a title deed to rule over the people. Our utterances and actions as alternative leadership must so demonstrate. 


It is insufficient to condemn arrogance in government while practising it within our political parties. We cannot promise inclusion while silencing young …

title: La derrota del trumpismo: ¿un canto de cisne o un cisne negro?
content:
LA DERROTA DEL TRUMPISMO: ¿UN

CANTO DE CISNE

 O UN

CISNE NEGRO

?


Por Rafael Bautista S.


Mientras el futuro más temible llegue,


lo único que nos devuelva la luz será


esta velita prendida que supimos


cuidar en plena oscuridad.


Ya con la cabeza fría, conviene profundizar analítica y prospectivamente lo que se ha de jugar en estos casi dos meses de transición hacia las más temibles opciones que se pondrán en movimiento, una vez que el Estado profundo ha decidido prescindir del episodio Trump. Por cuestiones de sobrevivencia discordante –como ya señalamos– entre dos opciones supremacistas de restauración del liderazgo imperial

[1]

, la derrota de Trump no limpia el panorama sino lo enrarece aún más.


Todos saben que los demócratas son rusóbos, para empezar, y eso no augura un cese de la amenaza nuclear sino la radicaliza, como ya se está observando en los últimos movimientos beligerantes de la OTAN, Inglaterra y Alemania

[2]

 contra Rusia. El AIPAC, por cuestiones ya de sobrevivencia del Estado sionista, más aún cuando perdió Netanyahu, hará uso de su fuerte influencia entre los demócratas

[3]

 para continuar la política nuclear contra Irán y el exterminio de los gazatíes y los palestinos en general (Líbano, Siria y Cisjordania). Lo cual, además de la prolongación del genocidio palestino, no hace sino continuar, por otros medios, la política expansiva (aunque cada vez menos posible, como la inutilidad de los bombardeos recientes de parte de USA e Israel a Irán) del Estado sionista.


Tampoco los inmigrantes verán otro panorama más alentador con los demócratas, cuando fue la administración “demócrata” de Obama, por ejemplo, la que más cantidad de deportados produjo. De boca para afuera, los demócratas harán de Trump el chivo expiatorio que necesita la restauración imperial para justificar su continuidad. Creyendo que la limpieza de la imagen imperial podrá ofrecerle demagógicamente al mundo, otra cosa que no sea una nueva versión de la continuidad de “un mundo basado en reglas” para los demás y excepciones para el Imperio.


En ese contexto, pondremos a consideración el panorama que sugiere Alexander Dugin y nuestro comentario a lo que creemos, una de las descripciones más cercanas a lo que se viene. En sus propias palabras

[4]

, si Trump pierde irremediablemente el control del Congreso: “la venganza de los demócratas contra Trump y sus seguidores

no se parecerá a nada de lo que hemos visto antes

”. Los demócratas no pasarán por alto, lo que significó el desmantelamiento de los brazos administrativos y operativos de su poder de influencia nacional y global, cuando se creó la Oficina de Eficiencia Gubernamental, el DOGE, y se inició la desarticulación de la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional, la USAID (desde donde se operó la restauración derechista –una vez desarticulada por la “primavera democrática”– en Latinoamérica, en favor de la tutela demócrata gringa). Esa era una de las vías que permitió la injerencia de los intereses que representa, por ejemplo, George Soros. Por eso, no es casual la sincronía de la ola de protestas en Europa

[5]

 y el triunfo demócrata en USA. Hasta el triunfo de Lula se explicaría, en parte, por esa caída de las piezas de dominó que sostenía al trumpismo, a nivel global (rival en la jefatura de un nuevo orden mundial que destaca otro tipo de intereses, sobre todo financieros, que tienen en Soros un actor reconocible).


Dugin, en tono de socarrón señala: “realmente creyeron que Trump cumpliría sus promesas y que el Estado profundo estaba a punto de ser erradicado de raíz”. Pero Trump, que nunca generó el contexto para la realización del golpe definitivo, ahora tiene, en el Congreso (tanto en diputados como en senadores, además de gobernadores), la mayoría necesaria para que el globalismo, que intentó atacar, reorganice filas con sus portavoces y comiencen el contraataque.


Ya algunos analistas en geopolítica preguntan si quien ganó en las “midterm” fue, en realidad, Soros. Pero éste es sólo el actor expuesto y si algo manifiesta el

poder duro

 es la no exposición. Éste

poder duro

 (o Estado profundo) actúa creando la objetividad que se constituye en escenario, una vez que ya ha mudado a otro tipo de realidad, teniendo a todos ocupados en el escenario conveniente que el poder produce para desplegar mediáticamente conspiraciones para el disfrute masoquista del morbo político. Con esos fines se viene activando la alerta, en 33 países …

title: Peter Gelderloos: Breathing Room
content:
Woodcut by Frans Masereel


from Peter Gelderloos’ substack page,

Suviving Leviathan

, 05/11/2026


Breathing Room


from the apocalyptic, fascistic Right to the insufficient, hypocritical, quietly genocidal Left


In the recent elections in Brasil, one of the largest countries in the Global South, leftwing darling Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro, the fascistic dynast supported by the country’s plantation owner class. In Israel, the extreme Right lost the elections to the far Right (not a typo). And in the US, a “blue wave” has given the Democrats an ample margin of control in both chambers of Congress as well as a strong majority of governorships (for non-US readers, for whatever weird-ass reason related to our especially amnesiac, isolationist culture, in the US blue is the color of the Left and red is the color of the Right). In once Republican-held or toss-up states like Texas, North Carolina, and New Jersey, Democratic candidates won by double digits while conservatives won in what were, until yesterday, solidly Republican states like Florida or Louisiana by only 1 or 2%.


A high level Republican operative connected to Trump admitted to the press that these elections were just “too big to rig,” casually acknowledging how common it is to redraw electoral maps or send the precise vote-counting machines to the friendly districts and low quality, high-failure-rate machines to the unfriendly districts, in order to win an extra percentage point and tip elections.


Brasil


In Brasil, where former far Right president Jair Bolsonaro serves a sentence of house arrest in his mansion for launching a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 elections, his son Flavio Bolsonaro carried the first round of the elections in early October but failed to attain a majority. In the second round, held October 25

th

, voters turned to the Left and re-elected the incumbent, Lula, off the Workers’ Party. Wealthy investors punished the country for their vote, with the Brasilian stock market taking a plunge after the election even though Lula is a very business-friendly politician who has overseen a large deal of growth and “development” in the Brasilian economy. In practice that means he promotes oil drilling and mining in the Amazon, he subsidizes the intertwined beef-soy industry causing so much destruction in the south and west of the country, and he also supports manufacture and higher tech industry.


Brasil’s stock market index, with the big crash on the right-hand side occurring on October 25.


If Bolsonaro’s son Flavio had won this past 25

th

 of October, the death squads that work for the ranchers, soy plantation owners, miners, loggers, or directly for the state, would have had free rein. Several of my friends and many of the

Indigenous

,

African diasporic

, and lower class mestizo or white people

I met last year

, people at the forefront of

rural

 and

urban struggles

 against the ongoing violence of colonial capitalism and

for a better world

, would have been at greater risk of getting murdered for their resistance. For sure, a lot of people are breathing a very valid sigh of relief. But they’re not naïve about the meaning of the leftwing victory.


[Some of those links above go to

Antimidia

 videos in Portuguese. Before pressing play, scroll down to “Legendas” and you’ll see buttons for English subtitles.]


As one friend put it, “

If Bolsonaro wins, they kill us; if Lula wins, they let us die.

” A second friend referred to a “mono-polarization” in which there are not two competing poles, just a single pole, “the extreme Right, which pulls everything into its proximity.”


Another friend described the following:


“Bolsonarismo already won. I don’t say that just because the Congress and Senate are controlled by fascists, I’m referring to Lula’s campaign replicating the methods of communication that are very close to fascism (including the name “Lula’s Army”). A few days ago on TV, Lula openly defended lowering the age at which children can be tried as adults (in order to appease the Right) and other similar things. Every time there is a “vote against fascism” which includes the attempt to also convince the Right or “center right,” the pendulum moves to the right.

the 2013 revolt

, some people (like the author Paulo Arantes) said that we were living in a situation with a horizon of diminishing expectations, without a view towards amplifying the struggles and the …

Given that we live in a society that promotes ignorance and superficiality, perhaps it shouldn’t be all that surprising that current day anarchist discussions of historic inter-anarchist debates usually miss the point when it comes to colonialism (and imperialism more generally.)

Anarchists do not somehow become immune to colonial society’s influence simply by making abstract and hollow declarations of opinion. Knowledge and comprehension require actual commitment and curiosity, and these are sadly rare qualities among the European, Euro-American and Euro-Canadian anarchists of today.

This article is an attempt at a brief analysis of what’s been missing in recent anarchist discussions of three historic inter-anarchist debates. The term “debates” is used here in the widest sense of a general disagreement rather than some formally-held event or correspondence. Specifically, I refer to the debates between Luigi Galleani and Ricardo Flores Magón over the Mexican Revolution, between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta on the First World War, and between Emma Goldman and Reginald Reynolds on Palestine.

In the case of Reynolds, we should note that he considered himself a fellow traveler and sympathizer of anarchism, wrote regularly for the anarchist periodicals edited by Vernon Richards, and married the socialist-turned-anarchist Ethel Mannin, but did not self-identify as an anarchist, so my phrase “inter-anarchist debate” must also be understood in the broadest sense.

The anarchist periodical Tinderbox and the anarchist website The Transmetropolitan Review (TTR) have recently invoked the Galleani-Magón debate, though without even being aware of it in the former case.

The individual who writes articles at the TTR website claimed in May of this year that the historic anarchist Partido Liberal Mexicano (PLM) made a “fateful alliance with Pascual Orozco,” the latter being a bourgeois revolutionary who, with the help of Pancho Villa, took control of Ciudad Juárez in 1911. The author makes no distinction between the on-the-ground forces of the PLM and the Junta (leadership board) of that organization, which, from Los Angeles obviously could not directly control the actions of every individual on the frontlines in Mexico, even if they had wanted to.

TTR goes on to sell the lie that at the time, “the PLM was willing to work with anyone against Madero, and they took positions in Orozco’s rebel government alongside oligarchs and hacienda owners, something which further isolated the PLM from anarchists.”

In reality, Magón and the rest of the Junta, in their periodical, Regeneración, called for violent resistance to Orozco once he took control of Juárez, denouncing him as bourgeois and openly accusing him of being on the wrong side of the revolution, specifically because he was trying to disarm other revolutionaries and was friendly with the rich.

To be clear where TTR wasn’t, the anarchists they claim the PLM isolated …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Bogus patriotism for Pax Silica
content:
The way the Philippine government and its servitors have framed the Pax Silica Initiative makes it appear that the $70-billion to be poured into the manufacturing hubs at the 1,620-hectare New Clark City would boost the Philippine economy, create between 130,000 and 190,000 direct jobs and up to 900,000 indirect jobs and save the country from stagnation. They appear to be saddled with what the Spaniards call “estar en Bebia,” or living in dreamland, much like the way Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio resides in her Utopia, which is actually nowhere land.


They are like Ramon Ang, Manny Villar and Ricky Razon, businessmen who thrive on hype, government subsidies, tax breaks, tariff barriers and favorable policies, all of whom have proven to be long on promise but short on achievements. First, despite the pious incantations of rah-rah boys, Pax Silica is what the Americans regard as work in progress.

Kumbaga sa atin, sinesementuhan pa lang, wala pang palitada at di malaman kung kailan mag-uumpisa.

 The US State Department conceived it in December 2025, meaning it will celebrate its birthday next month, and the Philippines jumped into the US chicharon in April 2026, barely four months after the initiative, which is as opaque as other Donald Trump policies, was written by Marco Rubio.


Now, Filipinos are being faulted for opposing Pax Silica and refusing to accept what has been dubbed as the country’s economic redemption.

Hindi pa napipisa ang itlog, nagbibilang na sila ng kiti.

 One even went to the extent of describing the bashing of the heads of protesters, the illegal suppression of mass actions against the Trump initiative, the prevention of thousands of participants from Los Banos, Southern Luzon, Central Luzon, Katipunan Ave. and Liwasang Bonifacio from attending the rallies, the arrest of protesters in Bonifacio Global City and the manhandling University of Makati students opposed to the initiative as mere “performative martyrdom,” whatever it means, thus blaming the victims and not the police and military agents who violated political and civil rights.


Fil-American Bea Millan-Windorski, the country’s Miss Universe bet competing in Puerto Rico, took a firm a stand against the suppression of protesters saying it is “an infringement on the right to free speech and freedom to assemble.” She added: “NO TO IMPERYALISMO, NO TO PAX SILICA.” Windorski studied at the University of Wisconsin and specialized in Philippines history and the oppression, exploitation by US imperialism. She highlighted the plight of marginalized sectors and “the environmental impacts of open pit mining and gold extraction in areas like Northern Luzon and Masbate” and warned against the negative impact of transnational deals like the Memorandum of Understanding on Critical Minerals Supply Chains.”


Windorski lamented the low wages of Filipino workers and the suppression of labor unions, in effect belying the mantra of Ayn Rand, who insisted that “capitalism has been the only system in history where wealth was not acquired by looting, but by production, not by force but by trade.” Moreover, the deployment of more than 40,000 policemen and thousands of soldiers to secure the site of the ASEAN Summit that cost the country P21-billion showed not only expensive overkill but also smarmy servility to the despised Donald Trump at the expense of the civil and political rights of the Filipino people. The Bill of Rights was suspended by the Philippine National Police (PNP), which found itself as the brownshirts dispensing with the law to make Trump feel good and appreciated in a country that he bludgeoned with higher tariffs.


What did Trump tell the Philippines as he ridiculed our journalists? There was no document to sign as it apparently wasn’t his priority. So, there goes the untethered narrative of Malacanang, special assistant Frederick Go and economic planners whose expertise is to belittle the chronic economic crisis and to offer solutions when they were out of their sinecures. In Shenzen, Trump bragged that the US would catch China in rare earths production “within 10 months.” This despite the fact that there is only one operating lithium mine in the US while the Trump administration invested in MP Minerals and other companies that have yet to produce rare earths. “We are making rare earths at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them within 10 months, they say,” he said.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Estados Unidos: Apostillas electorales
content:
Zohran Mamdani, alcalde de Nueva York, Estados Unidos


Por Mario Hernandez


El alcalde Mamdani disfrutó del triunfo de los cuatro candidatos a los que les dio su apoyo para el Congreso


Entre ellos estaban las integrantes del DSA (Socialistas Democráticos de América) Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier, el ex contralor Brad Lander y la gobernadora Kathy Hochul.


La victoria más contundente de la noche fue la de Chevalier, que se quedó con su distrito en el norte de Manhattan y el Bronx con el 87,5 % de los votos. Su rival, el republicano Jomo Williams, apenas arañó un 12 %. Semejante paliza electoral deja bien en claro que las propuestas de Chevalier, que incluyen impuestos a los ricos, salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE, entre otras demandas progresistas, calan profundo en gran parte de sus nuevos votantes. Su triunfo demuestra además que se puede hacer campaña definiéndose abiertamente como socialista, e incluso enfrentar a la policía en las calles, sin miedo a “espantar a los propios”. De hecho, el tono combativo de Darializa y su ya famoso cruce con la policía el día del tiroteo del ICE en el Bronx sin duda le sumaron un buen caudal de votos.


Chevalier cruzó duro al ICE y remarcó la importancia de la vivienda accesible, vistiendo una kufiyya como símbolo de apoyo a Palestina. De todos modos, sorprendió que su discurso hablara muy poco de política internacional: la única mención a Palestina se dio cuando la tribuna empezó a cantar de forma espontánea “Palestina libre”.


Además de Chevalier, el DSA conquistó una segunda banca por el Distrito 7, donde Valdez, que también contaba con el respaldo de Mamdani, logró un triunfo cómodo con más del 83 % de los votos frente a su rival republicano. Valdez, referente del DSA, va a reemplazar a la congresista del establishment demócrata Nydia Velázquez, que se retira en enero. Al igual que Chevalier, Valdez hizo campaña con propuestas de salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE. Un dato clave: a diferencia de Mamdani, ni Valdez ni Chevalier le dieron su apoyo a la gobernadora Hochul ni dijeron que la iban a votar.


Con esto, el DSA pasa a tener tres bancas en el Congreso por Nueva York: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier. Si a eso se le suma el flamante congresista y ex miembro del DSA Brad Lander, a quien Mamdani también apoyó, el alcalde pasa a contar con una bancada importante que representa sus intereses y muchas de sus ideas en el Congreso.


Pero el festejo de Chevalier no fue la única parada de Mamdani esa noche. Antes de subir hacia el Bronx, apenas cerraron las urnas, el alcalde pasó la primera parte de la noche con la gobernadora Kathy Hochul y sus seguidores. En el discurso que dio ahí, Mamdani definió la elección como un “punto de quiebre” para el Partido Demócrata y afirmó que “empezamos el trabajo de transformar a nuestro partido para que vuelva a ser de los trabajadores”.


Su respaldo fue determinante para darle un vuelco a la campaña de Hochul. Hace menos de dos años, parecía que su carrera se había terminado. Todavía golpeada por la ajustada elección de 2022, donde los demócratas de Nueva York perdieron cinco bancas en el Congreso en parte por su incapacidad para movilizar al electorado propio, sus chances de ganar la interna y la reelección parecían bajísimas. Su imagen positiva rozaba apenas el 40 % (al nivel o por debajo de la del presidente Trump), y las encuestas mostraban que un mano a mano en 2026 contra un candidato republicano fuerte podía ser muy parejo.


Pero entonces entró en escena el alcalde Zohran Mamdani. Su meteórico ascenso al poder fue una ola que, al igual que la “ola azul” demócrata, empujó a cuanto candidato llevara la “D” de demócrata en la boleta, y su apoyo temprano y explícito a Hochul le devolvió el aire a la campaña de la gobernadora. Los resultados del martes demostraron la fuerza que tuvo ese espaldarazo. Hochul no solo logró la reelección, sino que aplastó por completo a su rival republicano Bruce Blakeman por más de 20 puntos.


Gran parte de este triunfo se explica por los mismos factores que impulsaron las victorias demócratas en el resto del país: el rechazo a Trump y al Partido Republicano, la bronca con las atrocidades del ICE y la guerra contra Irán, y la frustración por la inflación y el costo de vida. En realidad, el éxito de los demócratas a nivel nacional tuvo más que ver con el odio a Trump que con las propuestas reales de …

author: Arnold Padilla
title: What’s at stake in Trump’s Manila visit?
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump’s upcoming visit to Manila for the ASEAN Summit happens in the wake of intensifying struggle between the U.S. and China for economic, technological, political, and military dominance in Asia. Washington aims to consolidate its strategic position in Southeast Asia, with the Philippines under Ferdinand Marcos Jr. playing an increasingly important role in advancing U.S. imperialist interests.

Trump arrives politically battered. The sweeping Republican defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, which handed both houses of Congress to the Democrats, represents a powerful repudiation of his administration’s policies. Trump’s unpopular U.S. war against Iran and his aggressive tariff policies and their disastrous economic consequences, such as rising living costs, contributed to widespread dissatisfaction among American voters.

The defeat further exposes the political crisis confronting U.S. imperialism. It reflects growing domestic opposition to policies that impose enormous economic and social costs on the American people while sustaining Washington’s aggressive military interventions and global ambitions.

But Trump’s weakened domestic position does not mean that the White House will abandon its imperialist agenda abroad. On the contrary, the administration may seek to demonstrate U.S. power through new military, economic, and diplomatic agreements. Trump could use his visit to Manila to project strength and secure strategic commitments to counter the political setback at home.

The central objective of Washington’s ASEAN agenda is to preserve U.S. supremacy in the face of China’s expanding economic and military power. Southeast Asia occupies a crucial place in this rivalry. It sits astride strategic maritime routes and contains vital manufacturing centers, mineral resources, emerging digital markets, and production networks essential to the world economy.

For U.S. imperialism, maintaining influence over ASEAN means safeguarding its military reach while securing access to markets, technology infrastructure, critical minerals, and industrial supply chains. The U.S. seeks to organize these strategic assets around its own economic and national-security priorities, particularly by reducing dependence on Chinese-controlled production networks.

At the same time, China is expanding its own economic and strategic influence through trade, investment, infrastructure, and military power. This competition between rival great powers seeks to expand their influence over the region’s resources, markets, territory, and political decisions.

Washington’s military agenda was made explicit during the ASEAN defense ministers’ meetings in Cebu in October, when Pete Hegseth, Trump’s so-called Secretary of War, proposed a new framework for U.S.–ASEAN defense cooperation.

Under the language of maritime security and interoperability, Washington seeks to deepen military coordination, intelligence sharing, joint exercises, and naval cooperation with Southeast Asian governments. The proposal complements the expanding network of U.S. military alliances and access arrangements across the Indo-Pacific. It aims to strengthen its First Island Chain strategy to encircle and contain China. On the sidelines of the Cebu meeting, U.S. and Japanese defense officials discussed implementing a more effective denial-defense posture along this chain.

With its geographical location, the Philippines has become a crucial platform for this strategy. Under Marcos Jr., U.S. military access under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) has expanded from five to nine designated Philippine facilities. Washington and Manila are also increasing joint military exercises and deployments of advanced missile and unmanned systems. These arrangements strengthen the capacity of U.S. forces to operate in the South China Sea and potentially respond to a Taiwan Strait conflict.

So far, only two ASEAN countries have formal defense treaties with the U.S., namely the Philippines and Thailand. But all the other members, except for Myanmar, have various forms of extensive defense or military cooperation arrangements with the U.S. However, unlike its Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) and related pacts with the Philippines, not all agreements with other ASEAN countries grant U.S. troops access to military installations, allow combat deployments, or entail an obligation to support U.S. military operations.

Hegseth’s proposal aims to move beyond …

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:


It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!


What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.


This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.


Glorification


A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo


Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:


…,

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo


being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…


With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.


The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Our undeniable victories and Marcos Jr.’s perpetual shame
content:
By

Renato Reyes Jr.

 / President, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan


The Marcos Jr. regime is a certified US-puppet regime that will break laws, suppress the people, and sell out the Philippines to imperialist interests. Marcos Jr. “can’t keep the US president waiting” even if Trump made everyone wait because of his lateness to the ASEAN events. Yet for all his pining for his US master, Marcos Jr. failed to get the Pax Silica framework pact signed.


Pax Silica has generated broad resistance from the Filipino people in just seven months since the Philippine signing of the declaration. Our biggest victory is the high public awareness, the nationwide and international mass mobilizations, and the organizing work around the issues of imperialism, environment, indigenous rights, and genuine development.


The PNP and DILG are ignorant or simply do not care about laws and human rights and have demonstrated utter contempt for the people’s right to protest. The people, however, will not be denied, and no terror tactics can suppress an awakened people. The people will always find a way to make their voices heard. The nationwide protests amid police brutality affirm this.


The Marcos Jr. regime underestimated the public pushback on the Imeldific beautification of Metro Manila and the massive public spending on the preparations while poverty remains unresolved. The people saw no real benefits to Marcos Jr.’s vanity project, while Malacañang took pains to explain why spending P22 billion for the hosting is good for the people.


Marcos Jr., with his fascism and puppetry, has opened the eyes of a new generation of Filipinos in the same way that corruption and bureaucrat capitalism did last year at the height of the anti-corruption protests. There are moments when years become months and months become days, as a wave of protests spreads throughout the country. The days of disquiet of November taught the youth what kind of society they stand to inherit and why they should fight to change it.


Thus the challenge remains: we need to wage collective struggle to change the system dominated by imperialism, feudalism, and bureaucrat capitalism. We cannot expect real change from a puppet regime, from corrupt political dynasties, fascist police and military, and the big compradors and landlords. Our hope lies in the people—in the workers, farmers, indigenous peoples, youth and students, and all oppressed sectors fighting for national democracy. #

title: Tanju Özcan hakkında tahliye kararı: Başka dava kapsamında cezaevinde kalacak
content:

Bolu Belediyesine yönelik eylül ayında yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında, bazı çöp toplama araçlarının çalışmadığı günlerde çalışmış gibi gösterilerek yüklenici firmaya 34 milyon 288 bin 376 TL fazla ve yersiz ödeme yapıldığı iddiasıyla 21 kişi hakkında gözaltı kararı verildi. Operasyon kapsamında gözaltına alınan Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Gülden Özaydın, Temizlik İşleri Müdür Vekili Basri Baytekin, Temizlik İşleri Müdürlüğü Muayene ve Kabul Komisyonu Başkanı B.T. ile yüklenici firmanın yetkilisi Faruk Güner ve F.L. ile Y.E. tutuklandı. Başka dava kapsamında tutuklu olan Bolu Belediye Başkanlığı görevinden uzaklaştırılan Tanju Özcan bu soruşturma kapsamında da tutuklandı.

Bolu 3'üncü Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'nde 4'ü tutuklu 21 sanık hakkında 'Kamu kurum veya kuruluşlarının ihalesine fesat karıştırmak', 'Edimin ifasına fesat karıştırmak', 'Zimmet' ve 'Kamu görevlisinin resmi belgede sahteciliği' suçlarından açılan davanın duruşması dün başladı. Dün akşam ara verilen duruşma, bu sabah devam etti. Duruşmaya, tutuklu sanıklardan Tanju Özcan, Sincan Cezaevi'nden SEGBİS aracılığıyla katıldı. Diğer tutuklu sanıklar Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Gülden Özaydın, Bolu Belediyesi Temizlik İşleri Müdür Vekili Basri Baytekin, şirket yetkilisi Faruk Güner ile tutuksuz sanıklar ve avukatları salonda hazır bulundu.

Duruşmada savunmasını yapan Bolu Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Gülden Özaydın, 16 yıldır Bolu Belediyesinde kamu görevini yerine getirdiğini söyleyerek, “Karşınızda en ağır suçlarla buradayım. Bunlar benim için de arkadaşlarım için de acı bir suçlama ve bunu bize yaşatanları asla unutmayacağız. Bu suçlama bizim bütün hayatımızı karalıyor. Eve geldiklerinde öyle bir baskına maruz kaldık ki çoktan bizim için hükmümüzün verildiğini gördük. 81 gündür cezaevinde, evimden, ailemden uzaktayım. Yüklenici firmaya fazla para aktarmışız, iddia bu yönde. İddianın temeline baktığımızda kullanılmayan araç yok. Bilirkişinin yanlış yorumlanmasından kaynaklanan bir durum var. Şartnamenin birçok maddesinde arıza üzerine maddeler var. Bir aracın 7/24 çalışması mümkün değildir. Görev yeri değişikliği, çalışma saatleri nedeniyle mümkün değildir. Her yeni gelen şoföre eğitim vermemiz gerekiyor. İş sağlığı ve güvenliği içinde bilgilendirmek zorundayım. Temizlik İşleri Müdürlüğü çok fazla sirkülasyonun olduğu bir müdürlük. Kimse çöp toplamak istemez. Mevsim koşullarında da bu araçları 7/24 çalıştıramayız. Bilirkişi raporlarında birim fiyat teknik cetvelinden bahsedilmemektedir. Bu araçlar aylık olarak idarenin hizmetine sunulacak ve biz günde 5 vardiya çöp topluyoruz. Bu araçları tek vardiyaya da kullanabilirim 5 vardiyada da kullanabilirim. Bu yorumdan ceza sorumluluğu ile karşı karşıyayız. Başka kamu kurumlarının şartnameleri de bu şekilde yapılıyor” diye konuştu.

“Hiçbir menfaat yokken kimlerle parayı nasıl organize ettiğimiz belli değil. Uzun yıllardır belediyedeyim. Bu iş hep aylık olarak yapılırdı. Yüklenici firmaya haksız ödeme yapmak için kurgulamışız. Ben bundan haberdarmışım. Buna dayanak olarak gösterilen benim 2024 yılındaki olur verdiğim yazı. 2024 yılında biz meclis kararı ile birlikte bakanlıktan ihale için onay aldık. 32 araç için ihale yapıldı ve 2024 yılında ihale imzalandı. Olur verdiğim yazı ihaleyi ilgilendiren bir yazı değil. Hukuken ben üst yönetici değilim, üst yönetici hukuken belediye başkanıdır. Bir diğer konu da edimin ifasına fesat karıştırmak. Burada da benim var olduğuma ilişkin hiçbir şey yok. Burada hak edişin ödenmesi yönünde benim imzam ve yetkim yok bulunamaz zaten. Arkadaşlarımın yanlışlıkla hata yaptığını düşünüyorum. author: CMI Argentina
title: El Congreso aprobó los desalojos exprés en plena crisis habitacional y caída del empleo formal
content:
Mientras miles de familias se endeudan para pagar el alquiler, el Senado aprobó una ley que permite solicitar la restitución anticipada de inmuebles con juicios sumarísimos. Inquilinos Agrupados advirtió sobre sus consecuencias.


En plena crisis habitacional y caída del empleo formal, el Gobierno acelera la asfixia a los millones de argentinos que alquilan a partir de la habilitación de los desalojos exprés. Los cambios impulsados por el gobierno de Javier Milei con la flamante Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada permiten que el dueño de una vivienda, terreno o campo pida su desocupación inmediata por falta de pago o vencimiento del contrato, antes de que haya una sentencia firme.


Para esto, la nueva norma promovida por la Casa Rosada y sancionada este jueves por el Senado, introduce profundas reformas al Código Procesal Civil y Comercial de la Nación al modificar artículos clave como el 679, 680, 684 bis y 686 bis, entre otros. A partir de ahora, la ley establece que, antes de iniciar una demanda, el dueño debe intimar al ocupante y darle al menos diez días corridos de plazo. También permite que la orden judicial de desalojo autorice el uso de la fuerza pública, el allanamiento y la apertura de cerraduras.


Tras la votación, la organización Inquilinos Agrupados denunció públicamente la medida al sostener que habilita el “desalojo masivo sin juicio previo de inquilinos urbanos y comunidades rurales”, al tiempo que compartió una foto con los legisladores que respaldaron la medida.


Estos son los senadores que acaban de votar el desalojo masivo sin juicio previo de inquilinos urbanos y comunidades rurales. https://t.co/7PKD6aYEJG


— Inquilinos Agrupados (@InquilinosAgrup)

November 20, 2026


El impacto de la crisis económica y los indicadores habitacionales


La aprobación de este régimen de desocupación rápida se produce en un escenario socioeconómico marcado por el deterioro del poder adquisitivo y el incremento de la precariedad en el acceso a la vivienda. De acuerdo con la Encuesta Nacional Inquilina realizada en junio de 2026, el 29,7% de los hogares inquilinos se encuentra en situación de emergencia habitacional, al acumular en forma simultánea sobrecarga del costo del alquiler, deudas y riesgo de mudanza.


El relevamiento señala que el 48,5% de las familias locatarias destina la mitad o más de sus ingresos salariales al pago del alquiler, situación que derivó en que un 20% debiera afrontar mudanzas forzosas por imposibilidad financiera. El sobreesfuerzo económico impactó severamente en los niveles de endeudamiento:


El 72,9% de los hogares inquilinos tiene deudas activas.


El 55,3% de esos hogares se endeudó para comprar alimentos.


El 47,4% de los encuestados recurre a más de un empleo para poder pagar el alquiler.


Por su parte, los datos oficiales del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) correspondientes al primer semestre de 2026 muestran la enorme porción de la población a la que afecta esta medida, ya que reflejan que, sobre un universo de 31 aglomerados urbanos, el 20,9% de los hogares revista en condición de inquilino o arrendatario, lo que representa a 2.144.000 hogares y 5.522.000 personas.


La desprotección de este grupo social converge con una pronunciada contracción de la actividad productiva y el empleo formal. Según un informe del centro de estudios Fundar, entre noviembre de 2023 y agosto de 2026 el país registró una pérdida neta de 32.429 empresas empleadoras, lo que equivale a una caída del 6,3% en el total de firmas. Se trata de la reducción porcentual más elevada para los primeros 33 meses de un mandato presidencial desde que existen registros comparables en 1996.


Patentes: aval del Senado y alerta por los medicamentos


Durante la misma sesión legislativa, el Senado aprobó por 47 votos a favor y 22 en contra la adhesión de la Argentina al Tratado de Cooperación en Materia de Patentes (PCT), norma solicitada por el gobierno de los Estados Unidos. En el debate, los legisladores del oficialismo argumentaron que la ratificación implica que “la Argentina abraza la previsibilidad jurídica” y promueve la economía del conocimiento, sectores de la oposición objetaron la medida.


Mientras que, por su parte, el senador del peronismo José Mayans sostuvo que “esto es un tratado de libre comercio donde la Argentina le levanta aranceles a 233 productos de Estados Unidos” y advirtió sobre el perjuicio para la producción local de medicamentos genéricos, al tiempo que …

title: Πορεία υπεράσπισης των καταλήψεων, Σάββατο 21/11, στις 19.00, στη πλατεία Λιονταριών, Ηράκλειο
content:
Καλούν οι:

Κατάληψη Ευαγγελισμού και  Συνέλευση Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών Λ. Αλεξάνδρας (ΣΥ.ΚΑ.ΠΡΟ.)


Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Κατάληψη Ευαγγελισμού


Κάλεσμα της Κατάληψης Ευαγγελισμού σε Πορεία Υπεράσπισης των Καταλήψεων το Σάββατο 21/11 στις 19:00 στην Πλ. Λιονταριών


Το κράτος επιτίθεται για ακόμα μία φορά στις καταλήψεις, αναγνωρίζοντας τον κίνδυνο που αποτελεί για αυτό η ύπαρξη χώρων, οι οποίοι προτείνουν ενεργά έναν τρόπο ύπαρξης εκτός των στενών ορίων που έχει θέσει, μέρη όπου οι κοινωνικοί αγώνες συσπειρώνονται και εξελίσσονται και μέρη όπου το κάθε ένα από εμάς μπορεί να πάρει μία ανάσα από την ασφυκτική καθημερινότητα που μας επιβάλλεται. Η απειλή προς τις καταλήψεις, από την Κατάληψη Ευαγγελισμού μέχρι την Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, αλλά και κάθε άλλη κατασταλτική ενέργεια ενάντια σε αυτοδιαχειριζομενους χώρους, δεν είναι μεμονωμένη, αλλά αποτελεί ένα κομμάτι της διαρκούς επίθεσης κράτους και κεφαλαίου στον αναρχικό/αντιεξουσιαστικό χώρο. Μία επίθεση, που επίσης παίρνει σάρκα μέσω της ποινικοποίησης της αναρχικής πολιτικής δράσης, με το πιο πρόσφατο παράδειγμα αυτής, να είναι η προσθήκη επιπλέον ποινής στον αναρχικό φοιτητή Ζ.Μ., η ανάσυρση της υπόθεσης της Μαρφίν από τα σκονισμένα ντουλάπια της Ασφάλειας, η υπόθεση της Θεσσαλονίκης. Για τις δύο τελευταίες μάλιστα, ένα γιγαντιαίων διαστάσεων μιντιακό σόου, διατυμπάνιζε την ενοχή των κατηγορουμένων πριν καν περάσει στα χέρια των δικαστικών αρχών και της δικαιοσύνης τους. Μία τακτική, λοιδορίας της αγωνιζόμενης κοινότητας και αποπροσανατολισμού της κοινωνίας, που παρατηρήσαμε και εμείς στις 12/11, με την Υπουργό Παιδείας να βγαίνει στα κανάλια και να μιλάει για την “αξιοποίηση” του Ευαγγελισμού και την “επιστροφή του στην κοινωνία”, διαφημίζοντας το προκλητικό ποσό των 6 εκατομμυρίων που θα διατεθούν για την “ανάπλαση” του κτηρίου, έργο που μόνο σκοπό έχει το μοίρασμα της πίτας των λίγων. Δεκαετίες είχαν αφήσει ένα κτήριο να ρημάζει παρατημένο και, όπως και όλες οι καταλήψεις, απέκτησε πάλι ζωή και χαρακτήρα χάρη στην ανιδιοτελή σπατάλη ατελείωτου χρόνου και χρημάτων από την ίδια κοινότητα, την οποία θέλουν να εκτοπίσουν, τώρα που θυμήθηκαν ξανά την ύπαρξή του. Εμείς όμως δεν θα υποκύψουμε στις απειλές τους και σίγουρα δεν θα ακολουθήσουμε τα πλάνα τους. Θα μείνουμε εδώ και θα τους περιμένουμε υπερασπιζόμενα τους αγώνες, τις αρνήσεις, τις επιθυμίες μας και τους χώρους μας, με όποιο μέσο θεωρήσουμε αναγκαίο.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI vice-president candidates share ambitions
content:
This story was updated on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 1:26 p.m. ET.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to each of the four candidates running to become one of two vice-presidents at Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. in

its Dec. 14 election

. Here’s what they had to share:


Aaron Aopaloktok Pedersen said three mottos are the heart of his campaign: “Homes we can own, a culture we all share, and money every Inuk can see.”


Pedersen, who is from Cambridge Bay, joined NTI last fall as a housing and homelessness project manager. Since October, he’s served as the chief operating officer of the organization’s

housing corporation, Igluvut

.


Igluvut will own and operate at least 25 affordable fixed rent apartments after they are constructed under a plan to build over 700 homes with the federal and territorial governments.


Pedersen said he wants to create pathways for renters to become homeowners by helping them access down payments.

He also wants to support social and cultural programming aimed at youth and elders and introduce annual reports that disclose how NTI spends its money in each community.


Robert Bourassa, from Pangnirtung, has worked in Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s marine and wildlife division since 2018, where he oversees the implementation of impact benefit agreements from protected areas. 


He also sits on the board of the investment firm Atuqtuarvik Corp., which invests money into Inuit-owned businesses.


“I want to see Inuit prosper,” he told Nunatsiaq News.


He has thought of getting into politics for a long time, he said, mentioning that his grandfather Ipeelee Kilabuk served as a Northwest Territories MLA in the 1970s. 


Bourassa said addressing the housing shortage and improving access to mental health services are his top priorities.


Under the federal budget, Canada pledged $50 billion for Indigenous people over the next decade in sectors like infrastructure, housing and education. Bourassa wants to lobby the government to make sure those funds support housing.


Paul Irngaut, from Igloolik, has been NTI’s vice-president since 2022.


He served as acting president after former NTI president Jeremy Tunraluk went on leave in December 2025. Tunraluk ultimately

resigned

 from the position, triggering a byelection which was held in May. Irngaut threw his hat into the ring to stay in the presidential post, but

lost

 to Gloria Uluqsi.


“I’ve always worked toward the betterment of Inuit, and I think I have a proven track record with the organization,” Irngaut said.


Last year, he helped oversee NTI’s signing of

a

$1.5 billion, 10-year implementation contract

 with the federal government, through which the organization secured $77.6 million per year in funding.


Irngaut wants to strengthen the territory’s fishing industry and create a “marine council” for discussions between Canada’s Department of Fisheries and Oceans and such organizations as the Nunavut Wildlife Management Board and Nunavut Water Board.


“We have to start talking closely with our government before devolution happens,” he said. “It’s important that we have all these things in place so that we can start protecting Inuit rights.”


Adamee Itorcheak serves as the Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s secretary-treasurer, a role he took leave from earlier this year to serve as NTI’s acting vice-president and, for a short time, acting president in the lead up to the May byelection to fill in during Irgnaut’s bid for president.


He also sits on the board of the non-profit Annauma Community Foundation and the Inuit Broadcasting Corp. He was president of Baffin Fisheries.


Itorcheak said he is focused on encouraging NTI to be more transparent about how it spends money, smarter spending, and revitalizing Inuktikut. He wants to continue the work he was doing under NTI’s $4.3-million education program, which aims to open an all-Inuktikut school.


“We need to make some conscious decisions on how we’re going to preserve our language.”


He also said “Inuit have to be front and centre” at talks about projects of national interest, such as the Kivalliq Hydro-Fibre Link and the Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydro Project.


Correction

: This story has been updated to correct information about Igluvut’s role in regards to the 25 affordable fixed rent apartments, as well as information about Aaron Aopaloktok Pedersen’s role in the plan to build over 700 homes with the federal and territorial governments.

title: Özgür Özel: Seçimi kazanacak cesarete ve ülkeyi yönetecek maharete sahibiz
content:
YENİ Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel, partisinin Ankara’da düzenlediği 1. Olağan Kurultayı’nda konuştu.


“Türkiye Yenileniyor” sloganıyla toplanan kurultayda Özel, partinin kuruluş sürecini, parti içi demokrasiye ilişkin düzenlemelerini ve ekonomi, adalet, dış politika ile toplumsal barışa yönelik hedeflerini anlattı.


“Müesses nizamın çarkları tepedeki bir azınlık için dönmektedir. İşte biz, o düzenin çarkına çomak sokanlarız” diyen Özel, partisinin “seçimleri kazanacak cesarete ve Türkiye’yi yönetecek maharete sahip olduğunu” söyledi.


YENİ Parti 1. Olağan Kurultayı çalışmalarına başladı


Bugün  13:00


Özel, 24 Temmuz’da kurdukları YENİ Parti’nin siyasi kuruluş sürecini kurultayla tamamlayacaklarını söyledi. Partinin ortaya çıkışını, CHP yönetimine yönelik yargı kararları ve müdahalelerle ilişkilendiren Özel, iktidarın siyasi rekabeti engellediğini savundu.


CHP’nin önceki kurultaylarına ilişkin kararları ve genel merkezine yönelik polis müdahalesini eleştiren Özel, bu gelişmelerin ardından yeni bir parti kurma kararı aldıklarını anlattı.


Özel, konuşmasında tutuklu İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu’na ve cezaevindeki belediye başkanlarına da değindi. Beşiktaş, Beykoz, Şişli, Büyükçekmece, Bayrampaşa, Ataşehir ve Adalar belediye başkanlarının YENİ Parti’ye katıldığını duyurdu.


Tutuklu yedi belediye başkanı YENİ Parti’ye geçti


Bugün  12:00


“Genel başkanı sadece üyelerimiz belirleyecek”


Özel, parti içi demokrasiyi güçlendirmek amacıyla ilçe başkanlarını, il başkanlarını ve genel başkanı doğrudan üyelerin seçmesini sağlayan bir sistem kurduklarını söyledi.


Eylül ayında ilçe, ekim ayında il başkanlığı seçimlerini gerçekleştirdiklerini belirten Özel, 8 Kasım’daki genel başkan ön seçimine ilişkin şu bilgileri verdi:


Tam 2 bin 502 sandıkta, 800 binden fazla üyemizin yüzde 82’sinin rekor katılımıyla Genel Başkan ön seçimini tamamladık.


Özel, mahalle, ilçe ve il meclisleri kuracaklarını, Siyaset Akademisi ve Dijital Katılım Platformu aracılığıyla üyelerin karar süreçlerine katılımını artıracaklarını söyledi.


Parti Meclisi’nin yapısını da değiştirdiklerini anlatan Özel, bu organın Parti Yasama Grubu, Parti Örgütü Grubu ve Politika Geliştirme Grubu olmak üzere üç bölümden oluşacağını açıkladı.


Asgari ücret, emekli aylığı ve sosyal konut vaatleri


Konuşmasının ekonomi bölümünde hayat pahalılığını, gelir dağılımındaki eşitsizliği ve barınma krizini ele alan Özel, YENİ Parti’nin ekonomik vaatlerini sıraladı.


Özel, asgari ücreti açlık sınırının üzerine çıkarmayı, ücret artışının işverenler üzerindeki yükünü devlet desteğiyle hafifletmeyi ve en düşük emekli aylığını asgari ücret düzeyine yükseltmeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi.


Barınma sorununa karşı sosyal konut stokunu artıracaklarını belirten Özel, sosyal konutlarda kira tutarını hane gelirinin yüzde 25’iyle sınırlama vaadinde bulundu.


Vergi politikalarına da değinen Özel, dolaylı vergileri azaltacaklarını, ücretlilerin gelir vergisi yükünü hafifleteceklerini ve vergilendirmede gelir ile serveti esas alacaklarını anlattı.


Tarım politikalarında ise çiftçilere alım garantisi vermeyi, mazottaki vergileri kaldırmayı ve çiftçi borçlarının faizlerini silerek borçları beş yılda yapılandırmayı hedeflediklerini söyledi.


“Bir daha kimsenin ele geçiremeyeceği bir yargı sistemi kuracağız”


Özel, konuşmasında yargı bağımsızlığına ve tutuklama uygulamalarına geniş yer ayırdı. İmamoğlu ve diğer tutuklu siyasetçiler hakkındaki davaların siyasi amaç taşıdığını savunan Özel, tahliye çağrısı yaptı.


“Tutuklama bir ön infaz yöntemi değildir. Son tedbirdir,” diyen Özel, iktidara gelmeleri durumunda yargının bağımsızlığını ve tarafsızlığını güvence altına alacaklarını söyledi.


Özel, “Biz iktidara geldiğimizde yargıyı ele geçirmeye asla çalışmayacağız. Bir daha kimsenin ele geçiremeyeceği bir yargı sistemi kuracağız” dedi.


Gazetecilere yönelik soruşturma ve tutuklamaları da eleştiren Özel, basın ve medya kuruluşlarının siyasi müdahalelerden bağımsız faaliyet yürütmesini sağlayacak bir düzen kurmayı vadetti.


Özel, adalet anlayışlarını dört başlıkta topladıklarını belirterek, “Mahkemede adalet, gelirde adalet, vergide adalet, sosyal hayatta adaleti sağlayacağız” dedi.


Eşit yurttaşlık ve barış çağrısı


Özel, YENİ Parti’nin sosyal demokrat bir parti olduğunu belirterek farklı kimliklerin, inançların ve siyasi görüşlerin eşit haklara sahip olacağı bir düzen hedeflediklerini söyledi.


Başörtüsü ve cemevi meselelerini eşit yurttaşlık hakkı …

author: James Crump
title: Spain Caps Rents and Protects Tenants After Four Million Join Protests
content:
Spain’s parliament has approved a package of reforms aimed at making housing more affordable, a day after four million took part in a

nationwide general strike

 over the country’s housing crisis.


The measures, proposed by prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s government, include extending eviction protections for vulnerable tenants and restricting speculative property purchases by preventing companies from buying homes for less than 70% of their assessed value.


Rent increases will also be capped at 2%, while those already above the government’s neighbourhood reference index will be frozen. A 10% tax on flats rented to tourists will also be introduced. 


The conservative Popular Party said it will repeal the reforms if it takes power in the 29 November elections, which were called by Sánchez after his government failed to pass similar housing measures.


“Yesterday, the right to housing won on the street and in workplaces, and I hope it will win again at the ballot box,” said interim housing minister Isabel Rodríguez after the vote on Thursday.


Spain has witnessed weeks of housing protests following the eviction and subsequent death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who was forcibly removed from the flat she had lived in for 70 years in September after she couldn’t afford rent increases.


The country has a deficit of 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to over a million by 2028. The average rental price of a home, €1,176, is equivalent to 98.7% of the average young person’s monthly salary, according to the Youth Council of Spain.


“We won’t stop until we transform this country’s housing model from top to bottom,” said Alicia del Rio of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.


Trade unions reported 90% turnouts among dockworkers and carmakers for the 24-hour strike on Wednesday – Spain’s first general strike in 14 years –

with “total stoppages”

 at Volkswagen’s factory in Navarre and SEAT’s in Barcelona, organisers said.


Around 85% of meat industry workers, 82% of waste collection employees and 75% from the energy sector also took part. In healthcare and ⁠social services roughly 38% went on strike, while 35% of postal service workers also joined.

author: Ming-Yeh T. Rawnsley
title: Making Hope Credible: Puma Shen and the Politics of Access in Taipei
content:
A HOME THAT can be renewed without repeated moves, a cultural allowance that continues into working adulthood, and an exercise service that comes to the neighbourhood: these are tangible reasons to pay attention to Puma Shen’s (沈伯洋) campaign for Taipei mayor. They also offer a way to test the comparison increasingly drawn between Shen and New York mayor Zohran Mamdani. Beyond the excitement surrounding an unexpected challenger, what would make the city more accessible to people with unequal resources?

Shen’s command of municipal policy has helped change how voters see him. Nathan Batto’s account dated September 28 describes how detailed answers helped him reach beyond his established image as a specialist in civil defence and Chinese information warfare. His appeal invites scrutiny of what that expertise could deliver for residents who find existing services difficult to use.

THE COMPARISON reportedly helped shape the contest itself. ETtoday’s Tao Ben-he (³³¥»©M) reported on October 29 that President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) drew inspiration from Mamdani’s unexpected rise when insisting on Shen’s nomination as the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) candidate. The reported connection poses a consequential question: if New York supplied inspiration for choosing a candidate, how much of Mamdani’s challenge to inequality has travelled with it?

Brian Hioe identified the distinction in New Bloom, also on October 29: Mamdani campaigned explicitly against socioeconomic inequality, while Shen has emphasised policy expertise and good governance. The proposals examined here suggest a distinctive contribution: reducing the practical burdens of using public provision. That could bring meaningful improvements, although its redistributive reach remains uneven, particularly where housing assistance depends on ownership.

Mamdani’s promises to freeze rents for rent-stabilised tenants, make buses free and provide universal childcare named household costs that government could reduce. His inaugural address on January 1 also connected childcare to taxing the wealthiest. Taipei need not reproduce those policies to learn from their political clarity: residents should understand whose circumstances will improve, who will contribute and what public authority will do.

Shen has offered a wide range of policy proposals. From that platform, I examine three areas—housing and urban renewal, cultural support for young adults, and neighbourhood exercise services for older residents—to assess how his proposals would change access to public resources. These examples reveal different relationships between administrative reform and inequality; they cannot establish the overall redistributive ambition of his platform.

HOUSING PROVIDES the hardest test. Taipei’s existing approach is not simply to leave residents to negotiate with developers. The city already promotes publicly led renewal and faster review through its urban renewal programmes. It also provides temporary accommodation and describes neighbourhood-based relocation as an objective, including arrangements involving social housing. Shen’s alternative must therefore demonstrate what it changes in practice.

His proposed circular urban renewal scheme (無限都更) changes the sequence of redevelopment. Willing owners would exchange existing property rights for a new home, or rights to use one, before their original site is rebuilt. The city would assemble an initial housing supply and manage the exchange; completed redevelopment would replenish resources for subsequent rounds. The objective is to avoid the familiar sequence of moving into temporary accommodation and moving again after reconstruction.

The scheme recognises disruption as a real cost, especially for older residents whose routines depend on nearby care and social relationships. It could make agreement easier without treating reluctant residents as obstacles. But Shen’s policy acknowledges limited initial supply. Its preference for nearby exchanges needs to be supported by identified sites and a realistic timetable.

Valuation is equally important. Shen’s scheme envisages settling differences between old and new property values, with loan assistance where needed. An older owner with little income may still struggle to bridge that difference. Independent valuations, accessible advice and safeguards against unaffordable debt would determine whether the exchange expands choice or mainly assists households already able to pay.

author: Unknown
title: Incekara: Determination of young people proves that resistance is possible
content:
Protests launched by high school students in Paris against poor educational conditions have had a domino effect, spreading across France and to other countries. What began as a protest over education has developed into broader opposition to the system, encompassing the rising cost of living, declining wages and the housing crisis. These developments have also drawn attention to Turkey, where exploitation and inequality are even more deeply entrenched. University students took to the streets in Istanbul on the anniversary of the establishment of the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), an institution created in the aftermath of the fascist military coup of September 12, 1980. Students protested against the government's increasingly repressive measures. Demonstrations in Beyazıt Square and Beşiktaş were particularly marked by anger over a directive issued by the Ministry of Interior concerning universities in September. Istanbul University student Yasin Incekara spoke to ANF and said, "The determination shown by young people during the March 19 protests demonstrated that it is possible to resist the repressive regime being established in Turkey and showed how these blockades can be broken."


'Young people face similar forms of repression worldwide'


Yasin Incekara, a second-year sociology student at Istanbul University, said that young people taking to the streets across Europe and other parts of the world reflected the problems they share. Incekara emphasized that although Europe is often portrayed as a prosperous society, young people there also struggle with poverty and the problems created by the capitalist system. He said, "Over the past few months, we have seen young people taking to the streets against poverty, the lack of a future and repressive policies, not only in the Middle East but also in Europe, which is presented as prosperous. The youth uprising that has emerged particularly in France shows that young people face similar forms of repression not only in Turkey but in many parts of the world."


'March 19 showed young people's determination to seek freedom'


Incekara said that although resistance in Turkey has been weaker than in other countries, the March 19 protests demonstrated how young people could break through the restrictions being imposed on them. He described the March 19 protests and subsequent developments as evidence of young people's determination to pursue freedom in the face of oppression. Incekara said, "Through their determination to demand freedom against oppression, young people demonstrated during the March 19 protests that it is possible to resist the repressive regime being established in Turkey and showed how these blockades can be broken."


'Repressive directives seek to label revolutionary students as terrorists'


Incekara said that the authorities had intensified repression through various mechanisms in response to the determination shown by young people in their struggle. He pointed to the 17-article directive sent to universities by the Ministry of Interior in September, which he described as fascist, as the latest example. He argued that the directive sought to label students involved in progressive and revolutionary activities at universities as "terrorists." Incekara said: "The directive explicitly refers to providing private security personnel at universities with training similar to that given to police officers, as well as intensifying efforts to recruit informants and pressure students into becoming collaborators. It also opens the way for officers from the Anti-Terrorism Branch to set up information stands at universities under the pretext of awareness-raising and preventive activities, allowing them to conduct intelligence operations. Through these stands, the police aim to criminalize students involved in political struggle in the eyes of newly enrolled students, portraying them as marginal groups associated with terrorism and manipulating newcomers with warnings to 'stay away from them.' Of course, this does not reflect reality. If there is any group seeking to spread terror today, it is the capitalist state and the police themselves."


'Families are also pressured to inform on their children'
