title: Habiter au corps d'un âne mort ou le chemin de Nietzsche
content:
Dans la continuité des très nombreux articles que nous avons publiés afin de déchiffrer l'Intelligence artificielle, le monde qu'elle avale, celui qu'elle charrie et celui qu'elle produit, nous partageons cette semaine l'épatante découverte d'Olivier Chiran et Pierre Muzin. La première occurrence de l'expression IA reviendrait au célèbre philosophe Friedrich Nietzsche dans le tout aussi célèbre

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

, un tiret séparait néanmoins les deux voyelles :

« Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit. »


« Donnez-moi du travail, de la fatigue,


de la douleur et de l'enthousiasme. »


George Sand


1.


Pour savoir précisément où nous en sommes, mais aussi faire face à ce qui nous arrive, alors que l'intelligence artificielle étend son emprise sur le monde et les vies, nous avons besoin d'un sémaphore.


2.


On dit que l'expression « intelligence artificielle » a été lancée par John McCarthy, en 1956, lors de la conférence de Dartmouth, coup d'envoi du programme de recherche consacré à la reproduction algorithmique de la pensée humaine. Soixante-douze ans plus tôt, en 1884, Friedrich Nietzsche, le célèbre philosophe allemand, rédige son grand poème philosophique :

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

. Dans la troisième partie de cet ouvrage (trouvée « sous le ciel alcyonien de Nice », dira-t-il), il écrit : « Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit

 [

1

]

. » Première apparition de ces deux lettres, longtemps avant Dartmouth. Évidence de leur rapprochement – en même temps que, d'un simple tiret, de leur mise à distance. On pourrait s'étonner que les traducteurs français (Henri Albert en 1903, Geneviève Bianquis en 1969) aient fait le choix, au lieu du « hi-han » conventionnel, de les conserver telles quelles. Mais le texte allemand dit bien : «

Immer I-A sagen – das lernte allein der Esel, und wer seines Geistes ist

 ! » – Nietzche ayant délibérément fait tomber le

h

 de «

iah

 », braiment de l'âne dans la langue de Goethe. Nous dirons donc, quant à nous, que l'histoire de l'I-A commence à la fin du xixe siècle, lorsqu'un philosophe visionnaire, cheminant à flanc de montagne, a compris qu'on pouvait arracher au cri de l'âne sa puissance d'exclamation intempestive – et qu'il y avait là, pour nous, un grand danger

 [

2

]

.


3.


C'est qu'il y a deux ânes. Gilles Deleuze, commentant les propos de Nietzsche : « On aurait pu croire que l'âne, l'animal qui dit I-A, était l'animal dionysiaque par excellence. En fait, il n'en est rien ; son apparence est dionysiaque, mais toute sa réalité est chrétienne

 [

3

]

. » Le braiment sans son ou ses

h

, c'est cette manière qu'a l'âne de dire toujours oui – mais un faux oui, une fausse affirmation qui ne sait pas dire non, qui ne sait qu'acquiescer face à ce qui est. Bêtise. Démission de la pensée. Obscurantisme. Post-vérité. Positivisme logique. (Margaret Thatcher : «

There is no alternative

 » → TINA : « I-A ! I-A ! ») Toutes choses contre lesquelles, justement, la philosophie s'évertue à lutter. « Le réel tel qu'il est, conclut Deleuze, c'est une idée d'âne. »


4.


Il arrive aussi, on le sait, que l'âne se cabre. L'I-A approbatif que dénoncent les philosophes est la forme mutilée de ce « hi-han ! » qui est à la fois refus catégorique et cri pour l'autonomie et la liberté. Entre les deux, il y a toute la différence entre l'âne vivant (dionysiaque) et l'âne mort (chrétien) – entre l'appel à la révolte et le bourdon béat de la fanfare. (« Si l'âne contribue peu à l'harmonie durant sa vie, écrivait-on au milieu du xixe siècle, il la sert généreusement après sa mort, lui fournissant les meilleures peaux qui existent pour les grosses caisses et les meilleurs tibias pour fabriquer des clarinettes

 [

4

]

. »)


5.


Dans

L'Âne

, de Lucius de Patras, le narrateur voit une magicienne se transformer en oiseau après s'être frotté le corps avec un onguent

 [

5

]

. Ayant voulu l'imiter, il se retrouve, quant à lui, métamorphosé en âne. Séquestré par une bande de brigands, il tente de leur échapper en emportant avec lui, dans sa fuite, une jeune prisonnière. Par malchance, les brigands retrouvent les fuyard

·

e

·

s, les renvoient à leur geôle et imaginent comment les punir avec toute la sévérité requise. « Écoutez une rare et nouvelle invention, qui vous plaira, ou je me trompe fort, dit l'un d'eux à ses comparses ; l'âne doit mourir, c'est la justice …

title: Lieblingsstreberin: Paula Saunders
content:
In der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ gerät Tatiana Maslany als geschiedene Mutter in einen Scam aus Cybersex, Erpressung und Verschwörung.

Geschiedene Soccer Mom, gewissenhafte Fact-Checkerin, falsch Verdächtigte? Paula Saunders (Tatiana Maslany), Protagonistin der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“, lässt sich auf kein Label festlegen. Sie jongliert mit einem Sorgerechtsstreit und einem schlecht bezahlten Medien-Vollzeitjob – worüber sie sich beim Online-Sexarbeiter Trevor ausheult, der ihr empathisch zuhört, solange sie ihn bezahlt. Bis Trevor plötzlich bei ihrer Camsex-Session entführt wird. Kurze Zeit später kriegt sie einen Anruf, dass sie 15.000 Dollar zahlen soll, um ihn freizukaufen. Von der Polizei wird sie mit dem Hinweis, dass das sicher Betrug ist, abgewimmelt. Als sie nicht zahlt, wird sie mit Cybersex-Aufnahmen erpresst. Da das Sorgerecht für ihre Tochter auf dem Spiel steht, nimmt sie die Sache selbst in die Hand und spürt anhand von ein paar wackeligen Screenshots und einer Überweisung die Erpresser*innen auf. Sie beherrscht alle Techniken der Open-Source-Recherche, ist kreativ und fokussiert, wenn es darum geht, die Fakten herauszufinden. Bis die Frage aufkommt: Wer sind eigentlich die Scammer hinter Trevor? Während die Darstellung von Online-Sexarbeiter*innen als „Scammer“ klischeehaft ausfällt, finden sich alle menschlichen Ambivalenzen in Paulas Charakter wieder, was sicher auch Tatiana Maslanys schauspielerischem Können zu verdanken ist. Paula wird von einer Mischung aus Erpressung, Gewalt und Tatendrang weiter in den Scam hineingezogen, bis sie der ziemlich nutzlosen Polizei immer verdächtiger erscheint. Dabei will Paula nach eigenen Angaben nur eine gute Mutter sein und legt sich dafür regelmäßig mit ihrem Ex-Mann Karl (Jake Johnson) an. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Wenn sie nur ihre Unschuld beweisen und die große Verschwörung aufdecken könnte, die sie in die Situation gebracht hat … Die Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ ist auf Apple TV verfügbar, eine zweite Staffel ist geplant. author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

title: Muslims Are Not a Security Threat. Western Governments Are.
content:
By Zobidah Yousif Elamin and Joseph Essertier,

Dissident Voice

, November 20, 2026


Sudan is a country where

9 million people

 have been driven from their homes;

34 million are in need of assistance

;

19.5 million people

 do not have enough to eat; and drones killed more than

300 civilians

 in three weeks in October alone, many of them in crowded markets.


The United Nations calls it the “

world’s largest humanitarian crisis

.” Yet if you asked your neighbors what is happening in Sudan, few could tell you anything. Here we explain in plain language what this war is about, why so few people have heard of it, and who is making money while Sudanese people die.


What is happening in Sudan?


Sudan is a large country in northeast Africa, on the Red Sea, with a population of about 50 million people. In 2019, after months of peaceful street protests, Sudanese people overthrew the dictator

Omar al-Bashir

, who had ruled for 30 years. Subsequently, a transitional government was formed, in which the generals shared power with a small group of civilian leaders.


That government did not last. In October 2021, two generals seized power together in a coup d’état. One was

Abdel Fattah al-Burhan

, the head of the “

Sudanese Armed Forces

” or “SAF.” The other was

Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo

, whose

nom de guerre

 is “Hemedti,” the head of a paramilitary force called the “

Rapid Support Forces

” (or “RSF”). The RSF grew out of the

Janjaweed militias

 that committed mass atrocities in Darfur between 2003 and 2008.


The two generals fell out over the question of who would control the guns. On 15 April 2023, fighting broke out in the capital Khartoum and spread across the country—not a war between “Muslims” and non-Muslims, or a war of ideas, but a war between two armed groups fighting for power, land, and money, with civilians caught in the middle.


Today the country is split into two territories. The

SAF holds Khartoum

, the north, and the east, including Port Sudan on the Red Sea. The RSF holds almost all of Darfur in the west and runs a rival government there. The heaviest fighting is now in Kordofan, near central Sudan, and in the

state of Blue Nile

, in the southeast.


A meeting of mediators in Geneva ended on the 21st of October

without a ceasefire

.


Why the 2019 transition failed


After al-Bashir’s fall, there was no democratic transition in any real sense. What happened instead was a political deal between the SAF and the RSF, the two forces actually in control on the ground, and a small group of leaders from revolutionary organizations, including the

Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-Revolutionary Democratic Front

 (SPLM-RDF), whom the military accepted as representatives of the civilian side. In other words, this period cannot be called democratic. It was a power-sharing arrangement between the two sides.


The group that represented the civilian side, the

Central Council of the Forces of Freedom and Change

 (CCFFC), kept political representation to itself. It extended the transitional period more than once. It never created the

Transitional Legislative Council

 required by the transitional constitution, even though that Council was meant to give the revolutionaries a voice and keep the transition in check. Over time, disputes grew between those who had climbed into civilian power and the revolutionaries on the street, and also between the CCFFC and the prime minister

Abdalla Hamdok

. In 2021, Hamdok’s government also stayed silent while

protesters were attacked and killed

, most notably at the first anniversary of the sit-in, in front of the prime minister’s office. As a result, the government, and Hamdok himself, became cut off from the revolution happening on the street.


There was also an unspoken dispute between Hamdok and some CCFFC leaders over who had the power to appoint people to senior posts, which deepened the rift between them. While these divisions grew, the SAF and the RSF watched and waited, until the coup came. Some have said that there was an indirect understanding between Hamdok and the military because he believed the revolutionaries would support him once the CCFFC was pushed aside.


After the staged arrest and his return as the prime minister appointed by the military, the revolutionaries on the street did not stand with him. Protests continued, and dozens of revolutionaries were killed. He then resigned and left for the United Arab Emirates (UAE).


It is …

title: 25 ülkede gençler "gelecekleri için ve savaşlara karşı" sokaktaydı
content:
20 Kasım Cuma günü, Avrupa'da öğrenciler ve genç emekçiler,“Geleceğimiz için mücadele, onların savaşları için değil” çağrısıyla sokaklara çıktı. 50'yi aşkın gençlik ve öğrenci örgütünün oluşturduğu Uluslararası Gençlik Grevi Koalisyonu'nun çağrısıyla 25'ten fazla ülkede düzenlenen gösterilerde eğitim ve sosyal hizmetlere daha fazla kaynak ayrılması, barınma hakkı, insanca ücretler, iklim adaleti ve silahlanma harcamalarının azaltılması istendi.


"GELECEĞİMİZ İÇİN ONLARIN SAVAŞLARINA KARŞI"


Avrupa, 20 Kasım'a en az 25 ülkede gençlik grevleriyle uyanıyor


Bugün  03:59


Roma'dan Lizbon'a, Paris'ten Londra'ya uzanan eylemlerde ortak talepler öne çıksa da katılımın ölçeği ve protestoların gündemi yerel önceliklere de bağlı olarak ülkeden ülkeye değişti. En kitlesel gösteriler İtalya'da gerçekleşirken diğer ülkelerde de yürüyüşlerde binlerce kişi bir araya geldi. 


Koalisyon yaklaşık 400 kentte eylem planlandığını açıklamıştı. Gerçekleşme düzeyi henüz net olarak belirlenmedi. .


İtalya: Gençlik eylemleri genel grevle birleşti


Günün en geniş katılımlı gösterileri İtalya'daydı. Ülkenin en büyük sendika konfederasyonu CGIL'in ücret artışı ve kamu hizmetlerine daha fazla yatırım talebiyle düzenlediği genel greve öğrenciler de katıldı.


Roma, Milano, Bologna ve diğer kentlerde on binlerce işçi ve öğrenci yürüdü. CGIL Genel Sekreteri Maurizio Landini, 100'den fazla kentteki gösterilere toplam bir milyondan fazla kişinin katıldığını ileri sürdü. İçişleri Bakanlığı ise kendi bulgularını açıklamadı. 


Landini, Roma'daki gösteride Avrupa çapındaki hareketle dayanışmasını şu sözlerle dile getirdi:


“Bugün çok önemli bir gün. Çünkü yalnızca İtalya'da değil, Avrupa'nın dört bir yanında gençler sokaklara çıkıyor.


“Avrupa genelinde ve sıradan insanlar arasında değişim talebi büyüyor.”


 Başbakan Giorgia Meloni hükümetinin 2027 bütçesine yönelik tepkiler grevin odağındaydı. Sendikalar, ücretlerin ve sosyal hizmetlerin desteklenmesi, eğitim ve sağlığa daha fazla kaynak ayrılması talebini yükseltti. 


24 yaşındaki üniversite öğrencisi Laura Peritore, hükümetin tercihlerini şöyle eleştirdi:


“Sağlık ve eğitim harcamalarını parça parça kesen, bugünümüzü elimizden alan ve geleceğimizi çalmaya çalışan bir hükümetin yönetimi altında yaşıyoruz.”


Peritore, geri çekilmeyeceklerini ve geleceklerini geri alacaklarını söyledi.


Roma'da Eğitim Bakanlığı önünde gösteriler düzenlendi. Bologna'da bazı protestocularla polis arasında çatışmalar yaşandı. Milano'da ise göstericiler kartondan yapılmış bir tankeri ve Donald Trump ile Binyamin Netanyahu'yu temsil eden maketleri yaktı.


Fransa: Süren öğrenci hareketinden Avrupa dayanışmasına


Avrupa çapındaki eylem çağrısının arka planında, Fransa'da haftalardır devam eden lise ve üniversite protestoları da bulunuyor.


Eğitim koşullarının kötüleşmesine, kamu hizmetlerindeki kesintilere ve toplumsal eşitsizliklere karşı gelişen hareket, 20 Kasım'da Avrupa'nın diğer ülkelerindeki gençlik örgütleriyle ortak talepler etrafında buluştu.


Paris'teki gösteride konuşan 25 yaşındaki öğrenci Evelyn, hayat pahalılığı ile iklim krizinin gençlerin gelecek kaygısını birlikte derinleştirdiğini söyledi:


“Kararları bugün veren insanlara bırakırsak bizi, ölümle dolu bir gelecek bekliyor.”


Fransa'dan Union Étudiante temsilcisi Alice Cohen ise uluslararası eylemin tek günlük bir protestoyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğini vurguladı:


“Ne kadar büyük olursa olsun, tek günlük bir grevin ihtiyacımız olan değişiklikleri sağlamaya yetmeyeceğini biliyoruz.”


Cohen, öğrencileri ve emekçileri ortak talepler etrafında birleştirecek kalıcı bir uluslararası hareket oluşturmayı hedeflediklerini belirtti.


Portekiz ve İspanya: Barınma hakkı ve sosyal adalet


Lizbon'da öğrenciler ortak grev çağrısına katılırken Portekizli gençlik örgütleri barınma krizini, eğitim hakkını ve Avrupa'nın silahlanma politikalarını gündeme taşıdı.


Estudantes pelo Fim ao Fóssil örgütünden Leonor Chicó, gençlerin kendi geleceklerini savunmak için örgütlenmeleri gerektiğini söyledi:


“Gençler olarak geleceğimiz için örgütlenmemiz ve mücadele etmemiz gerektiğini biliyoruz. Çünkü bunu bizim yerimize kimse yapmayacak.”

title: Iraqi army takes control of Jurf al-Sakhar, stronghold of Kataib Hezbollah
content:
The Iraqi central government has taken control of security in the Jurf al-Sakhar region, which has been dominated by the pro-Iranian militia Kataib Hezbollah for more than a decade. On Friday, army units and other security forces entered the town, located approximately 60 kilometers southwest of Baghdad. The deployment followed an agreement that temporarily averted an armed confrontation between government forces and the influential militia.


Jurf al-Sakhar, renamed Jurf al-Nasr by Shiite militias after its recapture from the Islamic State (ISIS) in 2014, is considered one of Kataib Hezbollah’s most important strongholds. The Iran-aligned militia has spent years establishing military structures there largely independently of the Iraqi central government. Baghdad’s attempt to regain control is therefore seen as a major test for Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.


Joint security command assumes responsibilities


According to Iraqi security officials, a joint command comprising units of the army, federal police, Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi), and police responsible for energy infrastructure began operating on Friday morning. The new command structure is expected to gradually assume responsibility for security and coordinate the withdrawal of the militia units previously stationed in the area. According to Iraqi government spokesperson Saad Maan, security forces have already begun monitoring the oil pipelines running through the region.


A major road link toward Karbala is also scheduled to reopen on Saturday. Units of the Iraqi army and federal police are expected to secure the route. The agreement stipulates that Kataib Hezbollah groups will leave the area and make way for state security forces. However, it remains unclear whether the militia will actually lose its longstanding influence over the region. The handover is expected to take place over an extended period.


Press conference by Iraqi officials


Iraqi officials held a press conference on the security situation in the Jurf al-Sakhar region on Friday.


Speaking here, Ahmed Hatim Hamid, commander of the Main Control Base, announced that a base had been established for the Iraqi army and police forces. He also reported that the Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Army had visited the region to monitor the deployment of military forces and inspect the measures taken.


The spokesperson for the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces stated that all administrative and management responsibilities in the Jurf al-Sakhar region had been transferred to the control base.


Meanwhile, the head of the Security Media Cell announced that a commando battalion had been deployed to the region to protect its oil pipelines. Stating that handover procedures were underway between the forces in the area, the head of the Security Media Cell said that security in the Jurf al-Sakhar region would now be under the control of federal forces.


Oil smuggling triggered power struggle


The latest confrontation was sparked by investigations into an alleged network involved in the illegal trade of Iraqi oil. According to an investigation by the Reuters news agency, members of Kataib Hezbollah, together with individuals from state security agencies and oil authorities, are suspected of having diverted crude oil from pipelines and smuggled it for years. Investigators reportedly discovered tampered pipelines, concealed pumping facilities, and a small refinery. The financial losses could amount to several hundred million dollars. Kataib Hezbollah denies the allegations and views the government’s actions as an attempt to force the militia to surrender its weapons.


In connection with the investigations, Prime Minister al-Zaidi ordered the dismissal of nine senior officials from security agencies and the oil sector. At the same time, government troops were placed on alert and prepared for a possible operation against the militia. The escalating tensions eventually led to negotiations involving influential Shiite politicians. Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Quds Force, also reportedly traveled to Baghdad to mediate between the parties. The handover now underway is seen as the outcome of these talks.


Closed off to the local population since 2014

author: Cami Koons
title: Army Postpones Detonation of Toxic Lead Azide in Iowa After Public Outcry
content:
Lead particles could spread 100 miles from the detonation site. The army says the detonation is now planned for Monday.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Environmental groups filed a lawsuit Thursday afternoon in an attempt to halt the planned detonation of degraded, lead-based explosive material at a munitions plant in southeast Iowa.

The lawsuit was filed hours before acting Secretary of the Army, Hon. Adam Telle announced the detonation would be postponed to Monday, Nov. 23, noting that “public safety is the Army’s top priority.” U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley said on social media the delay was to “further educate the public.”

Telle said in a post on social media that Monday was the “latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material.”

Earthjustice, on behalf of Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club Iowa Chapter, is suing the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency over its decision to grant an emergency permit to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown to intentionally detonate 68 drums of deteriorated lead azide, an explosive that is unstable in its deteriorated state.

The detonation, which will occur inside concrete bunkers that are surrounded by sand barriers approximately two stories high according to news releases from the Army, will cause a plume of air “with some lead-containing particles.” Nearby areas have been warned to stay inside while the lead particles are expected to be airborne and to spray down outdoor materials after lead-containing dust has settled on the surfaces.

In the lawsuit, filed in the U.S. Appellate Court for the Eighth District, environmental groups ask the court to either rule on the motion before Friday at 10 a.m. or issue an administrative stay until the motion can be fully heard in court.

Iowa Environmental Council Executive Director Sarah Green said in a statement Thursday that it “could be the case that the U.S. Army has no other safe alternative to disposing of the toxic lead azide.”

“But our federal government needs to do better at communicating the potential health risks of lead contamination in our communities and providing more time to keep our communities and vulnerable groups safe, like children and pregnant women,” Green said.

Petitioners allege the emergency permit from EPA failed to: incorporate applicable environmental performance standards, require all permit conditions necessary to protect human health and the environment, consider less dangerous alternatives that would avoid widespread dispersal and deposition of toxic lead, and adequately notify the public of the plan.

“The Army’s planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of explosive lead material poses a significant risk of irreparable harm that cannot later be remedied,” the lawsuit said.

The Army and EPA have said the intentional detonation allows them to mitigate the “explosion risk” of the degraded lead azide which presented an “imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment.”

Essentially, they said the intentional detonation of the material allows for precautions and public awareness that would not be possible if the material exploded on its own.

Environmental groups said they “do not dispute the EPA and Army’s assertion that there is risk involved in leaving the lead azide at the IAAP untreated” but said the Army left the explosive “to degrade for roughly two decades until it decided that the only safe option became detonating them near populated areas.”

According to the proposed action report from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, the lead azide was submerged in a water/ethanol storage solution. Temperature fluctuations caused the material to “dissolve and recrystallize” into a form that is “acutely sensitive to shock, friction, static electricity, and heat.” The Army determined in March the material had degraded, and in April had a briefing with EPA, according to the emergency permit.

“That turned the Army’s storage management failure into a public health event for people in at least two states,” the lawsuit said. “This rushed final week is a symptom of that; the Army has been aware of the risk since at least March, yet it gave public notice of its plans a mere five days before intended detonation.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Shenzhen no fue Yalta
content:
Bastó que Xi, Trump y Putin se sentaran a la misma mesa en Shenzhen, al margen de la cumbre de la APEC, para que muchos analistas desempolvaran Crimea en febrero de 1945.


Desde Kiev, Zelenski había anticipado una “redistribución de esferas de influencia”, un Yalta con Ucrania en el menú. La analogía seduce por su sencillez. Es falsa. Desde Moscú, Dmitri Peskov, vocero de Putin, respondió que si alguien pretende decidir los destinos del mundo, “seguro que no es Rusia, seguro que no es China”.


Yalta fue el reparto entre los vencedores de una guerra mundial librada contra un enemigo común. Roosevelt, Churchill y Stalin dibujaron fronteras porque tenían ejércitos sobre el terreno y un orden por fundar.


En Shenzhen no hubo vencedores ni enemigo común. Hubo una potencia hegemónica en declive, golpeada por la derrota en las elecciones de medio término y el empantanamiento de sus guerras, y urgida de prorrogar su tregua comercial con Pekín.


La tesis de las zonas de influencia no entiende el proyecto del anfitrión. China no gana nada encerrando el mundo en corrales; su economía vive de cadenas productivas que atraviesan fronteras. El lema de la cumbre, construir una comunidad del Asia-Pacífico para prosperar juntos, podrá sonar a fórmula diplomática, pero describe una estrategia material. Un Yalta le serviría sólo a Washington.


Porque la lógica de las esferas es la que practica Estados Unidos sin pedirle permiso a nadie. El corolario Trump de la Doctrina Monroe declara al hemisferio occidental patio propio. De eso no se habló en Shenzhen; eso se impone desde el Comando Sur.


Hablar de reparto tripartito le atribuye a la multipolaridad los rasgos del unipolarismo que se resiste a morir, cuando para los pueblos del Sur la multipolaridad es margen. Lo prueba que los tres presidentes de Nuestra América con silla en la APEC, Claudia Sheinbaum, Keiko Fujimori (Perú) y José Antonio Kast (Chile), cruzaran el Pacífico a buscar bilaterales con Xi, incluidos los dos que comulgan con Washington.


Nada de esto supone ingenuidad. Fue Putin quien le propuso a Trump sentarse los tres para discutir el fin de la guerra en Ucrania, y Trump aceptó aunque Zelenski quedara afuera. Es lo único que huele a Yalta, aunque el ausente no es una nación menor sino el ariete de la guerra

proxy

 que la OTAN encabezada por Estados Unidos sostiene desde 2014-22.


Y ni siquiera ahí hubo reparto. La declaración que difundió el Kremlin tras hora y media de reunión no trae mapas ni un solo acuerdo sobre Ucrania. Los tres miembros del Consejo de Seguridad se comprometieron a reformar la ONU que ya no expresa la correlación de fuerzas de Yalta. Coincidieron en el Perogrullo de que “una guerra nuclear no puede ganarse y nunca debe librarse”, sin una sola cifra de desarme.


Sumaron la estabilidad energética y un freno a los “abusos” de la Corte Penal Internacional. Puntos de contacto mínimos entre actores sin proyecto común, gestión del conflicto y no condominio. Es el interregno, el claroscuro donde lo viejo no termina de morir y lo nuevo no termina de nacer.


Mientras en Shenzhen se hablaba de paz, la guerra seguía por los mismos medios. Europa se reunió en Berlín con tambores de guerra pendientes de la cumbre en China. Yalta cerró una guerra. Shenzhen ocurrió en medio de una nueva guerra mundial, fragmentada, con otras formas, como definió el Papa Francisco.


Fernando Esteche es Director General del portal PIA global; doctor en Comunicación Social, profesor universitario.

Shenzhen no fue Yalta

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

author: L214
title: Budget 2027 : ce que les députés ont décidé pour les animaux
content:
Dernier budget de l’État avant la présidentielle, le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 est une occasion décisive de réorienter l’argent public vers un autre modèle agricole. Quel est le bilan des débats parlementaires et des décisions gouvernementales pour les animaux ?

Depuis le 13 octobre, l’Assemblée nationale a examiné en séance publique le projet de loi de finances pour 2027. Dans un contexte marqué par les canicules, les sécheresses et les incendies de l’été, le Gouvernement a annoncé plus d’un milliard d’euros pour « relancer la production agricole ». Face au dernier budget avant la présidentielle, les députés avaient un choix à faire : continuer à financer le modèle intensif ou investir dans une agriculture qui nous protège, nous et les autres animaux.

Avec Le Sauvetage du siècle, L214 défend des mesures concrètes pour atteindre la réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 : aider les éleveurs volontaires à sortir de l’élevage intensif ou de la pêche, développer les cultures végétales pour nous nourrir, taxer la publicité pour les produits animaux, ou encore soutenir les cantines pour qu’elles proposent une plus grande offre végétale.

Pourtant la quasi-totalité de ces propositions a été rejetée :

L’amendement I-3588 (Marianne Maximi, LFI) visant à réserver le suramortissement fiscal des projets d’avenir agricole aux élevages avec accès au plein air, rejeté par 50 voix contre 14,

L’amendement I-3467 (Anne Stambach-Terrenoir, LFI) cherchant à exclure du crédit d’impôt recherche les dépenses visant à intensifier les productions animales, rejeté par 101 voix contre 53,

L’amendement I-295 (Claire Lejeune, LFI) proposant de porter à 35 % l’impôt sur les sociétés pour les élevages intensifs soumis à autorisation, rejeté par 60 voix contre 27.

Un seul amendement favorable aux animaux a été adopté : l’amendement I-2017 de Romain Courbon (Socialistes), travaillé avec l’association QUATRE PATTES, qui crée un crédit d’impôt de 25 % pour les investissements favorisant la sortie des cages, l’accès au plein air et la réduction des densités. Il a été adopté par 10 voix contre 7.

Les débats ont aussi révélé la difficulté d’aborder sereinement la question de notre consommation de viande. Lors de l’examen du budget de la Sécurité sociale, Sandrine Rousseau (Écologiste et social) a défendu une taxe sur la viande ultra-transformée. Cette mesure a été qualifiée par Laurent Jacobelli (Rassemblement national) d’ « amendement le plus risible », malgré les impératifs pour les animaux, la santé publique et la transition écologique. L’amendement a été rejeté par 84 voix contre 14.

Le projet de loi de finances ayant finalement été rejeté par l’Assemblée nationale, aucun de ces amendements ne figurera dans le texte, en cours d’examen par le Sénat. La seconde partie du budget, consacrée aux dépenses, n’a pas pu être débattue à l’Assemblée. Encore une fois, les intérêts des animaux sont largement ignorés.

Pour la cinquième année consécutive, des députés ont tenté de s’attaquer aux associations qui révèlent les conditions d’élevage, de transport et d’abattage des animaux. Leur méthode : supprimer les réductions d’impôt sur les dons qui leur sont faits. Autrement dit, sanctionner les donateurs des associations pour entraver leur travail d’information.

Heureusement, tous les amendements examinés à l’Assemblée nationale ont été rejetés :

L’amendement I-1603 (Stéphanie Galzy, RN) : suppression de la réduction d’impôt pour les dons à une association condamnée pour intrusion, violation de domicile ou entrave à l’activité économique, rejeté le 15 octobre par 68 voix contre 58,

L’amendement I-1798 (Kévin Mauvieux, RN) : retrait de la réduction d’impôt pour toute association condamnée définitivement, quel qu’en soit le motif, rejeté le 15 octobre par 50 voix contre 44,

L’amendement I-357 (Corentin Le Fur, DR) : extension des infractions entraînant la perte des avantages fiscaux, rejeté le 16 octobre par 49 voix contre 38,

L’amendement I-1280 (Christelle d’Intorni, UDR) : même extension, élargie aux délits de presse, dont la diffamation, rejeté le 16 octobre par 47 voix contre 37.

D’autres amendements de même nature ont été retirés ou n’ont pas été défendus en séance. Un amendement de protection proposé par Romain Courbon (Socialistes), qui visait à interdire toute restriction de la réduction d’impôt pour des motifs portant atteinte à la liberté associative, a en revanche été rejeté par 58 voix contre 36 (scrutin n° …

title: Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.
content:
Legendary animal liberationist Barry Horne honoured by Northants Sabs.


Just weeks after publishing damning footage of the

Quorn Hunt killing a fox and training hounds

 to attack, saboteurs descended upon their prestigious opening meet – and completely ruined it.


Quorn Killers and Horne Haunts Quorn. Banners proudly displayed by Northants Sabs at the Quorn killers opening meet, 6 November, 2026. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


The day saw violence and abuse by the hunt, and resulted in the arrest of a terrierman who attempted to flee from police.


The day was dedicated to Barry Horne, a legendary activist who made the ultimate sacrifice for animal liberation.


Barry was involved in numerous daring rescue operations, helping to free animals destined for experimentation. He died following a series of hunger strikes intended to pressure Tony Blair’s Labour government over its promise to hold an inquiry into vivisection.


Barry Horne, 17 March 1990, rescuing 82 beagle puppies and 26 rabbits from Harlan Interfauna in Huntingdon. The site is now associated with MBR Acres Ltd, and the long-running Camp Beagle protests against the breeding of dogs for laboratory experiments for the petrochemical, chemical and pharmaceutical industries.


The government reneged on its promise, and animal rights activists reacted with fury in Barry’s name, and thousands more animals, including cats, rabbits and guinea pigs were liberated by activists during his hunger strikes.


Barry was also formerly a member of Northants Hunt Sabs. He died on November 5, 2001. His death radicalised and mobilised countless more animal liberations in his name.

In September 2026 multiple dogs were liberated from the MBR site

.


On Friday 6 November 2026, a day after the 25th anniversary of Barry’s death, the Quorn Hunt held their opening meet at its kennels in Kirby Bellars, Leicestershire.


The day did not quite go as they may have planned.


The Quorn Hunt October 2026, kill a fox and use the body to train the hounds. Notice the huntsman blowing for the kill over the hounds as they tear the body apart. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


On the back of the horrendous footage released only weeks earlier, Northants Hunt Sabs, including personal friends of Barry’s, turned out to stop the Quorn Hunt from killing on their watch.


Part time whipper-in and terrier ‘man’ Mickey Vaughn practising for the regional gurning championship.

Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


Northants Sabs truly smashed the day, hunt tempers flared as sabs arrived at the meet with banners and flags speaking truth about ‘trail hunting’.


Vaughan bravely attacking a woman. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


True to form, the hunters natural default for violence saw sabs attacked and pushed to the ground. Sabs stood their ground following the violent outburst and the hunt was soon put back in their box.


Vaughan being put back into his box. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Sabs stayed on the hunt throughout the day, leaving huntsman Joe Tesseyman struggling to find opportunities to hunt foxes with saboteurs on his case.


Huntsman Joe Tessyman on the run from sabs and police alike. Image Northants Hunt Sabs


Then, near Cream Gorse, the hunter became the hunted.


A Quorn terrierman was spotted leaving the covert on a quad bike, with officers from Leicestershire Police’s Rural Crime Team in hot pursuit.


The hot pursuit began with a terrierman fleeing from police after leaving the covert. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Mickey Vaughan, the terrierman and occasional whipper-in, attempted to slow the pursuing officers down by positioning his horse in the road. Police moved him aside and continued after the terrierman on the quad.


The quad overturned, and the terrierman was spotted running up Pasture Lane with a police officer hot on his tail behind.


You can’t park that there, mate. Image Northants Hunt Saboteurs.


Clearly a runner he was not.


He was promptly caught, cuffed and arrested.


At first I was all like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


We couldn’t possibly comment on what the arrest relates to and will not speculate, but lets hope they throw “obstructing an officer” at him whilst they are at it. Same goes for Vaughan who attempted to prevent the officer from pursuing the masked terrierman.


Then I was like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Meanwhile the mounted field dwindled out, no doubt many of whom left thoroughly embarrassed by the thuggish behaviour of this supposed-prestigious hunt …

title: Animal Rising Disrupts National Pig Awards in Central London Following Campaigner Arrests
content:
Animal Rising campaigners disrupted the National Pig Awards at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in central London this evening (16 November), while protesters outside blocked the main entrance. Police were called to the venue.

Despite enhanced security, six campaigners reached the event and were subsequently apprehended before being ejected from the hotel at approximately 7 pm. Around 70 protesters gathered outside as attendees arrived, holding placards reading “Free Luna” and “End Factory Farming”.

The group publicly declared its intention to shut down the awards last week, calling for Red Court, a pig factory farm in Suffolk, to release Luna, a mother pig whose life of confinement was filmed continuously for over a month by Animal Rising earlier this year. [1]

The investigation documented squalid conditions and illegal piglet thumping on the Red Tractor Assured farm. [2] Over 40,000 people have since signed a petition calling for Luna’s release to a sanctuary. [3]

The group filmed Luna confined in a narrow farrowing crate for five weeks, unable to turn around or take more than a step forward. A sanctuary has since offered her a home for the rest of her life. [4]

Red Court confirmed last week that Luna is once again in a farrowing crate. If the farm refuses to release her, she will remain there for approximately another month, confined with her newborn piglets, before she is removed and re-inseminated.

The farm has also rejected a proposed £5,000 donation to You Are Not Alone, an East Anglian charity supporting farmers’ mental health, in exchange for Luna’s release. [5]

Earlier today, Animal Rising announced that a third campaigner, Michelle Farnham, had been arrested on suspicion of burglary following the open rescue of three piglets (Leila, Nova and Maia) from Red Court.

Before the rescue, Animal Rising reported serious welfare concerns at the farm to the police, RSPCA and Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).

APHA, the body responsible for enforcing farmed animal welfare, informed Animal Rising that the farm’s conditions, including the illegal thumping of a piglet, were normal.

Farnham attended Stoke Newington Police Station at 10 am this morning. Her fellow rescuers, Thomas Cusick and Liam Shaughnessy, had previously reported themselves to the police and been arrested. [6]

Farnham, 26, Animal Rising’s Campaign Lead, attracted national attention in September when she spent 21 days and nights locked in a farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square, highlighting Luna’s story and the suffering of animals in factory farms. High-profile visitors included Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [7]

Animal Rising is campaigning for a government commitment to end UK factory farming by 2040.

author: Tobias Schalyo
title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt? 


Lea und Josias engagieren sich seit Jahren im Tierschutz und haben selbst zwei Katzen adoptiert.


PETA: Von Snacks über Pflege bis zu Alltagsprodukten: Wo findet ihr die Überraschungen, die es in euren Kalender schaffen?

  


Adventsome

: Die wichtigste Frage ist immer: Würden wir uns selbst darüber freuen, wenn wir morgens das Türchen öffnen? Das Produkt muss zudem vegan, unisex und alkoholfrei sein und auch darüber hinaus mit unseren Werten matchen!

author: Benji
title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Carrefour market, Carrefour city, supermarché, hypermarché… C’est vous qui choisissez !

Rayons conserve, frais, jouets ou même petit-déjeuner : saupoudrez les confettis dans le rayon de votre choix.

L’aquaculture et la pêche industrielle alourdissent ce total de plus de 7 milliards de poissons.

Pour faire face aux urgences éthiques, écologiques, sanitaires et sociales, L214 propose un objectif, consensuel et atteignable à moyen terme : diviser par deux le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation française d’ici 2030.

author: hsa_oryx
title: A Licence to Hunt: “Cruel, Inhumane and Selfish” Lauderdale Huntswoman Sentenced: 300 Hours’ Unpaid Work and Ten-Year Dog Ban
content:
Scotland’s first conviction under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023 has resulted in a substantial community sentence for ex-huntswoman Claire Bellamy, following evidence gathered by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.


Claire Bellamy after breaching the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Former Lauderdale Hunt master and huntswoman Claire Bellamy has been sentenced to 300 hours of unpaid work and banned from owning or keeping most dogs for ten years after being convicted of deliberately hunting a fox with hounds. 


Bellamy appeared at Paisley Sheriff Court on Monday 9th November, where Sheriff Gill imposed the maximum 300 hours of unpaid work permitted under a Community Payback Order, to be completed within 12 months. 


The sentence follows

Bellamy’s conviction in October

, the first secured under Scotland’s Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023.


The prosecution was made possible thanks to footage captured by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs, who have been documenting the ongoing illegal hunting in Scotland that has continued since the new licensing system became law. 


On the 4th January 2025 – almost 2 years after the new law came into force – Bellamy was hunting with approximately 17 hounds near Kirkton Woods, between Houston in Renfrewshire and Kilmacolm in Inverclyde.


The hunt had obtained a licence from NatureScot, the public body responsible for administering Scotland’s licensing scheme.


However, the licence did not give the hunt unrestricted permission to hunt foxes. It was also strictly restricted to a certain geographical area.


“The recording of the fox being chased by multiple hounds was particularly harrowing to watch.” Sheriff Gill


Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Footage captured by sabs, showed hounds hunting a fox into an open field beyond the boundaries specified in the licence. The dogs were not under control – also a requirement of the licence.


During the trial Sheriff Gill described the footage as harrowing and rejected Bellamy’s claim that she had not deliberately hunted the fox. 


A member of the Glasgow Hunt Sabs filming the hunt as they breach the NatureScot issued license.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs. 


At sentencing the sheriff praised the evidence of the witnesses, singling out the hunt sab who recorded the pursuit.


In contrast, Sheriff Gill addressing Bellamy directly described her actions as “

cruel, inhumane and selfish

”.


“Cruel, inhumane and selfish” – words used by Sheriff Gill to describe Bellamy during her sentencing hearing.  Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The court heard that Bellamy had taken part in approximately 1,500 hunts during her ‘career’ as a fox-killer. Despite this, she had shown no responsibility for what occurred that day.


A background report prepared by probation services for sentencing recorded that Bellamy believed she had done nothing wrong, showed no empathy towards the hunted fox, and considered herself to be the victim of an example being made.


The hounds chasing the fox.


“What you don’t understand is that the law is the law, and you are bound by the law.” Sheriff Gill.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


She also complained that Scotland’s legislation made hunting foxes more difficult, to which Sheriff Gill’s response was an astonished

“Ms Bellamy, that is the purpose of the legislation

”.


The court also made it clear that Bellamy was bound by the law regardless of whether she personally agreed with it.


The belief among the hunting community that their traditional animal cruelty should take precedence over legislation designed to protect wildlife was shattered in Paisley Sheriff courts.


Bellamy escaped a custodial sentence, although Sheriff Gill made it clear that prison was a genuine possibility.


Claire Bellamy hunting the fox in breach of the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The Community Payback Order requiring 300 hours of unpaid work was imposed as a direct alternative to imprisonment. Bellamy was further warned that failing to comply with the order could result in her returning to court and potentially receiving a custodial sentence. 


Bellamy was also disqualified from keeping dogs for 10 years, though there is an exemption which allowed her to retain her pet terrier (it would be a terrier wouldn’t it), and the collies she uses in her shepherding work.


Whilst Bellamy is no longer master of the Lauderdale Hunt, this didn’t stop the Lauderdale recently advertising a

‘Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week’

, which was quickly removed …

title: Animal Rights Radicals Destroy Several Hunting Hides in Italy amid Controversy over Hunting Law Reform
content:
Several hunting hides in Veneto have been wrecked and covered in anti-hunting graffiti. Images released by four hunting organisations show the Animal Liberation Front (ALF) signature and messages opposing the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation.

Vandalism against hunting facilities is making headlines in Italy once again. Several hunting hides (capanni da caccia) have been destroyed in the Veneto region, with their structures covered in graffiti opposing hunting and the reform of the legislation governing it in the country.

The incidents were publicly condemned this Wednesday, 4 November, by four organisations in the sector: the Cacciatori Veneti association, CONFAVI, ACR and FCR. The organisations released a gallery of photographs showing the damage to the facilities and the inscriptions left on their structures.

The graffiti includes the familiar ALF signature, standing for Animal Liberation Front (Animal Liberation Front), alongside messages calling for a boycott of the reform of Italy’s hunting law. The symbols visible in the images match those used in previous actions attributed to this animal rights movement.

The organisations accompanied the photographs with a strongly worded message directed at those responsible for the damage: “Destroying other people’s property does not defend any cause; it only demonstrates cowardice.”

The incident comes at a time of heightened tension over the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation. The bill seeks to amend Law 157/1992, which provides the basic legal framework for wildlife protection and the regulation of hunting.

The graffiti found on the Veneto hides directly links the property damage to this legislative controversy. However, the messages written on the facilities do not, on their own, identify the people who carried out the attacks. So far, no information has been released about arrests or police investigations relating to this incident either.

The appearance of the initials ALF recalls other incidents of vandalism recorded in Italy against facilities used by hunters.

One of the most notable previous incidents occurred in December 2019 in Montorfano, in the province of Brescia. On that occasion, eleven hunting hides in the municipalities of Rovato, Cologne and Palazzolo were wrecked. The damage was accompanied by threats and graffiti bearing the Animal Liberation Front signature.

More recently, in December 2025, six hides were destroyed in the Lower Valsugana area, between the municipalities of Grigno and Ospedaletto, in the province of Trento. The structures were found knocked down and marked with offensive messages directed at hunters. The ALF signature was also found in that case.

These previous incidents show that the destruction of hunting facilities is nothing new in Italy. The repeated attacks on hunting hides reveal a problem that goes beyond the war of words between supporters and opponents of hunting.

title: Termik santraller su kaynaklarını tüketiyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Özer Akdemir/Evrensel

Greenpeace işbirliğiyle Muğla’nın Milas ve Yatağan ilçeleri ile Maraş Elbistan’da yürüttükleri araştırmaya ilişkin konuşan gazeteci Doğu Eroğlu, kömürlü termik santrallerin sağlık üzerindeki etkilerinin çok sayıda çalışmaya konu olduğunu ancak su kaynakları ve suya erişim üzerindeki etkilerinin daha az incelendiğini belirtti. Araştırma kapsamında bilimsel çalışmaları taradıklarını ve bölgelerde yaşayan, suya erişim güçlüğü çeken çiftçiler ve yerel halkla görüştüklerini ifade eden Eroğlu, her iki havzada yaşanan su sorunlarını belgelemeye çalıştıklarını söyledi.

Elbistan’da termik santrallerin çalışması ve linyit madenciliği için kullanılan su miktarına dikkat çeken Eroğlu, “Elbistan’daki termik santrallere yıllık tahsis edilmiş su miktarı yaklaşık 100 milyon metreküp. Yine aynı havzada yapılan madencilik çalışmaları için havzadan uzaklaştırılması gereken su da yılda 100 milyon metreküp. Yani sadece termik santralin çalışması ve madencilik yapılabilmesi için orada harcanan ve o bölgeden uzaklaştırılan suyun toplamı yıllık 200 milyon metreküp” dedi. Kömür çıkarılabilmesi için maden sahalarının kurutulması gerektiğini belirten Eroğlu, yeraltı sularının drenaj kuyuları açılarak pompalarla dışarı atıldığını söyledi. Bu durumun özellikle maden sahalarının çevresinde tarım yapan çiftçilerin suya erişimini zorlaştırdığını kaydetti.

Yeraltı sularının çekilmesi nedeniyle çiftçilerin daha derin sondajlar açmak zorunda kaldığını kaydeden Eroğlu, “Özellikle o havzaların etrafında çiftçilikle uğraşanların suya erişebilmesi için 200-250 metreye varan derin sondajlar kurması gerekiyor. Bu sondajlardan çıkan suyla çiftçilik yapabilmek için aylık 100 bin lirayı bulan, 200 bin lirayı bulan, çok suya ihtiyaç olan dönemde 300 bin lirayı bulan elektrik faturalarına katlanması gerekiyor” diye konuştu. Bu maliyetlerin tarımsal üretimi ağır biçimde etkilediğini ifade eden Eroğlu, “En ciddi, en artık karşı çıkılamaz bulgulardan bir tanesi bizim rastladığımız tarımın, sulu tarımın bitme noktasına gelmesi, özellikle linyit madenciliği yapılan bu havzalarda. Çünkü çok maliyetli” ifadelerini kullandı.

Termik santrallere su sağlanmasına öncelik verilmesinin bölge halkının yaşamını etkilediğini belirten Eroğlu, birçok köyde insanların kendi ihtiyaçlarını karşılayacak suya erişemediğini söyledi. Eroğlu, "İnsanlar kendi hayvanlarını sulayamıyorlar, yaşamak için gereksinim duydukları bahçelere su veremiyorlar. Hatta bunları geçtim, içecek su bulamadıkları dönemler oluyor. Sular tankerlerle taşınıyor. Başka bölgelerden su satın almak zorunda kalıyorlar” dedi. Yaşananların yalnızca tarım ve hayvancılıkla sınırlı olmadığını vurgulayan Eroğlu, suya erişim sorununun bölgedeki yaşam koşullarını ağırlaştırdığını belirterek, “İnsanların o bölgede yaşamasını güçleştiren, o bölgeden insanları her gün göçe zorlayan, oradaki yaşam koşullarını güçleştiren bir suya erişim zorluğundan bahsediyoruz” diye konuştu.

İklim değişikliği nedeniyle su kaynaklarının daha kıt hale geldiğine dikkat çeken Eroğlu, yağış rejiminin değiştiğini, kurak dönemlerin uzadığını ve suyun daha fazla korunması gereken bir kaynak haline geldiğini belirtti. Termik santrallerin su kaynaklarından yararlanma konusunda öncelikli konumunun devam etmesinin bölgedeki yaşamı olumsuz etkilediğini belirten Eroğlu, “Termik santrallerin bu öncelikli konumu o bölgelerden uzaklaştırılmadan, o bölgelerden termik santrallerin su tüketimi kaldırılmadan bu bölgelerdeki yaşamın normal hattında ilerlemesi, kendini iyileştirmesi, iklim değişikliğine adapte olması ya da iklim değişikliğinin etkilerini bir şekilde absorbe etmesi mümkün olmayacak gibi gözüküyor” dedi.

Kömürlü termik santrallerin sağlık üzerindeki etkilerinin geçmişte de bilindiğini ancak zamanla bu etkilerin daha görünür hale geldiğini hatırlatan Eroğlu, su kaynakları üzerindeki etkilerin de benzer biçimde değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Termik santrallerin ürettiği enerjinin maliyetinin yalnızca yakılan kömür ve üretilen elektrik üzerinden hesaplanamayacağını ifade eden Eroğlu, “Her yeni ortaya çıkan yeni yüz aslında termik santrallerin ürettiği enerjinin maliyetinin sadece o piyasanın ölçmeye çalıştığı ‘şu kadar ton kömür yaktık ve karşılığında bu kadar elektrik enerjisi ürettik’ denkleminden çok daha geniş bir etki alanına sahip olduğunu gösteriyor. Su da aynı şekilde” dedi. Kömürlü termik santrallerden vazgeçilmesi için hükümetin gerekli verilere sahip olduğunu belirten Eroğlu, santrallerin devreden …

author: Unknown
title: COP31: Women’s organizations criticize inequitable distribution of climate finance
content:
Criticism of international climate finance is mounting at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya. Women’s rights and environmental organizations accuse industrialized countries of failing to adequately meet their financial commitments and disadvantaging the populations most affected by the climate crisis in the allocation of funds. They say the focus is not only on the amount of funding pledged, but also on who decides how it is used and which initiatives actually gain access to international climate funds.


On Thursday, the Women and Gender Constituency (WGC), a coalition of women’s rights and gender organizations involved in the UN climate negotiations, highlighted significant shortcomings in funding for climate adaptation measures, the participation of local communities, and a socially just energy transition. Together with other civil society organizations, it is calling for public climate finance to be directed specifically toward the people and communities most severely affected by the consequences of global warming.


Little funding reaches women-led initiatives


Figures from the Dutch environmental and development organization Both ENDS illustrate how unequally international climate finance is distributed. According to the organization, only around 0.1 percent of global climate finance goes to initiatives supporting women and the environment. Women’s organizations and local communities developing their own solutions to the impacts of the climate crisis thus receive only a tiny fraction of the available funding.


The Global Alliance for Green and Gender Action (GAGGA) points to another figure: Just 0.22 percent of climate-related official development finance reaches women’s rights organizations. Although the two figures are based on different definitions and scopes, the organizations argue that both highlight the structural barriers faced particularly by smaller initiatives.


International climate funds are largely administered through governments, development banks, and major institutions. For local women’s organizations, complicated application procedures, demanding administrative requirements, and short funding periods often pose significant obstacles. Daan Robben, who is responsible for locally led climate finance at Both ENDS, criticizes the notion that merely promising public participation is sufficient. Instead, women’s organizations and local communities need direct access to flexible, long-term funding.


Adaptation Fund falls far short of funding target


The funding gap is also evident in the international Adaptation Fund, which supports developing countries in addressing the impacts of climate change that have already occurred or are anticipated. Among other things, the fund supports projects aimed at protecting communities from droughts and floods, securing water supplies, and strengthening local livelihoods. At a high-level funding meeting on November 17, only Spain, Germany, and Ireland announced new contributions. Together with earlier pledges from Estonia, Portugal, and the Belgian region of Brussels, the announced contributions totaled US$50 million by the following day.


This means that only one-sixth of the annual minimum target of $300 million has been met. In a joint statement issued on November 18, the WGC and other civil society coalitions described the contributions as wholly inadequate. They called on industrialized countries to provide additional funding before the climate conference concludes.


The scale of the funding gap becomes clear when compared with actual needs. According to calculations by the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), developing countries will require approximately $305 billion annually by 2035 to adapt to climate change. Taking inflation into account, this figure could rise to around $420 billion. The organizations emphasize that additional funding must not lead to further indebtedness among the affected countries. Instead of loans, they are calling for grants that do not have to be repaid and can be used as directly as possible for local adaptation measures.


Public responsibility instead of dependence on investors


Underlying the dispute over funding is a fundamental question of international climate policy. Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement obliges industrialized countries to provide financial support to developing countries for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and adapting to the impacts of climate change. Women’s organizations warn …

author: Amy Goodman
title: COP31 Declared a Failure as Declaration Text Excludes Mention of Fossil Fuels
content:
“I do not bear good news,” Panama’s environment minister said. “We are being held hostage by the petroleum mafia.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In our closing broadcast from Antalya, Turkey, the site of the 31st annual U.N. climate change summit, we take a look at what has — and hasn’t — been accomplished at this latest attempt to reach an international framework to stem the impacts of climate change.

“This COP was being touted as a COP of implementation, but what it has become is a COP of betrayal and a COP of distraction,” laments environmental justice advocate Harjeet Singh, the founding director of India’s Satat Sampada Climate Foundation. He’s joined on Democracy Now! by Meena Raman of Friends of the Earth Malaysia and Nafkote Dabi of Oxfam International as a number of NGOs announce their rejection of the conference’s final declaration text, which contains no mentions of fossil fuels or clear financial commitments from polluter countries.

“At the heart of the negotiations right now lies money,” says Dabi. “What rich countries, especially the EU, [are] saying is, ‘There is no money at home.’ But we know there’s money. They can tax the richest. They can tax the excess profit of fossil fuel companies. They can tax private jets. They can tax extreme wealth and raise the funds that’s needed to support communities.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman. We’re broadcasting from Turkey on the final scheduled day of the global U.N. climate summit, known as COP31.

Climate advocacy groups and Indigenous organizations from across the world have slammed this gathering as the “worst COP ever” and rejected the latest draft text as a “disaster,” urging developing countries to reject the latest draft text.

Meanwhile, at a news conference just before our broadcast, Panama’s Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro has threatened to block any final agreement if it doesn’t include a cap on oil production. Earlier this week, he spoke out forcefully against the role of what he described as the “petroleum mafia.”

JUAN CARLOS NAVARRO: I do not bear good news. We are being held hostage by the petroleum mafia.

AMY GOODMAN: And this is Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama’s environment minister, speaking just before we went to air, flanked by representatives from Finland and Vanuatu, Belgium, Ivory Coast, France, Guatemala and other countries.

JUAN CARLOS NAVARRO: We have come together because we feel that the COP can still be saved if we focus on six key issues for our final declaration that clarifies for the world where we must go.

The first is that science must be the foundation. Everything we do must be based on science.

Second, we need a clear transition away from fossil fuels. It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it. We need to tell the truth and to speak clearly. We must transition away from fossil fuels in an orderly manner, if we are to confront climate change.

The third point for us, which is very important, is that fair contributions to climate finance must come from those with greatest responsibility. You pollute, you pay. It’s actually rather simple. You cause the problem, you must help to fix it. If you are the biggest emitter of CO2, if you are the biggest producers or consumers of petroleum, then you must contribute to solve this problem and these issues.

AMY GOODMAN: Earlier today, in a packed room for the press, the Climate Action Network, which encompasses over 2,500 civil society groups worldwide, as speakers detailed the failures of the COP, there were activists in the room, journalists and many others representing this COP31. The activists on the stage called out the European Union and other developed nations for their obstruction. The room repeatedly broke out into chants of “shame.” The moderator of CAN called the draft text a “disgrace” and introduced speakers.

DANNI TAAFFE: Tasneem Essop, executive director of Climate Action Network International.

TASNEEM ESSOP: There is nothing on the table that protects people or addresses the priorities of the Global South. In fact, the opposite is true. … This COP has had the highest number of lobbyists — fossil fuel lobbyists, AI lobbyists, CCUS lobbyists, CDR …
