Sözcü TV’ye yönelik müdahale, basın özgürlüğüne, halkın haber alma hakkına ve farklı görüşlerin kamuoyuna ulaşabilmesine yönelik kabul edilemez bir müdahaledir. Bizler özgür basının ve halkın doğru bilgiye ulaşma hakkının savunucusu olmaya devam edeceğiz. Sansüre ve baskıya karşı Sözcü TV emekçileriyle dayanışmamızı sürdüreceğiz. Kamu yararını, halkın haber alma hakkını, gazetecilik mesleğini hedef alan, Türkiye’de demokrasiyi yerle bir eden, anayasal hakları yok sayan otoriter tek adam rejimi adım adım tahkim etmeye dönük yapıldığı malum olan uygulamaların hayata geçirilmesi kabul edilemez. Foncu hırsızlar, yağmacılar gönüllü iadelerle işledikleri suçtan yırtarak veya aflarını isteyerek halk arasında serbestçe dolaşırken sesini çıkaranın, itiraz edenin gerçekleri, doğruları kamu adına yayınlayanların sabaha karşı kapısına dayanan bu düzende hiçbir hakkımızın güvence altında olmadığını kamuoyunun bilgisine sunarız. Artık bıçak kemiğe dayandığı, sözün bittiği yerdeyiz" dedi.

Daha sonra konuşan ÇGD Bursa Yürütme Kurulu üyesi Hatice Nur Derya, "Halk TV’nin ardından Sözcü’ye de kayyum atanması, Türkiye’de medya ikliminin kara kışa döndüğünü gösteriyor. Kayyum kararının gerekçesi, gözaltıların hukuki dayanağı ve TMSF’ye verilen yetkilerin sınırları gecikmeden açıklanmalıdır. Hangi haberin yayımlanacağına, hangi sorunun sorulacağına ve kime söz verileceğine gazeteciler karar vermelidir. Haber kaynaklarının gizliliği, çalışanların iş güvencesi ve haber merkezlerinin editoryal bağımsızlığı korunmalıdır. Yetkilileri kayyum kararını kaldırmaya çağırıyoruz. Sözcü çalışanlarıyla dayanışma içindeyiz. Bu günler de geçer. O gün geldiğinde, bugün gerçeğin peşinden giden gazeteciler de halkın o gerçeği öğrenmesini engelleyen kararlar da hatırlanacak" dedi.

Eylemde konuşan KESK Genel Sekreteri Sevgi Yılmaz, "Halk düşmanı, emek düşmanı, otoriter rejimler halkın haber alma hakkından korkarlar. Onun için de basın otoriter rejimlerde her zaman tehdit altındadır. Her zaman gazetecileri susturmaya çalışırlar. Türkiye Cumhuriyeti tarihinde de aslında hiç iç açıcı bir tablo yok. Bu baskıları niye yapıyorlar çünkü fon vurgununun yazılmasından rahatsızlar. Bu ülkenin Milli Eğitim Bakanı bizim çocuklarımızı MESEM'lerde ölüme gönderiyor bunun haber yapılmasından rahatsız. Bizim en temel meseleler hakkında bilgi sahibi olmamızdan rahatsız. Haber alme hakkımız, seçme ve seçilme hakkımız ve bütçe hakkımız için birleşmekten başka çaremiz yok. DİSK, KESK, TMMOB ve TTB olarak bu haklarımız için 12 Aralık'ta Ankara'dayız" dedi.

CHP'nin 38. Olağan Kurultayı'na ilişkin ceza davasında 2 yıl 1 ay hapis ve siyasi yasak cezası alan Yeni Parti Bursa İl Başkanı Nihat Yeşiltaş ise şunları söyledi, "İktidarın TELE1 Halk TV ve Sözcü TV’den rahatsız olduğunu ve bu nedenle kayyum atadı. Bunun tek bir sebebi var. O da halkın haber alma özgürlüğünü engellemektir. Çünkü bu iktidar foncuların, talancıların, rantçıların düzeni, bu düzenin içinde kurdukları bütün yapıları deşifre olmasın, halk öğrenmesin, millet öğrenmesin diye kendilerine muhalif olan sadece ve sadece gerçekleri yazan basını susturmaya çalışıyorlar. Hepimize bir görev düşüyor. Biz basına sahip çıkacağız."

Hakkında verilen hukuksuz karara ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulunan Yeşiltaş, “Dün Ankara'da bir hukuk garabeti yaşandı. Delil yok. Kanıt yok. Dosyanın içi bomboş ve biz savunma yaparken saat 10.00'dan saat 17.00'a kadar sadece bizi dinleyen merak edip hiçbir soru bile sorulmayan ve daha önceden artık kararı bile verilmiş, sonuçları bile belli olmuş bir hukuk tiyatrosuyla karşılaştık. Burada hukukun nasıl siyasallaştığını orada gördük. Bugün aynı dosyadan aynı ithamlarla yargılandığımız birlikte yargılandığımız kişilerin İzmir'e ihanet eden İzmir'in iradesini satan Cemil Tugay beraat etti. Ve bizler siyasi yasak aldık. İktidara karşı direnenlerin, onurlu bir mücadele ortaya koyanların ve yapılan haksızlıklara karşı yoksulluğa, açlığa, sefalete karşı bir direnci bir itirazı ortaya …

author: Katie Myers
title: Trump Admin Proposes Easing Protections for Coal Miners From Black Lung Disease
content:
Miners’ advocates said revisions to a Biden-era rule on silica exposure would weaken already insufficient protections.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Coal mining is dangerous and takes a toll on the body, but a miner working underground can earn enough to buy a house, drive a nice car, and send the kids to college. There was a time when John Robinson thought the trade-off was worth it. No longer. He was diagnosed with black lung disease at age 47, a consequence of inhaling toxic silica dust in the mines of Virginia.

“These companies will bait you in with this big money,” said Robinson, who is now 60 and vice president of the National Black Lung Association. “When you get down and out, well, guess what? You’re like an old wore-out tire on the car or something. They’ll throw you to the side ’cause you ain’t worth nothing.”

For more than 50 years, coal miners, their families, and advocates have pressed the federal government for stricter limits on silica exposure, stronger enforcement of rules meant to protect miners, and improved health benefits for those disabled by the disease. In 2024, the Biden administration set the permissible exposure limit for respirable crystalline silica at 50 micrograms per cubic meter of air, matching the Occupational Safety and Health Administration threshold for workers in other industries. The rule was finalized in 2024, with coal companies required to comply beginning in April 2025.

That regulation was meant to update protections in coal mines and in what regulators call metal and nonmetal mines, which extract everything from copper and critical minerals to stone, sand, and gravel. All of them carry a risk of inhaling silica dust, whose fine particles can lodge deep in the lungs. But research over the past two decades has shown that Central Appalachian coal miners have experienced an acute increase in exposure and the most severe forms of lung disease associated with it, including progressive massive fibrosis.

Though the Biden-era revision wasn’t perfect, advocates like Robinson and his wife Vonda Robinson, who is president of the National Black Lung Association, were hopeful. It seemed as though decades of organizing for a stronger standard were finally coming to an end. But a federal appeals court put the rule on hold last year while it considered legal challenges filed by the mining industry. Now the Mine Safety and Health Administration wants to revise the rule.

Its proposal would retain the 50-microgram silica limit while changing several requirements governing how mines monitor exposure and protect workers. Brendan Muckian-Bates, a policy analyst with Appalachian Citizens’ Law Center, said those revisions could substantially weaken the protections behind the stricter limit.

Black lung is the common name for coal worker’s pneumoconiosis, an incurable, progressive, and fatal respiratory disease caused by inhaling coal dust and fine silica particles, which can cause severe inflammation in the lungs. Over time, that irritant scars and stiffens lung tissue, making respiration increasingly difficult until many of those afflicted with it cannot breathe at all.

In the 1960s and 1970s, according to the National Institutes of Health, as many as 1 in 3 miners with more than 25 years of work experience were testing positive for black lung. The United Mine Workers of America agitated for stricter protections again the disease, and in 1969, Congress passed the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Act, which required regular inspections. Disease rates plummeted to a historic low in the 2000s, only to begin climbing again. Rates of black lung are now at a 50-year high and still climbing. A study led by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, or NIOSH, found these increases across all age groups, including miners in their 20s and 30s, although rates remained highest among those who had spent decades underground. In routine health screenings by the agency during the past three years, more than 1 in 3 miners in Central Appalachia once again tested positive for the disease, making the epidemic into a U-shaped curve.

The new rule was published in the Federal Register on November 12 and will be open for public comment until January 11. Although the stricter limit of 50 micrograms remains, Muckian-Bates said the fine print matters: Other changes in the rule …

author: infolibre
title: Συγκεντρώσεις για τη Διεθνή Ημέρα Τρανς Θυμάτων, Παρασκευή 20/11
content:
Συγκεντρώσεις καλούνται σε Αθήνα και Θεσσαλονίκη για την 20η Νοέμβρη, διεθνή ημέρα τρανς θυμάτων. Συλλογικότητες, ομάδες, οργανώσεις καλούν σε μία ημέρα διεκδίκησης και μνήμης.


Αθήνα:

 Στις 18:00 στην πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος


Θεσσαλονίκη:

 Στις 18:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


ΑΘΗΝΑ


ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗ


20 Νοέμβρη


ΗΜΕΡΑ ΜΝΗΜΗΣ ΤΡΑΝΣ ΘΥΜΑΤΩΝ


Διεκδικούμε φροντίδα // μέριμνα // συμπερίληψη // αποδοχή για τα τρανς αδέρφια μας


Και αυτή η 20η Νοέμβρη θα είναι μέρα μνήμης και διεκδίκησης,


Επειδή μέσα σε έναν χρόνο έχουμε χάσει 273 τρανς αδέρφια μας, χωρίς να μπορούμε καν να υπολογίσουμε τις αυτοκτονίες, καθώς συχνά οι άνθρωποι που αυτοκτονούν καταγράφονται με το φύλο που τους αποδόθηκε κατά τη γέννηση


Επειδή κάθε 32 ώρες ένα τρανς ή φυλοδιαφορετικό άτομο δολοφονείται σε κάποιο σημείο αυτού του κόσμου, με 106 δολοφονημένους ανθρώπους μόνο στη Βραζιλία


Επειδή, από αυτούς τους ανθρώπους, ένα στα τρία άτομα είναι γυναίκα σεξεργάτρια


Επειδή οι τραμπικής έμπνευσης παραλογισμοί περί «woke ατζέντας» και στις δύο πλευρές του Ατλαντικού οπλίζουν το χέρι φασιστών και ομοτρανσφοβικών


Επειδή το σύστημα εκπαιδεύει κοινωνίες ολόκληρες στη ματσίλα, την τοξική αρρενωπότητα και το στερεοτυπικό έμφυλο δίπολο, όπου οι τρανς υπάρξεις εξοβελίζονται, περιθωριοποιούνται, υφίστανται συνεχή βία


Επειδή οι αστικές κυβερνήσεις όχι μόνο δεν ευνοούν, αλλά αντιθέτως βάζουν κωλύματα και απαγορεύουν τη φυλομετάβαση σε ανήλικα τρανς άτομα


Επειδή σε μια περίοδο πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, οι δημόσιοι πόροι κατευθύνονται σε θηριώδεις στρατιωτικούς εξοπλισμούς και όχι σε ερευνητικά ιατρικά προγράμματα ή στην κατάλληλη εκπαίδευση του ιατρικού και νοσηλευτικού προσωπικού ως προς τη φροντίδα που οφείλουν να παρέχουν σε τρανς ανθρώπους


Επειδή δεν έχει εισαχθεί ακόμα το μάθημα της σεξουαλικής αγωγής στα σχολεία με ισότιμη παρουσίαση όλων των ταυτοτήτων φύλου, έκφρασης φύλου και σεξουαλικότητας


Επειδή οι υπηρεσίες υγείας (τεστ παπ, μαστογραφίες) δεν είναι απεμφυλοποιημένες, ώστε να είναι προσβάσιμες σε όλα τα άτομα


Επειδή δεν έχει εισαχθεί η χρήση ουδέτερης ως προς το φύλο γλώσσας στα κρατικά έγγραφα, ώστε να μην απαιτείται η δήλωση ταυτότητας φύλου


Επειδή παραμένουν οι διακρίσεις για το δικαίωμα στη γονεϊκότητα


Αυτόν τον Νοέμβρη, με τις φωνές της Πάολα Ρεβενιώτη και της Νικόλ να ηχούν στα αυτιά μας, βγαίνουμε στον δρόμο και διεκδικούμε φροντίδα, μέριμνα, συμπερίληψη και αποδοχή για όλα τα τρανς/φυλοδιαφορετικά αδέρφια μας.


Καλούμε αυτή την Παρασκευή 20 Νοέμβρη στις 18:00 στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


REclaim PRIDE-Thessaloniki


273 θύματα σε όλο τον κόσμο θρηνούμε τη φετινή Διεθνή Ημέρα Μνήμης Τρανς Θυμάτων. Για άλλη μια φορά η

μεγάλη πλειονότητα ήταν τρανς γυναίκες ή θηλυκότητες (95%) και μαύρα ή μη λευκά τρανς άτομα (75%). Η αντι-τρανς εκστρατεία της ακροδεξιάς παγκοσμίως οπλίζει το χέρι των δολοφόνων, είτε αυτοί είναι μέσα στο σπίτι των τρανς (20% των δραστών ήταν ερωτικοί σύντροφοι των θυμάτων) είτε έξω από αυτό.


Όσο και αν η τρανσφοβική βία είναι επικίνδυνη και τρομακτική, τα τρανς άτομα θα συνεχίσουν προπαντός να χαίρονται το φύλο με το οποίο αυτοπροσδιορίζονται. Αυτό δεν μπορεί να μας το στερήσει κανένας.


Διεκδικούμε το δικαίωμά μας να υπάρχουμε με όποιο φύλο μας εκφράζει.


Διεκδικούμε τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα που θα έπρεπε να έχουμε ήδη.


Διεκδικούμε να είμαστε ο εαυτός μας. Και θα είμαστε!


Όλες, όλα και όλοι την Παρασκευή 20 Νοεμβρίου στις 18:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου για την Πορεία της Διεθνούς Ημέρας Τρανς Μνήμης. Θα μας βρείτε εκεί με το πανό και τις σημαίες μας.


ομάδα Sylvia Rivera – για ένα κινηματικό Thessaloniki Pride


Συγκέντρωση για την ημέρα μνήμης trans θυμάτων


Αν τα παιδιά σας είναι τρανς και δε σας το λένε, είναι γιατί φοβούνται τη βίαιη αντίδρασή σας. Κουράστηκαν να σας εξηγούν. Κουράστηκαν τον έλεγχό σας και τον έλεγχο της κοινωνίας. Και δε θα σταματήσουν να είναι, είτε το ξέρετε είτε όχι. Το λιγότερο που έχετε να κάνετε είναι να τα προστατέψετε.


Κάθε χρόνο διαβάζουμε ονόματα που αρνούμαστε να ξεχάσουμε. Η 20ή Νοέμβρη μνημονεύει τα τρανς αδέρφια μας που δολοφονήθηκαν από το τρανσφοβικό σύστημα. Δηλαδή, από ανθρώπους που ενεργά μισούν, πιέζουν, κυνηγούν ή λοιδορούν την ύπαρξη των τρανς ανθρώπων. Ξεκίνησε το 1999 ως μια πρωτοβουλία ενάντια στη διαγραφή των τρανς ατόμων από τη συλλογική μνήμη, από ακτιβίστριες όπως η Gwendolyn Ann Smith, έπειτα από την αυξανόμενη δολοφονική τάση ενάντια σε τρανς άτομα. Σήμερα, η ημέρα αυτή σηματοδοτεί μια διεθνή πρωτοβουλία ενάντια στην τρανσφοβική βία.


Κάθε χρόνο θρηνούμε αμέτρητα …

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: Votar con las tripas, oh sí.
content:
Tiene que quedar claro: yo no hago campaña por la abstención. La abstención electoral no necesita de mi incentivo. Existe sin pegar ni un solo cartel, sin llamamientos, sin promesas. Más o menos lo veo de este modo, ya que entre un treinta y un cuarenta por ciento del censo, comicio tras comicio, prefieren agarrarse otra cosa que agarrar la papeleta. Así que muchacho/a, vamos a ver las opciones.

Hace unos días escuchaba el discurso de un candidato de izquierdas. Venía a decir, yo lo explico mucho mejor que él, que con el rollo del voto útil, acabas votando por gente que no conoces, y que no sabes de qué van, y con los que no estás de acuerdo. Con el voto útil, no votas por aquello que te gusta realmente, si no por lo menos malo que se te ocurre. Y entonces el candidato de izquierdas, que teme que muchos de esos votos de izquierdas acaben en el PSOE, instaba no a votar con la razón, si no a votar con el corazón, con el sentimiento, con el deseo. Pedía que no se hiciesen cálculos raros para evitar que salieran los fascistas, si no que echasen la papeleta al candidato simpático, afín, cercano, que por supuesto, era él. En fin, que me se puso la cara como a mi madre, un día que comíamos en la terraza y se encontró una cagada de golondrina en la sopa. Cuando se la estaba acabando.

¡Pero si la gente vota con las tripas, joder! Porque si de sentimientos irracionales se trata, la mayoría de la gente es capaz de votar por la derecha. Vamos, que es lo que van a hacer. Por muy misterioso que me resulte, eso del voto inútil no tiene que ver con un cálculo racional de intereses. Tiene que ver con una nube de hormonas que oscurecen el entendimiento y te convierten en gilipollas, si ya no lo eres.

Decía además ese candidato, y mucho ojo, que no estoy en contra de él ni mucho menos, que el día de las elecciones, es el único día en el que el voto de un limpiabotas vale lo mismo que el de un ricachón. Y es verdad. Ese voto vale lo mismo, o sea NADA. Por eso un millonario, no vota. ¿O acaso habéis visto el día de las elecciones, a pie de urna, a algún distinguido banquero, líder de la patronal o altísimo cargo de multinacional? ¿Para qué quiere votar ese bribón si con una llamada de teléfono a la persona adecuada, consigue lo que le interesa?

En cuando al trabajador/a de sueldo micromínimo, posiblemente se abstenga porque percibe que su vida sigue al día siguiente igual de chunga: despertador a las seis, y jornada diabólica por cuatro perras. Por eso, puede que el día de las elecciones, en lugar de votar prefiera hacerse una paja. Porque al menos al acabar le queda algo en la mano.

author: Unknown
title: Şenzen'e Berlin'den yanıt: “Yeni Yalta'ya hayır, Avrupa masada olacak"
content:
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin ve Şi Cinping'in 19 Kasım Şenzen zirvesi ve zirveden çıkan bildiriye en kapsamlı siyasi karşılık Berlin'den geldi. Almanya Başbakanı Friedrich Merz, Ukrayna'yı destekleyen ülkeler toplantısında “Yalta formatında bir düzenleme barış getirmez” dedi: “Yalta'da Avrupa bölündü, paylaşıldı. Bunun yeniden olmasına izin vermeyeceğiz.”


Berlin: "Odada Ukrayna olmadan Ukrayna, Avrupa olmadan Avrupa konuşulamaz"


Berlin'deki buluşma, Fransa ve Britanya'nın öncülüğünde Mart 2025'te oluşturulan “Gönüllüler Koalisyonu”nun (Coalition of the Willing) zirvesiydi. Berlin'deki zirvenin Şenzen'le aynı güne denk gelmesi tesadüf değildi. Financial Times'ın Alman hükümet yetkililerine dayandırdığı bilgiye göre, Gönüllüler Koalisyonu'nun toplantısı, Trump, Putin ve Şi'nin görüşmesine hızlı, ortaklaşa ve hazırlıklı bir yanıt verebilmek amacıyla özellikle bu tarihe planlanmıştı.


Ukrayna'nın güvenliğini desteklemek ve olası bir ateşkesin uygulanmasına yönelik güvenceler geliştirmek amacıyla kurulan koalisyon, Türkiye de dahil olmak üzere 36 ülkeyi kapsıyor. Adı, 2003'te ABD öncülüğündeki Irak işgaline katılan ülkeler için kullanılan “Coalition of the Willing” ifadesini çağrıştırsa da iki oluşumun amaçları ve siyasi bağlamları farklı. Berlin toplantısı, Şenzen Bildirisi'ne verilen yanıtın yalnızca birkaç Avrupa başkentinden değil, önceden örgütlenmiş uluslararası bir diplomatik girişimden geldiğini de gösterdi.


Fransa, Almanya, Britanya'nın ortak açıklaması


Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron ise Şenzen bildirisinin başlı başına yeni bir dünya düzeni getirdiği yorumuna katılmadı:


“Bunun dünyanın yeniden düzenlenmesi anlamına geldiğini sanmıyorum.”


Macron Avrupa güvenliği kapsamında Berlin toplantısını öne çıkardı.


Britanya Başbakanı Andy Burnham da ilkeyi açıkça ifade etti:


“Ukrayna odada olmadan Ukrayna hakkında, Avrupa temsil edilmeden Avrupa güvenliği hakkında karar alınamaz.”


Berlin yalnızca tepki açıklamakla kalmadı. Almanya, Fransa, Britanya ve Ukrayna liderlerinin ortak bildirisinde, Rusya'nın saldırıları kınandı; ateşkes sonrasında Ukrayna'ya hukuken bağlayıcı güvenlik güvenceleri, Avrupa öncülüğünde çokuluslu bir güç ve ABD ile eşgüdüm içinde ateşkesin denetlenmesi seçenekleri sıralandı. Rusya'ya ekonomik baskının sürdürülmesi ve enerji ateşkesi istendi.


Görünürdeki farklılıklara karşın, Berlin Bildirisi bir Washington–Avrupa kopuşunu haber vermiyor. Berlin zirvesine katılan Trump'ın özel temsilcileri Jared Kushner ve Steve Witkoff da Avrupalıların görüşme masasında yer almasını desteklediler. Kushner Berlin bildirisiyle aynı doğrultuda konuştu: 


“Avrupa'nın masada olmasının adil, uzun vadeli ve kalıcı barış için zorunlu olduğuna inanıyoruz”


Putin de Şenzen'de Avrupa'nın Ukrayna müzakerelerine katılmasına karşı olmadığını, ancak bunun koşullarını önce Moskova'da görüşmek istediğini söyledi.


“Avrupalılar olmadan Avrupa'nın güvenliğini tartışmanın anlamsız olduğunu biliyoruz.”


Ardından da şunu ekledi:


“Avrupa'nın bu görüşmelere ne getireceğini anlamamız gerekiyor.”


Avrupa'da farklı görüşler 


NATO Genel Sekreteri Mark Rutte, nükleer güçlerin görüşmesini olağan bulduğunu ve yeni bir Yalta'dan endişelenmediğini söyledi.


Litvanya Cumhurbaşkanı Gitanas Nausėda ise zirveyi dünyanın yeniden paylaşılması olarak yorumlamaktan kaçındı, ama Çin ve Rusya'nın veto yetkisini sürekli korurken BM reformunun öncülüğüne soyunmasını sorguladı.

author: Chris Walker
title: Musk Says He’s Not MAGA After Spending Nearly Half a Billion Backing Republicans
content:
After years of promoting Trump’s far right agenda, Musk claimed that he is actually “quite moderate.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

After years of promoting Donald Trump’s “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) agenda, Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he no longer considers himself part of the pro-Trump movement.

Speaking remotely at The New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk attempted to suggest that he had never harbored such viewpoints — despite his stint as the head of the Trump administration’s so-called “Department of Government Efficiency,” or DOGE.

“I’m not MAGA. … I’m not sure what MAGA means, but I don’t think I’m — like, if it means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that,” the multi-billionaire said.

Musk further claimed that he prefers “checks and balances” in government, and described himself as “quite moderate.”

Musk added that he felt “pretty foolish for how much money I spent in the midterms” in support of MAGA-aligned Republicans.

Elon Musk claims he’s “not MAGA” pic.twitter.com/3hZZQgSPaN

Musk’s rejection of MAGA on Wednesday is a stark departure from his attitude over the past two years. In fact, Musk embraced MAGA while campaigning for Trump in 2024, describing himself as “dark MAGA” while wearing a black version of the red hat often donned by the president.

Musk didn’t just make speeches in support of the movement — he jubilantly championed MAGA, jumping wildly on campaign stages in rockstar fashion, with then-candidate Donald Trump alongside him.

His “dark MAGA” persona continued into 2025, when he wore the black cap during appearances at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) and in Oval Office meetings while discussing his work with DOGE.

Musk’s comments come as he has been trying to distance himself from the Trump administration in recent months, even going so far as to say he got “carried away” with the major funding cuts to international programs that he implemented as head of DOGE. Those cuts, experts have noted, could lead to the deaths of 14 million people worldwide, including 4.5 million children, by 2030.

Despite those comments, Musk still spent almost half a billion dollars in support of MAGA-aligned Republicans during the midterms, including an anti-trans ad blitz across multiple states.

Musk may be attempting to distance himself from MAGA with hopes that doing so will prompt Democrats to back away from their promised investigations into his work at DOGE and his companies’ many lucrative contracts with the government — though some Democrats have already publicly told the billionaire that won’t happen.

Musk’s attempts to rebrand himself as anti-MAGA could also stem from his recognition that the movement has run its course. Indeed, recent polling indicates that most Americans are tired of MAGA.

A Quinnipiac University poll in September, for example, found that only 32 percent of Americans remain dedicated to the movement, with 65 percent rejecting it. That poll also found that candidates describing themselves as MAGA did so at their own peril, with 51 percent of voters saying the label made them less likely to vote for a candidate and only 18 percent saying it made them more likely to do so.

A post-midterm poll from Politico also found that nearly one in two MAGA supporters recognize that their movement is dwindling, with 45 percent of those identifying with MAGA agreeing with the idea that they were “losers” in the elections held earlier this month.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we must raise $16,000 before midnight. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can …

title: PCC Workers in Solidarity With Palestine (UFCW PCC Workers Speak Out)
content:
A post shared by PCC Workers (@pcc.workers.speak.out)

DON’T CROSS THE PICKET LINE!!! 📣✊🏾🍉

PCC Workers will be picketing outside the Columbia City store every single day from 11/18 – 11/24 unless they meet the demands of our petition:

1.) Return our pins and stop taking them from our bulletin board

2.) Stop sending workers home for wearing their watermelon pins.

3.) Reverse any discipline justified by this appearance policy.

4.) IMMEDIATELY REHIRE Anthony and any other workers fired for wearing their watermelon pin.

Want to support the workers? Sign on to the demands at the link in our bio! 📝

PCC claims to support progressive values — but what happens when its workers try to show solidarity?

Earlier this year, PCC made headlines for forcing workers to go home for wearing watermelon pins. After UFCW 3000 and the community rallied behind the workers, and the union authorized union watermelon pins, we thought that would be the end of it.

So far 9 employees have missed a combined total of 106 hours of work after being sent home by their management for refusing to remove their union watermelon pin. When one employee refused to take his pin off, citing a violation of his labor rights under the National Labor Relations Act, he was pulled into a disciplinary meeting for “badmouthing” PCC in front of the customers.

We must defend the rights of workers to organize at their workplace without fear of retaliation. We must expose the deception and hypocrisy of the CEOs like Krish and businesses like PCC that have stood by and looked the other way as suffering families being deprived of clean food and fresh water in Gaza, and as ancestral farmland is being destroyed and occupied in the West Bank and now southern Lebanon.

Sign this petition to tell PCC management that the community stands in solidarity with PCC workers! Stop sending them home for wearing legally protected union apparel!

Palestine Solidarity and Internationalism Working Group

To: To Krish, Dana, All Store Directors and Assistant Store Directors, From: Michael Letwin

Stop violating the protected rights of PCC workers!

Although you claim the PCC appearance policy itself has not changed since 2024, the implementation of this policy has shifted drastically since Krish and Dana’s emails to all staff on 6/29 and 7/7. While previously, buttons such as the PCC Pride button or a Black Lives Matter button have been considered unobjectionable, currently, workers are being sent home for wearing UFCW 3000 pins with watermelons on them. This is a noticeable change in working conditions, and as such, workers have a right to express their collective voice over this appearance policy as it’s currently being enforced in our workplaces.

PCC co-op members, shoppers, and the broader community stand in solidarity with PCC workers as they express their collective dissatisfaction and anger over this unreasonable change.

The new enforcement of this appearance policy is in violation of NLRA protected rights to wear union apparel and participate in concerted union activity, and thus any discipline administered over violations of this policy for wearing our union apparel is a violation of the Discipline and Discharge sections of the collective bargaining agreement (2.4 & 2.5 for grocery, 11.7 for meat).

As a community, we uplift the following worker demands:

● Return any union pins you have confiscated and stop taking union pins, including removing them from the break room bulletin boards. ● Reverse and cease all steps of progressive discipline justified by violating this appearance policy. ● Rehire any employees terminated for not complying with this appearance policy. ● Stop sending union workers home without pay for wearing union pins.

After 10 months of negotiating over all aspects of working conditions, none of which included the appearance policy, we consider the disrespectful timing of your changes to this policy to be inexcusable. Moreover, we are appalled at the lack of justification given for such a dramatic change to begin with. How does this promote our commitment to inclusion, diversity, and celebration of values? How does this continue in the legacy of PCC’s commitment to transparency and member democracy? Who decided the policy must now be enforced in this way and why? Why is a pin with the political statement “Black Lives Matter” allowed, but a slice of watermelon is unacceptable?

We expect to see these questions answered and these demands met. Until then …

The cat is out of the bag now that Lonely Planet knows that Bandung, Indonesia, is a hot spot for punk rock. Over the years, I have discussed my research with different people from all over the world, and many are surprised that punk still exists. Punk is not dead; in fact, it is alive and thriving in the urban centers of Indonesia and has been for some time.

If you are tuned in to the visual cues of punk, it is difficult to wander around Bandung, Jakarta, Denpasar, or any other major city in the country without seeing markers of the scene. Early in my fieldwork, I bumped into some teenagers in the Dago area of Bandung, and one of them was extremely excited that the band shirt I was wearing and the back patch on his jacket were both representing the same obscure punk band from Portland, Oregon. Indeed, the punks in Indonesia are numerous and, as the kid’s fandom exemplified, plugged into the broader global punk rock scene. While punk takes different forms in Indonesia today, I focus on Bandung’s anarcho-punk scene and the global connections they maintain that are predicated on do-it-yourself (DIY) or anarchist principles. This group is redrawing sociopolitical and cultural borders, which is particularly noteworthy in a post-authoritarian nation with an emerging democracy.

Bandung is a sprawling and densely populated city in West Java, situated approximately 90 miles southeast of Jakarta. The city proper has nearly three million inhabitants, while the metropolitan area has nine million residents. Physical remnants of Dutch colonialism in the form of broad boulevards and European architecture have earned the city the moniker “Paris of Java.” Bisected by the Cikapundung River, Bandung sits in a valley surrounded by volcanic peaks. Like all cities in Indonesia, Bandung’s profound income inequalities are hard to miss; corrugated metal shacks bunched together form sprawling communities nestled up alongside opulent malls and high-rise buildings. Bandung is known as something of a college town, as it is home to several major universities, both secular and Islamic. This has attracted people from different backgrounds to Bandung creating a “hip” and cosmopolitan atmosphere against its abject poverty. The Bandung rock scene is embedded in this setting of striking juxtaposition of rich and poor. Although the city is associated with a rapidly evolving youth pop culture, the punk scene has been thriving for some time and well-known bands have been playing for over 20 years.

Anarchist punk does not exist in a vacuum, and punk’s lived realities are complicated by familial, financial, and social expectations. Band members have children and jobs and are situated in complex global power dynamics.

It would be inaccurate to discuss the Bandung punk scene as though it is a cohesive and well-delineated group. From a purely logistical standpoint, Bandung is too large a …

author: Unknown
title: Теория коммунизации: Коммунизм > Социализм
content:
Процессуальное понимание коммунизма лишь относительно недавно пришло в современное левое движение. Традиционно устоялось понимание коммунизма как статичной общественно-экономической формации, чему линейно предшествовал этап диктатуры пролетариата, сохранявшийся как посреднический этап даже в представлении левых коммунистов, которые оказались ближе всех к реальному пониманию государства как враждебного буржуазного института.

Переосмысление этого положения вещей в современном марксистском дискурсе осуществили Жиль Дове и французский коллектив Tiqqun во второй половине XX века, сформулировав т.н «теорию коммунизации» — идеи о том, чтобы осуществлять коммунистическое общество без переходных этапов в виде диктатуры пролетариата и воссоздания вертикальных структур управления социалистическим обществом. Ничего не напоминает, правда? Подобного рода достижениям в левой мысли можно только радоваться, потому как это отвечает нашим анархическим структурным интересам в организации глубинных общественных изменений.

Разумеется, «теория коммунизации» — это дублирование анархо-коммунистического подхода к организации общества, что Жиль Дове и не скрывал, отсылая к Кропоткину в формулировке этой теории. К тому же, современность предоставляет нам пласт для эффективной коммунизации на базе кибернетического платформенного самоуправления социоэкономическими процессами.

В первую очередь, мы, анархисты, поддерживаем понимание политики и социальных противоречий как динамического, а не статического процесса, следовательно, и коммунизм — как практику и процесс, а не абстрактную онтологическую цель.

Собственно, нам есть чем возразить Жилю Дове и его представлению о коммунизации со стороны первоисточника и реальной системной практики. Разумеется, переходный этап как состояние и процесс — это устаревшее линейное модернистское представление, на практике своей редко перевешивающее реформистскую практику по своей эффективности — в критике переходности мы проблем не видим.

Другое дело — в методологическом «катастрофизме» и разрыве будущего с прошлым, неизбежно сводящемуся к безосновному ожиданию накопления тщательно скрываемых противоречий современного мира. Коммунизация — вне сомнений, процесс необходимый и чрезвычайно важный, но ключевой акцент на том, что это — процесс, что вульгарно упускается из внимания «катастрофистами» и апологетами деструктивного подхода к политике.

Любой процесс на этапе своего возникновения или развития нуждается в корректировке и оптимизации тех методов, которыми он достигается — без этого императива жизнеспособность системы практически предрешена, поскольку не осуществляется никаких мер для поддержания её гомеостаза и выработки ответов на вызовы. Целеполагание такой системы при этом прямо зависит от подбора методов, которые она использует, что требует их отбора в реальном времени.

Простыми словами — коммунизация должна проходить здесь и сейчас, через практику и внедрение механизмов, ликвидирующих участие государства и капитала в самоорганизации и ликвидирующих товарно-денежные отношения в производстве и потреблении, в противном случае — мы наблюдаем реформизм и смену лиц в системе, полностью сохранившей свою семантическую основу.

Поэтому методология коммунизации — это либо её практика через префигурацию, либо полное отсутствие этой методологии до «часа Х», когда намеченная французскими постмарксистами ситуация достигнет состояния, когда необходимо будет её проводить. И, разумеется, в кризисных условиях, когда вертикаль выигрывает у горизонтали за счет простоты мобилизации системы, это будет обречено на ещё один цикл прохождения доминирующих вертикальных систем через железный закон олигархии Михельса, и — voilà — реставрация государства и капитализма.

Потому что дать реальное понимание фундамента будущего общества может только его отражение в настоящем и диалектическое прохождение через разнообразие тех методов, которые мы могли бы использовать.

author: Stephen Prager
title: ICJ Finds Myanmar Guilty of Committing Genocide Against Rohingya Muslims
content:
The International Court of Justice for the first time in its 80-year history has found a state responsible for genocide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In a historic ruling, the International Court of Justice on Thursday found Myanmar’s government responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority during its brutal military campaign in 2017.

It is the first time in the ICJ’s 80-year history that it has found a state responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention, with the court ruling in a 9-6 vote that “the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar’s actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part” of the Rohingya population.

ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said the court found that during Myanmar’s military campaign that began in northern Rakhine State in August 2017, “security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers.”

NEWS: @CIJ_ICJ determines Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the 2017 clearance operations in northern Rakhine State.@antonioguterres calls the judgement a demonstration of international justice.https://t.co/1RCbI9g5hb pic.twitter.com/E51EwzIIDf

In the case brought by the West African nation of The Gambia, the court found that the evidence supported UN investigators’ estimate that at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, including women and children. It also showed soldiers committed widespread rape and sexual violence. The ICJ additionally found that Rohingya villages were systematically burned and destroyed while neighboring villages belonging to other ethnic groups were spared. In all, more than 700,000 Rohingya were forced to flee into neighboring Bangladesh.

The court ordered Myanmar to investigate, prosecute, and punish suspects, and enact laws implementing the Genocide Convention to prevent future violations. It also ordered the country to facilitate the voluntary return of displaced Rohingya, help locate missing people, return or replace lost or damaged property, provide rehabilitation for victims, and ensure protection against discrimination. Myanmar must also compensate the Rohingya for harm done with an amount to be determined later, the ICJ said.

The ruling was celebrated by human rights advocates. Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnes Callamard called it “a historic and authoritative recognition of the atrocities committed against the Rohingya and a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families.”

Genocide. The international Court of Justice is fully convinced that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. Complex and well presented lines of arguments on genocidal intent. Many implications for jurisprudence and future trials. Well evidenced and well argued…

She said the ruling “must serve as a wake-up call to the international community” and “must not simply be ignored,” especially since those who committed the atrocities are still in positions of power.

“The man who oversaw a campaign of crimes against humanity and other crimes under international law against the Rohingya, the former head of the armed forces, Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, is now Myanmar’s president following engineered elections,” she said. “Governments should not welcome him on the international stage, especially as grave violations continue unchecked inside Myanmar. Instead, they should stop any transfer of all weapons, security and surveillance equipment, and military and security assistance to Myanmar.”

Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch, said that in addition to being a “long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military,” it also “provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.”

Nimer Sultany, a law professor at the University of London’s School of Oriental and African Studies, said the ruling had massive implications for the December 2023 genocide case brought before the ICJ against Israel over its military campaign in Gaza.

title: PL Samuel Klein é aprovado no Senado e vai à sanção presidencial
content:
No mesmo plenário em que encaminhou o ajuste fiscal do governo, o Senado também aprovou, em votação simbólica, nesta quarta-feira, 18 de novembro, um projeto que nasceu de uma reportagem da

Agência Pública

.


O

PL 4186/2021

, conhecido como PL Caso Klein ou PL Samuel Klein, amplia de três para 20 anos o prazo para que vítimas de crimes sexuais sofridos na infância ou na adolescência recorram à Justiça e sejam indenizadas.


No Senado, o projeto recebeu apenas uma emenda de redação, que não altera seu conteúdo principal. O texto segue agora para o presidente Lula (PT), que terá 15 dias úteis, contados a partir do recebimento, para sancioná-lo. Como o projeto prevê vigência imediata, o novo prazo de 20 anos passará a vigorar na data da publicação da lei. 


O texto foi apresentado a partir da investigação na qual a

Pública

 revelou, há mais de cinco anos, denúncias de exploração sexual de meninas e mulheres envolvendo Samuel Klein, fundador das Casas Bahia. “A série de reportagens da

Pública

 foram fundamentais para que o Brasil conhecesse esse problema e nos inspirou muito para que a gente pudesse protocolar esse projeto de lei”, afirmou um das deputadas autoras, Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL-SP). 


A deputada conta que também foi procurada pela vereadora Bruna Biondi (PSOL-SP), que acompanhava os desdobramentos do caso em São Caetano do Sul, a cidade-sede da rede varejista. A partir desse contato e das informações reunidas pela investigação, as parlamentares apresentaram a proposta em novembro de 2021, que também contou com a participação de Fernanda Melchionna (PSOL-RS). 


O que prevê o texto aprovado 


Pelo texto aprovado, o prazo de 20 anos começará a contar quando a vítima completar 18 anos – ou seja, ela poderá, em regra, ajuizar a ação até os 38 anos. A mudança limita-se à reparação dos danos e não altera as regras de responsabilização criminal dos agressores. “Não foi um prazo que a gente tirou da cabeça. A gente quer equiparar à legislação da esfera criminal”, explicou Sâmia Bomfim.


Na esfera criminal, a prescrição varia conforme a pena prevista para cada delito e pode chegar a duas décadas. Nos casos de violência sexual contra crianças e adolescentes, a contagem, em regra, só se inicia na maioridade. 


O projeto busca aproximar as condições oferecidas nos dois campos: enquanto o processo criminal trata da punição do agressor, a ação civil permite à vítima pleitear indenização. A intenção é que ela tenha mais tempo para recorrer a ambos os caminhos e não perca tão cedo a possibilidade de obter reparação.


“Mesmo para mulheres adultas, a gente demora às vezes anos para se dar conta da gravidade da violência que a gente vivenciou. Imagina para uma menina de 14, de 16 anos”, disse a deputada. Segundo ela, muitas vítimas só conseguem reconhecer a violência sofrida e buscar ajuda quando já são adultas, o que torna o prazo atual insuficiente. Se a vítima tem menos de 16 anos, a contagem só começa quando ela atinge essa idade. Na prática, quem sofreu abuso na infância pode, em regra, ter apenas até os 19 anos para pedir reparação. Em algumas situações, a existência de uma investigação ou de um processo criminal pode adiar esse limite. Ainda assim, quando o prazo começa a correr, pode se esgotar antes que a vítima tenha condições e entendimento para recorrer à Justiça.


Uma conquista para as mulheres


Para Sâmia, a aprovação é uma resposta às dificuldades enfrentadas pelas mulheres que denunciaram o empresário, mas pode beneficiar também vítimas de outros casos de violência sexual. “Eu acho que é uma reparação para as vítimas do Caso Klein, para as vítimas dos demais casos, mas também é uma reparação simbólica e fundamental para todas as mulheres brasileiras”, disse.


No plenário, a votação do projeto foi acompanhada pelas autoras do projeto e também pela vereadora Bruna Biondi. Eleita em 2020 pelo mandato coletivo Mulheres por Mais Direitos, Bruna passou a atuar em defesa das vítimas de Samuel Klein depois da publicação das denúncias da

Pública

. Em São Caetano do Sul, a vereadora mobilizou o mandato para cobrar justiça e questionar as homenagens públicas ao empresário, conhecido como “rei do varejo”.


“A

Pública

 deu luz a um tema que a elite política de São Caetano sempre soube, mas nunca levou a público e nunca debateu com seriedade”, afirmou a vereadora. Além de ter participado da articulação do PL, ela integra desde 2021 as mobilizações para retirar o nome de Samuel Klein de espaços públicos da …

author: David Swanson
title: WBW Takes Part in Annual Conference of Doctors Against Genocide in Washington, D.C.
content:
Asia, Immorality, North America, Videos

By John Reuwer, World BEYOND War, November 19, 2026

Doctors Against Genocide was founded in 2023 by Palestinian American doctors whose family members had long been attacked and displaced in their homeland, and were now being systematically killed by the Israeli invasion of Gaza. They have worked relentlessly since then to alert the medical profession and the public of this grave health and humanitarian crisis. They have been joined by thousands of health care workers and supporters to monitor, document, educate, and advocate for an end to the horror of genocide not only in Palestine, but in Lebanon, Sudan, Congo, Myanmar, and other areas of intense conflict.

We gathered at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C., for three days of reports, analyses, and networking across a broad range of related topics. Here are a few highlights that I witnessed. To view any part of the full, incredibly rich conference, here are the recordings for Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3.

Co-founder and pediatric neurologist Karameh Kuemmerle describes the need for a medical definition of genocide for governments and medical associations to use in order to protect health care workers in areas of violent conflict.

Dr. Mazen Al-Rantisi spoke from the West Bank about his 128 day detention without charges in an Israeli prison. Known in Ramallah as the “doctor of the poor” for his 40 years treating people without regard for their ability to pay, he was abducted from his home at 3:00am and kept in a 2 x 6 meter cell with 10 other inmates sharing one toilet with almost no toilet paper or soap. He describes disturbances day and night, random beatings, and denial of medical care despite serious medical problems and pervasive scabies. The guards seemed to competer with one another to see who could be most cruel. My two days imprisoned on an Israeli floating concentration camp this summer left me no doubt about his testimony.

I led a conversation with two medical colleagues who have been on the front lines challenging ICE agents in the streets and their hospital at considerable cost to their health and careers. This led to making the connections between U.S. government support of Israel in its genocide, and its bringing the techniques of population control for use on its own citizens.

Anthropologist and artist Dana Walrath tells about her study of ten genocides, the latest of which is against the Palestinians. The common beginning is always dehumanization of the target group. Gaza is the first time the horror has been lifestreamed in real time to the screens of anyone paying attention. What does that mean for humanity? Dana expressed her studied impression that there is no evidence for war in most of human prehistory nor an inevitable part of the human condition.

title: Nvidia agli onori della cronaca: il mercato dei chip tra USA e Cina
content:
La vicenda salita gli onori della cronaca per il gossip tra gli Huang che ha in seguito portato alle dimissioni dell’ad di Nvidia, leader mondiale nel settore dell’intelligenza artificiale, ha riaperto il dibattito sul mercato dei microprocessori e, sullo sfondo, dello scontro tra USA e Cina. 


Al di là dello “scandalo” per la relazione tra l’ad di Nvidia e Alice Huang, dirigente dell’azienda Megaspeed con sede a Singapore e presunta spia cinese (dettaglio lasciato poi nel dimenticatoio), è interessante interrogarsi sullo stato dell’arte del comparto delle Big Tech a livello mondiale. 


Le catene del valore nel settore dei microchip intraprendono delle strade spesso considerate “zona grigia” e gli scambi tra aziende cinesi e statunitensi sono di là dall’essere una novità. Questo interroga sull’eventualità della bolla dell’ai, della posizione sul mercato di queste aziende e quali sono i fattori che poi ne determinano l’egemonia su di esso.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Judge Nominee Won’t Say If He Can Run for President a Third Time
content:
James Sullivan, who refused to say if Trump could run for president again, is currently a Texas Supreme Court justice.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Wednesday, a nominee to a federal judgeship struggled to recall and then refused to answer basic questions about the 22nd Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which stipulates that a person cannot run for a third presidential term if they’ve previously been elected president twice.

James P. Sullivan, who is presently a Texas state Supreme Court justice, lost his reelection bid earlier this month when the state saw a “blue wave” in the midterm elections. Days after his loss, President Donald Trump nominated Sullivan to become a federal judge within the state.

Although Sullivan’s time as a judge was limited — he was appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott (R-Texas) in early 2025 and served just under two years on Texas’s high court after a vacancy occurred — he has a strong legal background rooted in conservatism, having previously served as general counsel to the governor from 2018 to 2025. Sullivan is also a member of the far right Federalist Society.

During his nomination hearing in the Senate on Wednesday, Sullivan refused to answer queries regarding basic constitutional theory and recent history.

When Sen. Chris Coons (D-Delaware) asked him to explain the meaning of the 22nd Amendment, Sullivan appeared to struggle, at one point closing his eyes tightly, as if to focus. After several seconds, Coons gave him a hint: “No person shall be elected…” he began, prompting Sullivan to recall that the amendment bars people from running for a third presidential term.

Coons then asked Sullivan if Trump could run for a third term, citing numerous remarks by the president suggesting he might try to do so. Sullivan refused to answer the question.

“As a nominee for a federal district court, it would be a violation, I believe, of Canon 5 for me to opine on something like that,” Sullivan responded, citing American Bar Association (ABA) standards for nominees for judgeships. He then described the issue as something that “seems like it’s the sort of thing that is the subject of ongoing political debate.”

Coons disagreed, stating that it seems clear that the amendment — and Trump’s suggestions that he could run again — are contradictory.

“The question of whether someone can serve a third term as president of the United States, I think, is only unresolved in the mind of President Trump, who has repeatedly said that he’s thinking he might run for a third time,” Coons explained.

“I don’t believe it is the subject of political debate,” he added.

After the two continued a short back-and-forth on the matter, Coons reiterated his disbelief in Sullivan’s non-answer.

“The amendment is bracingly clear: ‘No person shall be elected to the office of the president more than twice,’” he said. “There is no debate about this, in my view.”

OMG — Trump judicial nominee James P Sullivan (a Texas Supreme Court justice!) reveals he doesn't know what the 22nd amendment says, but then after Chris Coons explains it to him, he refuses to say it'd be illegal for Trump to serve an illegal third term 🤦 pic.twitter.com/YwkDcVa70C

The ABA’s Canon 5 rule does contain a subsection prohibiting “a candidate for judicial office from making statements that commit the candidate regarding cases, controversies or issues likely to come before the court.” However, there is a caveat to that rule that Sullivan appeared to ignore: “As a corollary, a candidate should emphasize in any public statement the candidate’s duty to uphold the law regardless of his or her personal views.”

Had Sullivan responded to Coons’s question on the 22nd Amendment by correctly pointing out that the law forbids Trump from running again, he likely wouldn’t have been in violation of the standard he cited.

Later during the hearing, multiple nominees were asked by Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Connecticut) to recall the events of January 6, 2021, when a mob of loyalists to Trump sought to violently disrupt the proceedings of Congress following Joe Biden’s victory in the 2020 presidential race.

Blumenthal sought to discern whether any of the nominees were “willing to say the Capitol was attacked” on that date. The nominees, including Sullivan, did not respond.

“Nobody? It’s a sad day,” Blumenthal said.

author: Gabriel Aguirre
title: Work For Peace, In Berlin / Trabajos por la Paz en Berlín
content:
Culture of Peace, Europe, Latin America, South America

By Gabriel Aguirre, World BEYOND War, November 19, 2026

Berlin has historically been a city where peace occupies a central place in the public discourse of its inhabitants. The historical events—from the Second World War to the fall of the Berlin Wall—speak for themselves.

For this and other reasons, organizations such as the International Peace Bureau (IPB) have their headquarters there—a space that has served to promote the vision of a different kind of world. During the second week of October, Gabriel Aguirre, the Latin America organizer for World BEYOND War (WBW), had the opportunity to visit these offices as part of a working tour that included several European countries.

During the visit, meetings were held with the International Peace Bureau team, alongside discussions and interviews with various organizations within the German peace movement. The situation in Latin America and its processes of resistance sparked great interest among the participants. Furthermore, the two organizations discussed joint projects currently underway between World BEYOND War and the IPB—most notably the Peace Wave, an initiative that has established itself in recent years as a key platform for the mobilization and coordination of peace advocates worldwide.

Naturally, a stay in the German capital would not be complete without a visit to the Anti-War Café (*Anti-Kriegs-Café*), located near the bustling Alexanderplatz area. It is a must-visit spot for anyone in Berlin who speaks out against war. There, visitors are welcomed by Heinrich, the coordinator of the WBW Berlin chapter—a man who has long been deeply active in, and supportive of, various global struggles for peace. Beyond enjoying a German beer, visitors can learn about historical instances of solidarity and anti-war activism from around the world.

Gabriel Aguirre, Un Mundo Más Allá de la Guerra, 19 de noviembre de 2026

Berlín ha sido históricamente una ciudad donde la paz ocupa un lugar central en el debate público de sus habitantes. Los acontecimientos históricos hablan por sí solos, desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial hasta la caída del Muro de Berlín.

Por este y otros motivos, organizaciones como el Buró Internacional de la Paz (IPB, por sus siglas en inglés) tienen allí su sede central, un espacio que ha servido para proyectar la idea de un mundo diferente. Durante la segunda semana de octubre, el organizador para América Latina de World BEYOND War (WBW), Gabriel Aguirre, tuvo la oportunidad de visitar estas oficinas en el marco de una gira de trabajo que incluyó varios países de Europa.

Durante la visita, se llevaron a cabo reuniones con el equipo del Buró Internacional de la Paz, así como encuentros y entrevistas con diversas organizaciones del movimiento pacifista en Alemania. La situación de América Latina y sus procesos de resistencia despertaron un gran interés entre los participantes. Asimismo, se abordaron proyectos conjuntos que actualmente se desarrollan entre World BEYOND War y el IPB, entre los que destaca la V Ola de la Paz, una iniciativa que en los últimos años se ha consolidado como un espacio clave de movilización y articulación para los defensores de la paz en todo el mundo.

Por supuesto, la estadía en la capital alemana exigía visitar el Café Antibélico (Anti-Kriegs-Café), ubicado en las cercanías de la concurrida zona de Alexanderplatz. Es un lugar de parada obligatoria para quienes visitan Berlín y alzan su voz contra la guerra. Allí los visitantes son recibidos por Heinrich, coordinador del capítulo de WBW en Berlín, quien durante muchos años se ha mantenido muy activo y solidario con las distintas luchas globales por la paz, donde además de tomarte una cerveza alemana, podrás aprender sobre las experiencias históricas de solidaridad y contra la guerra en el mundo.

title: How the Riots Spread to Italy : An Account from the October 17 Uprising in Milan
content:
Across Europe, young people are rising up in rebellion. From

Spain

 and

France

 to Albania and even

Germany

, demonstrators are breaking with complacency and obedience and breaking through the constraints intended to control them.


This is reminiscent of the previous wave of unrest. In November 2018, the

Yellow Vest

 movement broke out in France, precipitating

several months

 of street conflict throughout the country. By fall of 2019, a global wave of uprisings was underway from

Hong Kong

,

Ecuador

, and

Chile

 to

Sudan

,

Catalunya

, and

Lebanon

. All this set the stage for the

George Floyd Rebellion

 to spread

around the United States

 in 2020.


It remains to be seen whether the wave of protest emanating from France today is indicative of a new groundswell of worldwide momentum—and it remains uncertain what it would take for these movements to address the fundamental problems of our time. Everywhere around the world, the movements of 2019 and 2020 reached an

impasse

 when they exhausted the force they could bring to bear in the streets and shifted instead to doomed electoral and reformist campaigns. The heroic failure of those powerful movements suggests that nothing short of a revolutionary transformation of our society can address the catastrophes that

capitalism

 and the consolidation of political power in the hands of autocrats are creating.


Hopefully, these upheavals can serve as laboratories in which a new generation of revolutionaries can experiment with methods for making profound change. In the following account, anarchists in Italy describe the moment in October 2026 at which the movement in Italy exceeded control.


Cracks in the Façade


In Italy, despite soaring prices, stagnating wages, and deteriorating schools and public services, the right-wing regime of Giorgia Meloni continues to ignore widespread misery while increasing military spending. Did they think we would not resist as wealthy elites attempt to loot our future?


This fall, cracks began to appear in the façade of the ruling order. On September 22 and 23 in Modena, about fifty young people organized themselves to loot supermarkets. They all walked in together and recorded footage of themselves taking whatever they wanted. Since the beginning of October, truck drivers across southern Italy have been blocking the roads and striking in protest against the rising price of diesel. For weeks, supermarkets in the south lay nearly empty.


As the ferment slowly grew, a call from a newly formed initiative called “Italia in piazza” [“Italy in the Squares”] circulated on social media. Anonymous chats on Telegram channels began to promote a date to mobilize against the high cost of living: October 17. The call was picked up on TikTok and Instagram and circulated widely. In Milan, the group called for a convergence in a city park. This contributed to swelling the ranks of protesters.


The protests of October 17 took an array of different forms in cities across the country. In Turin, Bergamo, and Milan, widespread unrest and looting indicated a political dimension rarely seen in Italy.


The demonstrators who assembled in Milan’s Piazza del Duomo on October 17 only traveled a few streets before the police blocked them. This would usually stop a protest in its tracks, but that day was different. Within the blocked group of approximately five hundred demonstrators, the energy remained strong. They chanted and threw themselves against the assembled cops, applying pressure until they finally broke through the police line and poured into the side streets. This time, the repressive maneuvers of the police failed, enabling anyone who so desired to join in the protest.


The following week, the Meloni regime called in the army to repress the demonstrations, which only infuriated people further. On October 30, a nationwide strike brought tens of thousands into the streets in over 40 cities around Italy. Since then, protests have continued around the country. But the uprisings of October 17 marked the turning point when masses of young people shattered the consumer spectacle in an explosion of looting and street fighting.


The following testimony reaches us from some participants in the unrest of October 17 and 18 in Milan.


Under the Madonnina


Gleaming atop the dome of Milan Cathedral, the famous golden statue of the Virgin Mary known as the Madonnina looms over a city in revolt. Beneath her gilded gaze, cobblestones fly at …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Biden Told Netanyahu He Loved Him in Final Call From White House
content:
Former US president Joe Biden told Benjamin Netanyahu that he loved him on his last call to the Israeli prime minister before leaving office. 


“I still love you, pal”, a transcript of the 15 January 2025 call,

published by the Jerusalem Post,

quotes Biden as saying. “You’re a good man,” he added. “I admire you.”


Biden acted as a key supporter of Israel’s genocide in Gaza while in office, lending direct military, politcal and diplomatic support and overseeing the

transfer of billions of dollars worth of weapons

 to the country. 


In the wake of the 7 October attacks in 2023, Biden repeated false Israeli claims that Hamas had beheaded children, which was seen to bolster Israeli propaganda efforts to justify its massive escalation of war crimes against Gaza’s civilians. 


“I never really thought that I would see, have confirmed, pictures of terrorists beheading children,” Biden said at the time, only for a White House spokesperson to later confirm he had “not seen pictures or confirmed such reports independently”. 


In the January 2025 call, Biden told Netanyahu: “You’ve been through hell. I can’t tell you how much I appreciate you and what you’ve been through,” adding: “I know we’ve disagreed on occasion but, you know… I still love you, pal.”


He added: “I don’t know how you’ve done it all… Next time I think I have a tough job, I’ll think of you… you’re a good man… I admire you. It took a lot of courage to do what you did.”


The transcript stands in contrast to Biden’s comments on Netanyahu in his new memoir, Promise Me, America, which describes the Israeli leader as a “Trump-like” figure “bending democratic institutions to serve his personal needs.”

author: Unknown
title: 8 dicembre-marcia popolare Notav. Contro gli sprechi e per la difesa dei territori
content:
Sono passati

ventun anni

 da quell’

8 dicembre 2005

, quando migliaia di persone tornarono a

Venaus

 per riprendersi i terreni sottratti dopo lo sgombero e l’occupazione militare dei giorni precedenti. Una giornata rimasta impressa nella memoria della Valle di Susa e che ha segnato una

tappa fondamentale nella storia del Movimento No Tav

.


Da Notav Info


Nel corso di tutti questi anni, la questione della

Torino-Lione

 ha assunto una portata che va ben oltre la realizzazione di una linea ferroviaria. Ha mostrato cosa significa imporre un

modello di sviluppo

 che concentra enormi risorse nelle

grandi opere

, consuma territori e risorse e affida al continuo aumento delle infrastrutture e della circolazione delle merci la propria idea di progresso. Una visione che oggi si confronta con una realtà fatta di

impoverimento, precarietà e servizi pubblici sempre più in difficoltà

.


È una contraddizione che attraversa il nostro presente.


Mentre il

carovita

 erode salari e pensioni, il

lavoro precario

 rende sempre più difficile costruire prospettive di vita e

l’accesso alla casa e ai servizi essenziali

 diventa un problema per fasce sempre più ampie della popolazione, si continuano a presentare come inevitabili i

tagli e la mancanza di fondi per sanità, scuola, trasporti e welfare

. Allo stesso tempo, crescono gli

investimenti nel riarmo e nella produzione bellica

, alimentando un’economia che individua nella guerra e nella sua preparazione nuovi settori di espansione.


Non è una questione di risorse che mancano, ma di come vengono distribuite

 e degli interessi a cui vengono destinate. La Torino-Lione è una delle espressioni di queste priorità: un’enorme concentrazione di

denaro pubblico

 per un’opera che sacrifica territori e comunità, mentre rimangono inevase necessità ben più urgenti. Un’opera ormai priva di qualsiasi giustificazione, che si cerca oggi di legittimare riconducendola alle esigenze della

mobilità militare

.


Difendere i territori

 significa allora anche mettere in discussione questo modello, rivendicando un diverso uso delle risorse collettive, riconoscendo come prioritarie la

cura delle persone, dei luoghi, dei beni comuni e rifiutando la guerra

.


La storia della Valle di Susa dimostra che opporsi a questo modello

non è soltanto necessario, ma possibile

. In questi anni abbiamo costruito relazioni, mobilitazioni e forme di partecipazione che hanno saputo andare oltre i confini della nostra Valle. Oggi più che mai davanti a un mondo in fiamme e alle piazze piene sappiamo che questa lotta si innesta nella volontà ampiamente condivisa di

cambiare un sistema ingiusto

 nella distribuzione delle risorse e spietato nella

repressione del dissenso

.


L’8 dicembre torniamo a camminare insieme

, a ventun anni da Venaus, consapevoli che le ragioni di questa lotta continuano a parlare al presente e che la difesa dei territori è parte di una

battaglia più ampia per un futuro diverso

.


Ci vediamo in marcia, contro gli sprechi e per la difesa dei territori!

author: Mag
title: Betriebsratswahlen 2026 vom 1. März bis 31. Mai – warfen braune Schatten voraus
content:
Dossier


„

Von März bis Mai 2026 finden die nächsten Betriebsratswahlen statt. Während in kleineren Betrieben sich die Frage stellt, ob es überhaupt Kandidat:innen gibt, stellt sich in Großbetrieben die Frage, wieviel Listen antreten und wie hoch die Wahlbeteiligung ist. Nur noch 37% der Beschäftigten in Betriebe mit fünf und mehr Mitgliedern haben einen Betriebsrat. (…) Die Entpolitisierung der Gewerkschaften und ihre Anpassung an das kapitalistische Profit- und Konkurrenzsystem haben dazu geführt, dass sich die meisten Betriebsräte als Co-Manager betrachten. In der Krise führte das dazu, dass sie bereit sind, erkämpfte Errungenschaften über Betriebsvereinbarungen – meist völlig undemokratisch ohne Diskussion und Zustimmung der Belegschaft – zu opfern. (…) Die Gefahr besteht, dass sich der Unmut in der Belegschaft bei VW über die von IGM und Betriebsräten mitgetragene Arbeitsplatzvernichtung mit zusätzlichem Lohnverzicht teilweise in Stimmen für das „Zentrum Automobil“ bei den Betriebsratswahlen 2026 ausdrückt

…“ Umfangreiche

Analyse vom 27. August 2025 bei der Vernetzung für kämpferische Gewerkschaften


 („Betriebsratswahlen 2026: Harte Zeiten brauchen kämpferische Betriebsräte“) und mehr zum Thema (

Zentrum gibt es extra

):


Forschungsgruppe BR-Wahlen 2026: »Betriebsratswahlen in stürmischen Zeiten« – Herausforderungen und Gegenstrategien


„…

Während quantitative Studien vor allem Wahlergebnisse analysieren und qualitative Arbeiten insbesondere Betriebsratsgründungen, arbeitgeberseitige Behinderungsstrategien sowie die Beziehungen zwischen Management, Betriebsräten und Gewerkschaften beleuchten, fehlt es an systematischen Untersuchungen der Wahlkämpfe selbst. Offen bleibt damit, wie betriebliche Konflikte, ökonomische Rahmenbedingungen und gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen die Wahlkampfführung prägen und welche Strategien betriebliche Akteurinnen zur Mobilisierung und Repräsentation der Beschäftigten entwickeln. Diese Lücke hat unser Forschungsprojekt angesichts der Betriebsratswahlen im Frühjahr 2026 in einem sechsmonatigen, von der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung geförderten Projekt bearbeitet. Welche Probleme traten auf und wie wurde Union Busting sowie Zentrum- und AfD-Propaganda begegnet? Was folgte daraus in Bezug auf Strategien einer langfristigen und nachhaltigen Entwicklung von Mitbestimmung und gewerkschaftlicher Interessenvertretung im Betrieb?.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya, UN’s Top Court Rules
content:
Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during a scorched-earth military campaign in Rakhine state, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled. 


Judges at the UN’s highest court reached the historic verdict on Thursday, with nine voting in favour and six voting against. They also ruled by ten votes to five that Myanmar must adopt “measures of restitution”. 


It is the first time the court has ruled that a state is fully responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention.


Myanmar’s military launched what it claimed were “clearance operations” against the Muslim minority group in 2017, razing entire villages to the ground while committing mass killings and gang rapes. 


Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya were forced across the border to Bangladesh, where they remain confined to camps in squalid conditions. 


Authorities in Myanmar have blocked investigations and carried out “extensive destruction of evidence” crimes by burning and disposing of bodies, Judge Iwasawa said during the ruling. The case was initiated by The Gambia in 2019. 


Crowds of people celebrated at one refugee camp on Thursday as they watched the verdict being delivered on a small screen, the BBC reported.


But Nay San Lwin, a prominent Rohingya activist,

told Al Jazeera

 that a court verdict alone would not bring “meaningful justice”, which required “recognition of our identity, restoration of our rights, justice for every victim and the opportunity to return to our homeland safely, rebuild our lives, and live in peace and dignity.”


Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch, said: “The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.


“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.” 


The UK government last month

hosted representatives of Myanmar’s dictatorship

, which critics said would give the military junta an opportunity to launder its image. 


“The British government has been gradually softening its approach towards the Myanmar military regime, but hopefully this will stiffen their spines,” Mark Farmaner, director of the Burma Campaign UK pressure group, told Novara Media. 


“There have been no new sanctions rounds for two years,” he added, “and aid to the Rohingya has fallen… Myanmar has been pretty much forgotten.”

author: Nahuel Lag
title: La economía agroecológica avanza en América: lecciones desde los movimientos
content:
Por Nahuel Lag


Desde Perú


¿Qué economías agroecológicas queremos? Es la pregunta que se instaló en Pisco (Perú), en el encuentro de "Intercambios de Aprendizajes de las Américas sobre Economías de la Agroecología", que reunió a 60 organizaciones de 15 países, con el respaldo de Agroecology Fund. El análisis partió de lo que está en marcha: mercados locales, Sistemas Participativos de Garantías (SPG), comercialización, financiamiento, agregado de valor y cooperativismo. 


La anfitriona fue la Asociación Nacional de Productores del Perú (

ANPE

), una organización con economía propia: 281 agrupaciones territoriales, una marca de alimentos certificados y ferias locales. A lo largo de una semana, las diferentes experiencias expusieron el rumbo de las economías agroecológicas, advirtieron los desafíos en un contexto regional amenazado por gobiernos de ultraderecha y evidenciaron la necesidad de profundizar las políticas de fomento en una economía que continúa promoviendo el agronegocio para la exportación de materias primas. El aprendizaje e intercambio fueron profundos y dejaron lecciones e inspiración para el desarrollo de las economías agroecológicas de las Américas. 


“Hay que hacer sinergia e integración entre todas las organizaciones para generar el cambio del sistema convencional”, convocó Moises Quispe, director ejecutivo de la ANPE, y propuso continuar buscando aliados estratégicos para incidir en las políticas públicas y “convencer desde el estómago”. 


Economías agroecológicas: una experiencia continental  


La puerta de entrada del encuentro fue la visita a la

Agroferia Campesina

 de Lima que, con 90 productores de 23 regiones del Perú, ofrece una diversidad de alimentos disruptiva con la uniformidad de las góndolas de los supermercados. 


“El agricultor tiene el conocimiento de cómo cultivar y cocinar los alimentos. La gente valora que quien produce la tierra esté en los puestos y agradecen el acceso a alimentos más nutritivos y sanos”, destaca Jorge Panta, presidente de la Coalición Campesina, que hace 13 años sostiene la feria a la que asisten 6.000 personas por domingo. 


“El comercio es algo que está presente desde siempre, desde las culturas precolombinas los pueblos indígenas tenían intercambios, pero en la modernidad se ha transformado en algo muy concentrado. Entonces, cuando hablamos de agroecología no hablamos sólo de prácticas y técnicas de producción sino de otras cosas como la economía”, señaló Ángela Cordeiro, co-directora del Agroecology Fund, sobre el eje que atravesó los intercambios en Pisco.


Foto: Agroecology Fund


La experiencia de la Agroferia Campesina, en la que participan productores integrantes de la ANPE, no es ajena a las miles de organizaciones que promueven la agroecología desde sus territorios. Los mercados locales son la base de las economías agroecológicas en toda América, el punto de encuentro de “productor a consumidor”. La Red de Mercados Agroecológicos Campesinos del Valle del Cauca (

Redmac

), Colombia, lleva 17 años y reúne 21 mercados. María Fernanda Palacios Salcedo, integrante de la Redmac, compartió su experiencia sobre esos espacios en los que no ocurre solo una relación comercial: quienes se acercan son un “amigo consumidor”.  


Los productores de la Redmac se favorecen de los circuitos cortos de comercialización evitando intermediarios y largas distancias, lo que les permite ofrecer un precio anual por los alimentos. “No competimos con los precios de mercado; establecemos precios justos y fomentamos el valor de los alimentos sanos”, señala María Fernanda e indica también cómo la red transforma la comercialización en un acto solidario de organización, cuidado del territorio y construcción de soberanía alimentaria. Experiencias de mercados locales en Guatemala, Panamá, México, Honduras, Brasil y Perú ratificaron el camino virtuoso de estos mercados y los desafíos para ampliar el abastecimiento y la llegada a más consumidores.  


Los Sistemas Participativos de Garantía (SPG) son una herramienta construida por el movimiento agroecológico para saltar los altos costos en dólares de las certificaciones orgánicas y construir nuevas lógicas de relación. “Por un lado fortalecen el modelo de producción agroecológica con reglas comunes y, por otro, la confianza de los consumidores”, valoró Alfredo Patricio Robles, representante del

Colectivo Agroecológico del Ecuador

 en Pisco. El colectivo sostiene seis sistemas de SPG autónomos y colaborativos en …
